Ace_In_The_Hole.name: Ace in the Hole
Ace_In_The_Hole.description:
Whenever you loot an item from a Chest, it will have:
  • A Visceral or lower rarity add-on.
  • 50/75/100% chance for an Uncommon or lower rarity add-on.


When you escape, you keep your add-ons.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you loot an item from a Chest, it will have:
  • A Visceral or lower rarity add-on.
  • 50% chance for an Uncommon or lower rarity add-on.


When you escape, you keep your add-ons.

Whenever you loot an item from a Chest, it will have:
  • A Visceral or lower rarity add-on.
  • 75% chance for an Uncommon or lower rarity add-on.


When you escape, you keep your add-ons.

Whenever you loot an item from a Chest, it will have:
  • A Visceral or lower rarity add-on.
  • 100% chance for an Uncommon or lower rarity add-on.


When you escape, you keep your add-ons.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Ace that caps the rarity of the add-on pulled from a Chest, with higher tiers raising the chance the result lands at an even lower, more common rarity. It also lets a survivor keep the add-on they are carrying after escaping through an Exit Gate.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chest hunting becomes more predictable since the roll is kept within a capped rarity range instead of swinging wildly from one extreme to the other. Carrying the result out through a clean escape means the find is not wasted even though it is not guaranteed to be a top-tier item.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor likes collecting add-ons and wants steadier quality from every Chest opened. Plan a route that threads through Chests and keep a clear escape path so the carried add-on survives the final push.

Adrenaline.name: Adrenaline
Adrenaline.description:
When all Generators are completed, if you are downed or injured, heal instantly. Then, ignoring Exhausted:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
When all Generators are completed, if you are downed or injured, heal instantly. Then, ignoring Exhausted:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60s.

When all Generators are completed, if you are downed or injured, heal instantly. Then, ignoring Exhausted:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 50s.

When all Generators are completed, if you are downed or injured, heal instantly. Then, ignoring Exhausted:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Adrenaline is a survivor perk taught by Meg that instantly mends a downed or injured survivor the moment every Generator is finished, then grants a burst of speed for a brief window. The perk also costs a period of Exhausted after it fires.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts the final stretch of a trial into a healing and escape moment, letting a survivor who was carrying an injury stand back on their feet the instant the generators are done. That speed burst helps a survivor cross open ground or reach a hook rescue without being caught.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who wants a reliable late-trial safety net for an injury or a down state. Keep it in mind for the moment the last generator chimes, since the effect only fires after all Generators are completed.

Aftercare.name: Aftercare
Aftercare.description:
You and up to 1/2/3 Survivors see each other's Auras whenever:
  • You unhook them, or they unhook you.
  • You finish healing them, or they finish healing you.


This effect lasts until you are hooked.
descriptionTiers:
You and up to 1 Survivors see each other's Auras whenever:
  • You unhook them, or they unhook you.
  • You finish healing them, or they finish healing you.


This effect lasts until you are hooked.

You and up to 2 Survivors see each other's Auras whenever:
  • You unhook them, or they unhook you.
  • You finish healing them, or they finish healing you.


This effect lasts until you are hooked.

You and up to 3 Survivors see each other's Auras whenever:
  • You unhook them, or they unhook you.
  • You finish healing them, or they finish healing you.


This effect lasts until you are hooked.

beginner.whatItIs: Jeff teaches it as a perception perk that lets a survivor and a teammate see each other's Auras after they unhook or heal one another. The window of mutual visibility stays active until the survivor is hooked again.
beginner.whyItMatters: It keeps a rescued survivor in sight of their partner, which is exactly when a killer likes to pick off the freshly unhooked. That shared awareness helps the pair move together to safety instead of scattering blindly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor plays a rescue or healing role and wants to stay linked with a teammate after a save. It shines in the moments right after a hook unhook or a completed heal, when staying together beats splitting up.

Agitation.name: Agitation
Agitation.description:
While carrying a Survivor:
  • You gain 6/12/18% Haste.
  • Your Terror Radius is 12m larger.
descriptionTiers:
While carrying a Survivor:
  • You gain 6% Haste.
  • Your Terror Radius is 12m larger.

While carrying a Survivor:
  • You gain 12% Haste.
  • Your Terror Radius is 12m larger.

While carrying a Survivor:
  • You gain 18% Haste.
  • Your Terror Radius is 12m larger.

beginner.whatItIs: Taught by Chuckles, it is a killer perk that pays out while a Survivor is being carried. It adds a modest layer of speed and widens the Terror Radius for as long as the killer holds a Survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the carry phase into a control tool, giving the killer more room to loiter near hooks and less fear of being caught from behind. The extra Terror Radius helps the killer sense approaching rescuers sooner.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer who wants the hook-to-carry window to feel safer and more commanding. It rewards a patient killer who moves a carried Survivor carefully rather than rushing the drop.

Alert.name: Alert
Alert.description:
Whenever the Killer breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall, or damages a Generator:
  • You hear a sound cue.
  • You see their Aura for 3/4/5s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Killer breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall, or damages a Generator:
  • You hear a sound cue.
  • You see their Aura for 3s.

Whenever the Killer breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall, or damages a Generator:
  • You hear a sound cue.
  • You see their Aura for 4s.

Whenever the Killer breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall, or damages a Generator:
  • You hear a sound cue.
  • You see their Aura for 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Alert is a survivor perk taught by Feng that rings a sound cue and briefly reveals the killer's Aura whenever the killer breaks a Pallet or a Breakable Wall, or damages a Generator. It keeps a survivor aware of the killer's activity around them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the killer's own actions into a tracking signal, since every broken pallet or damaged generator pings a clue. That helps a survivor stay one step ahead of a killer who is actively working the map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor wants to hear the killer's movements without turning their head. It suits a cautious survivor who prefers to reposition based on where the killer is making noise.

AnyMeansNecessary.name: Any Means Necessary
AnyMeansNecessary.description:
While next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button for 5/4/3s to reset it.

You see the Auras of Dropped Pallets.
descriptionTiers:
While next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button for 5s to reset it.

You see the Auras of Dropped Pallets.

While next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button for 4s to reset it.

You see the Auras of Dropped Pallets.

While next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button for 3s to reset it.

You see the Auras of Dropped Pallets.

beginner.whatItIs: Any Means Necessary is a survivor perk taught by Yui that lets a survivor stand next to a Dropped Pallet and use an Active Ability button to reset it for a few seconds. It also reveals the Auras of Dropped Pallets so a survivor knows where they are.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a survivor a way to reclaim a broken pallet that a killer left behind, turning lost cover back into a tool. Seeing Dropped Pallet Auras helps a survivor plan routes that still have defensible ground available.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a survivor wants to recycle broken pallets instead of abandoning them. It rewards a survivor who keeps moving through pallet-heavy routes and wants to recover cover on the fly.

Autodidact.name: Autodidact
Autodidact.description:
You start the trial with 0 Tokens, up to 3/4/5, and your good basic healing Skill Checks give 15% less progress.

While healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit:
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, you earn 1 token.
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, for each Token, you gain 15% more progress.
  • You cannot get great basic Skill Checks.
descriptionTiers:
You start the trial with 0 Tokens, up to 3, and your good basic healing Skill Checks give 15% less progress.

While healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit:
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, you earn 1 token.
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, for each Token, you gain 15% more progress.
  • You cannot get great basic Skill Checks.

You start the trial with 0 Tokens, up to 4, and your good basic healing Skill Checks give 15% less progress.

While healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit:
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, you earn 1 token.
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, for each Token, you gain 15% more progress.
  • You cannot get great basic Skill Checks.

You start the trial with 0 Tokens, up to 5, and your good basic healing Skill Checks give 15% less progress.

While healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit:
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, you earn 1 token.
  • Whenever you hit a basic Skill Check, for each Token, you gain 15% more progress.
  • You cannot get great basic Skill Checks.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Adam that starts a trial with no Tokens banked and trades a little accuracy on good basic Skill Checks for a chance to earn Tokens while healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit. Banked Tokens boost later healing progress, though landing a great basic Skill Check becomes impossible while the perk is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: It reframes healing as a skill-based gamble where careful basic checks build a payout for the rest of the trial. It suits a survivor who is confident with the healing wheel and wants rewards for clean checks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor is comfortable with Skill Checks and wants a healing perk that scales with their accuracy. It rewards a steady, deliberate healer rather than one who rushes the wheel.

Babysitter.name: Babysitter
Babysitter.description:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They gain 10% Haste for 20/25/30s.
  • They leave no Pools of Blood for 20/25/30s.
  • They leave no Scratch Marks for 20/25/30s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 8s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They gain 10% Haste for 20s.
  • They leave no Pools of Blood for 20s.
  • They leave no Scratch Marks for 20s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 8s.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They gain 10% Haste for 25s.
  • They leave no Pools of Blood for 25s.
  • They leave no Scratch Marks for 25s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 8s.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They gain 10% Haste for 30s.
  • They leave no Pools of Blood for 30s.
  • They leave no Scratch Marks for 30s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 8s.

beginner.whatItIs: Babysitter is a survivor perk taught by Steve that, whenever a survivor unhooks another, grants that survivor a short speed boost and makes them leave no Pools of Blood or Scratch Marks for a stretch of time. It also briefly reveals the killer's Aura to the one who rescued.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes the survivor right after an unhook harder to track, since the usual telltale trails are suppressed for a while. The killer's Aura reveal also helps the rescuer keep an eye on where the killer is heading.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor plays a frequent unhook role and wants the rescued teammate to vanish from the killer's tracking tools. It rewards a rescue-first playstyle where saving teammates is a regular part of the run.

Balanced_Landing.name: Balanced Landing
Balanced_Landing.description:
Whenever you fall from at least 1.25m:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 3s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.
  • Your stagger is 75% shorter.
  • Your Grunts from falling are 100% quieter.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you fall from at least 1.25m:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 3s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60s.
  • Your stagger is 75% shorter.
  • Your Grunts from falling are 100% quieter.

Whenever you fall from at least 1.25m:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 3s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 50s.
  • Your stagger is 75% shorter.
  • Your Grunts from falling are 100% quieter.

Whenever you fall from at least 1.25m:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 3s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 40s.
  • Your stagger is 75% shorter.
  • Your Grunts from falling are 100% quieter.

beginner.whatItIs: Balanced Landing is a survivor perk taught by Nea that reacts whenever a survivor falls from a meaningful height. It grants a brief speed burst, shortens the stagger, and makes the landing far quieter, at the cost of a period of Exhausted.
beginner.whyItMatters: It softens the punishment of a fall, which can otherwise stun a survivor and give away their position with a loud grunt. The quiet, quicker landing helps a survivor recover and keep moving instead of freezing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a survivor expects to vault or drop from heights during a chase. It suits a survivor who plays aggressive loops and wants to land cleaner and recover faster.

Bamboozle.name: Bamboozle
Bamboozle.description:
Whenever you vault a Window, it is blocked for Survivors for 8/12/16s.

You basic-vault Windows 5/10/15% faster.

Only 1 Window can be blocked at a time.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you vault a Window, it is blocked for Survivors for 8s.

You basic-vault Windows 5% faster.

Only 1 Window can be blocked at a time.

Whenever you vault a Window, it is blocked for Survivors for 12s.

You basic-vault Windows 10% faster.

Only 1 Window can be blocked at a time.

Whenever you vault a Window, it is blocked for Survivors for 16s.

You basic-vault Windows 15% faster.

Only 1 Window can be blocked at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: Bamboozle is a killer perk taught by Clown that blocks a Window for survivors for a while whenever the killer vaults it, and lets the killer basic-vault Windows a little faster. A single Window can be blocked at a time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes survivors who rely on a favorite window loop, since the killer can seal the very exit they are about to use. The extra vault speed also helps the killer keep pace through window-heavy routes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a killer wants to shut down window loops and control a survivor's preferred escapes. It rewards a killer who is comfortable reading a survivor's favorite vault points.

BBQAndChilli.name: Barbecue & Chili
BBQAndChilli.description: Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 5s, you see the Auras of all Survivors who are at least 60/50/40m away from the hooked Survivor.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 5s, you see the Auras of all Survivors who are at least 60m away from the hooked Survivor.
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 5s, you see the Auras of all Survivors who are at least 50m away from the hooked Survivor.
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 5s, you see the Auras of all Survivors who are at least 40m away from the hooked Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: Barbecue & Chili is a killer perk taught by Cannibal that, right after hooking a Survivor, reveals the Auras of Survivors who are far away from the hooked one for a brief moment. It helps the killer spot survivors who are out of the immediate area.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a window to find survivors who are hiding the distance, which matters when a hook has just happened and the killer needs a new target. The far-away reveal helps the killer redirect pressure onto a survivor who is trying to stay out of reach.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer who wants a quick re-targeting pulse after each hook. It suits a killer who plays around the board and wants a moment of wide visibility to find the next victim.

BeastOfPrey.name: Beast of Prey
BeastOfPrey.description: Whenever you gain Bloodlust, gain Undetectable for 30/35/40s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you gain Bloodlust, gain Undetectable for 30s.
Whenever you gain Bloodlust, gain Undetectable for 35s.
Whenever you gain Bloodlust, gain Undetectable for 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Beast of Prey is a killer perk taught by Bear that grants Undetectable for a long stretch whenever the killer gains Bloodlust. It lets the killer slip into stealth after a kill or a chase-building moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a long window of invisibility to reposition, hide near hooks, or wait for the next opportunity without being seen. The stealth reward makes each kill feel like it buys real repositioning room.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer who wants stealth as a reward for landing kills. It suits a patient killer who uses each Bloodlust to vanish and set up the next approach.

BetterTogether.name: Better Together
BetterTogether.description:
While you are repairing a Generator:
  • Other Survivors see that Generator's Aura.
  • Whenever the Killer downs a Survivor, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20/25/30s.
descriptionTiers:
While you are repairing a Generator:
  • Other Survivors see that Generator's Aura.
  • Whenever the Killer downs a Survivor, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20s.

While you are repairing a Generator:
  • Other Survivors see that Generator's Aura.
  • Whenever the Killer downs a Survivor, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 25s.

While you are repairing a Generator:
  • Other Survivors see that Generator's Aura.
  • Whenever the Killer downs a Survivor, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Better Together is a survivor perk taught by Nancy that lets other Survivors see a Generator's Aura while a survivor is repairing it. It also reveals the Auras of all Survivors for a while whenever the killer downs someone.
beginner.whyItMatters: It keeps a survivor's progress visible to teammates, so a generator under repair is not a hidden target. The all-survivor reveal after a down state helps the group react and regather.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor wants their generator work to be legible to the team. It rewards a survivor who plays as an anchor on a generator and wants teammates to coordinate around it.

Bitter_Murmur.name: Bitter Murmur
Bitter_Murmur.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Auras of Survivors within 16m of it for 5s.

When all Generators are completed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 5/7/10s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Auras of Survivors within 16m of it for 5s.

When all Generators are completed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 5s.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Auras of Survivors within 16m of it for 5s.

When all Generators are completed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 7s.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Auras of Survivors within 16m of it for 5s.

When all Generators are completed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: Bitter Murmur is a general killer perk that anyone can unlock rather than one taught by a single character. It reveals the Auras of Survivors near a Generator the moment it is completed, and reveals all Survivors for a brief window when every Generator is finished.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a reliable tracking pulse at the two most important progress beats of a trial. The completion reveal helps the killer find survivors who scatter when a generator chimes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a killer wants a dependable source of survivor visibility tied to game progress. It suits a killer who wants to react to generator completions instead of relying on chasing alone.

BloodEcho.name: Blood Echo
BloodEcho.description:
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 20/25/30s, all injured Survivors:
  • Gain Exhausted.
  • Gain Hemorrhage.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 20s, all injured Survivors:
  • Gain Exhausted.
  • Gain Hemorrhage.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 25s, all injured Survivors:
  • Gain Exhausted.
  • Gain Hemorrhage.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, for 30s, all injured Survivors:
  • Gain Exhausted.
  • Gain Hemorrhage.

beginner.whatItIs: Blood Echo is a killer perk taught by Oni that, whenever a Survivor is hooked, makes all injured Survivors gain Exhausted and Hemorrhage for a stretch of time. It pressures the injured group after a hook.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a single hook into board-wide pressure, since every injured survivor starts moving slower and bleeding out. That forces the surviving group to spend their healers and their time dealing with the fallout.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a killer wants hooks to cascade into pressure on the rest of the group. It rewards a killer who hooks early and wants to punish a group that is carrying multiple injuries.

BloodHound.name: Bloodhound
BloodHound.description: Pools of Blood are brighter and last 2/3/4s longer.
descriptionTiers: Pools of Blood are brighter and last 2s longer.
Pools of Blood are brighter and last 3s longer.
Pools of Blood are brighter and last 4s longer.

beginner.whatItIs: BloodHound is a killer perk taught by The Wraith that makes Pools of Blood brighter and easier to spot. Its tracking-focused effect also stretches how long those blood pools stick around before fading.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes blood trails more reliable, which helps a killer track an injured survivor through dark or busy parts of a map. The longer-lasting pools give the killer more time to follow a fresh trail.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer who leans on blood trails to hunt an injured survivor. It suits a patient tracker who wants the trail to stay readable for longer.

BloodPact.name: Blood Pact
BloodPact.description:
While you are not the Obsession:
  • While you or the Obsession are injured, you see each other's Auras.
  • Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, or they finish healing you, while within 16m of each other, you both gain 5/6/7% Haste.


When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.
descriptionTiers:
While you are not the Obsession:
  • While you or the Obsession are injured, you see each other's Auras.
  • Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, or they finish healing you, while within 16m of each other, you both gain 5% Haste.


When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

While you are not the Obsession:
  • While you or the Obsession are injured, you see each other's Auras.
  • Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, or they finish healing you, while within 16m of each other, you both gain 6% Haste.


When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

While you are not the Obsession:
  • While you or the Obsession are injured, you see each other's Auras.
  • Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, or they finish healing you, while within 16m of each other, you both gain 7% Haste.


When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Blood Pact is a survivor perk tied to a specific character that lets a survivor who is not the Obsession see each other's Auras with the Obsession while either one is injured. It also grants both a small speed boost when they heal each other close together, and makes the survivor less likely to become the Obsession at the start.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pairs a survivor with the Obsession so the two can watch each other, which is exactly when the killer is hunting. The reduced chance of becoming the Obsession also softens the early-trial pressure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor wants a built-in link to the Obsession and a steadier start without being the marked target. It rewards a survivor who plays close to the Obsession and wants mutual awareness during injuries.

BloodWarden.name: Blood Warden
BloodWarden.description:
When an Exit Gate is opened, once per trial, when you hook a Survivor, both Exits are blocked for 40/50/60s.

You see the Auras of Survivors within Exit Thresholds.
descriptionTiers:
When an Exit Gate is opened, once per trial, when you hook a Survivor, both Exits are blocked for 40s.

You see the Auras of Survivors within Exit Thresholds.

When an Exit Gate is opened, once per trial, when you hook a Survivor, both Exits are blocked for 50s.

You see the Auras of Survivors within Exit Thresholds.

When an Exit Gate is opened, once per trial, when you hook a Survivor, both Exits are blocked for 60s.

You see the Auras of Survivors within Exit Thresholds.

beginner.whatItIs: Blood Warden is a killer perk taught by Nightmare that, once per trial, blocks both Exit Gates for a while when the killer hooks a Survivor after an Exit Gate has been opened. It also lets the killer see the Auras of Survivors within the Exit Thresholds.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes a survivor who tries to rush an open exit, since hooking them can seal both doors for a stretch. The Exit Threshold visibility also helps the killer guard the escape route.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a killer wants to control the endgame and punish hasty escape attempts. It suits a killer who camps near Exit Gates and wants to keep survivors trapped until the gates re-close.

BoilOver.name: Boil Over
BoilOver.description:
While carried by the Killer:
  • Whenever the Killer falls from at least 1.25m, you gain 33% of your current wiggle progress.
  • Your wiggle is 60/70/80% stronger.
  • Within 16m, the Killer cannot see Hook Auras.
descriptionTiers:
While carried by the Killer:
  • Whenever the Killer falls from at least 1.25m, you gain 33% of your current wiggle progress.
  • Your wiggle is 60% stronger.
  • Within 16m, the Killer cannot see Hook Auras.

While carried by the Killer:
  • Whenever the Killer falls from at least 1.25m, you gain 33% of your current wiggle progress.
  • Your wiggle is 70% stronger.
  • Within 16m, the Killer cannot see Hook Auras.

While carried by the Killer:
  • Whenever the Killer falls from at least 1.25m, you gain 33% of your current wiggle progress.
  • Your wiggle is 80% stronger.
  • Within 16m, the Killer cannot see Hook Auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Boil Over is a survivor perk taught by Kate that helps a Survivor being carried by the killer. It recovers some wiggle progress whenever the killer falls from a height, strengthens the wiggle overall, and blocks the killer's view of Hook Auras at close range.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a carried survivor a better shot at breaking free, since falls and stronger wiggles both chip away at the killer's grip. Hiding Hook Auras also makes rescues and post-carry escapes less predictable for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor wants a real chance to escape a carry. It rewards a survivor who stays calm on the token and wants the killer's stumbles to work in their favor.

Bond.name: Bond
Bond.description: Within 20/28/36m, you see other Survivors' Auras.
descriptionTiers: Within 20m, you see other Survivors' Auras.
Within 28m, you see other Survivors' Auras.
Within 36m, you see other Survivors' Auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Bond is a survivor perk taught by Dwight that lets a survivor see other Survivors' Auras within a generous radius. It keeps teammates visible even when they are out of direct line of sight.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a survivor a running sense of where the group is, which helps with coordination and with knowing who is in danger. The wide radius means a survivor can react to a teammate's trouble from across the map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a survivor wants constant awareness of their teammates' positions. It suits a survivor who plays as a coordinator and wants to spot a struggling ally before the killer does.

BoonDestroyer.name: Shattered Hope
BoonDestroyer.description:
Whenever you snuff a Boon Totem:
  • You see the Auras of all Survivors within its range for 6/7/8s.
  • It is destroyed.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you snuff a Boon Totem:
  • You see the Auras of all Survivors within its range for 6s.
  • It is destroyed.

Whenever you snuff a Boon Totem:
  • You see the Auras of all Survivors within its range for 7s.
  • It is destroyed.

Whenever you snuff a Boon Totem:
  • You see the Auras of all Survivors within its range for 8s.
  • It is destroyed.

beginner.whatItIs: Available to every killer, a general perk that reveals the Auras of all Survivors within a Boon Totem's range once the totem is snuffed. It is a general perk, so any killer can unlock it without needing a specific character.
beginner.whyItMatters: Snuffing a totem that a team blessed for protection instantly exposes everyone nearby. It turns a defensive ritual into a free location reveal for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when running a hunter-style build that already moves quickly between totems and wants the snuff to pay off with a wide reveal. Since it is a general perk, any killer can unlock it without learning a specific character.

BorrowedTime.name: Borrowed Time
BorrowedTime.description:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They retain their unhook Endurance for 6/8/10s longer.
  • They retain their unhook Haste for 10s longer.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They retain their unhook Endurance for 6s longer.
  • They retain their unhook Haste for 10s longer.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They retain their unhook Endurance for 8s longer.
  • They retain their unhook Haste for 10s longer.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor:
  • They retain their unhook Endurance for 10s longer.
  • They retain their unhook Haste for 10s longer.

beginner.whatItIs: Bill's survivor perk extends the brief Endurance and Haste bonus a survivor normally gets after being unhooked. The extra buffer lasts only a short while, so timing the unhook matters.
beginner.whyItMatters: That extra buffer after an unhook gives a freed survivor more time to reach a window, a locker, or a distant generator. It helps most when the killer is close and the freed survivor has nowhere obvious to hide.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if playing a teammate who is likely to get hooked, since the payoff only happens once per unhook. It rewards a survivor who can immediately put distance between themselves and the hook after being freed.

Botany_Knowledge.name: Botany Knowledge
descriptionTiers: You heal 30% faster.
You heal 40% faster.
You heal 50% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Claudette's survivor perk that makes healing actions complete noticeably faster than normal. The speed bonus applies to every heal, whether reviving a downed ally or patching up an injury.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster healing matters most in late-trial moments when a downed teammate needs to be revived quickly. It also helps a survivor recover a long injury sooner while the killer roams nearby.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on any survivor who will be doing a lot of healing, whether that is a dedicated rescue role or a teammate who tops up allies between chases. It is a steady benefit that fits any build wanting less time spent kneeling at a hook or over an ally.

Breakdown.name: Breakdown
Breakdown.description:
Whenever you are unhooked:
  • The Hook breaks, then is repaired after 180s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 4/5/6s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you are unhooked:
  • The Hook breaks, then is repaired after 180s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 4s.

Whenever you are unhooked:
  • The Hook breaks, then is repaired after 180s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 5s.

Whenever you are unhooked:
  • The Hook breaks, then is repaired after 180s.
  • You see the Killer's Aura for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: Jeff's survivor perk that, right after an unhook, breaks the hook that was used and then briefly reveals the killer's Aura. The broken hook cannot be used again for a long stretch, denying the killer a rescue spot.
beginner.whyItMatters: Destroying the hook denies the killer a rescue spot for a long stretch. The short aura window also helps the freed survivor figure out which way to run before being hooked again.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when playing the survivor who is most likely to get hooked and wants to punish the killer for choosing that hook. It is also useful when a team is struggling against repeated double-downs on the same spot.

Breakout.name: Breakout
Breakout.description:
Within 5m of a carried Survivor:
  • You gain 6/8/10% Haste.
  • The carried Survivor wiggles 25% faster.
descriptionTiers:
Within 5m of a carried Survivor:
  • You gain 6% Haste.
  • The carried Survivor wiggles 25% faster.

Within 5m of a carried Survivor:
  • You gain 8% Haste.
  • The carried Survivor wiggles 25% faster.

Within 5m of a carried Survivor:
  • You gain 10% Haste.
  • The carried Survivor wiggles 25% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Yui's survivor perk that grants Haste to any survivor who stands near a carried Survivor. It also makes the carried Survivor wiggle out of the carry faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shortens the dangerous window between a pickup and the hook, since the carried survivor escapes sooner. The rescuer also has a speed advantage to get back into cover before the killer returns.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor whose job is to track the killer's carrying path, because it only pays off while standing close to a carried teammate. It wants to be near the killer's movement rather than at a generator.

Brutal_Strength.name: Brutal Strength
Brutal_Strength.description: You basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 10/15/20% faster.
descriptionTiers: You basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 10% faster.
You basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 15% faster.
You basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls, and damage Generators 20% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: The Trapper's killer perk lets basic attacks destroy pallets and breakable walls. It also speeds up generator damage, so the killer punishes repairs with regular swings.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the killer's regular swings into map-control tools, so pallets that normally protect survivors can be broken without spending a special ability. Generators are also punished faster, rewarding a killer who keeps pressure on repair.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when running a killer who wants to break through survivor defenses aggressively rather than relying on a power to remove pallets. The generator damage bonus suits a hunter who stays close to repairs and wants every swing to count.

BuckleUp.name: Buckle Up
BuckleUp.description:
While healing a downed Survivor, you both see the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you finish healing a downed Survivor or fully recover:
  • The Survivor gains 50% Haste for 3/4/5s.
  • The Survivor leaves no Scratch Marks for 3/4/5s.
descriptionTiers:
While healing a downed Survivor, you both see the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you finish healing a downed Survivor or fully recover:
  • The Survivor gains 50% Haste for 3s.
  • The Survivor leaves no Scratch Marks for 3s.

While healing a downed Survivor, you both see the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you finish healing a downed Survivor or fully recover:
  • The Survivor gains 50% Haste for 4s.
  • The Survivor leaves no Scratch Marks for 4s.

While healing a downed Survivor, you both see the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you finish healing a downed Survivor or fully recover:
  • The Survivor gains 50% Haste for 5s.
  • The Survivor leaves no Scratch Marks for 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Ash's survivor perk that lets the healer and the downed survivor both see the killer's Aura during a healing action. After the healing finishes or a survivor fully recovers, the survivor gains a short burst of Haste and leaves no Scratch Marks for a brief moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing where the killer is during a vulnerable healing can save a rescue from being interrupted. The short stealth window afterward helps the revived survivor slip away without trailing a path of Scratch Marks back to the hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who wants safer healing and a clean escape after being revived. The aura sight helps the healer spot a stalker, and the post-healing stealth helps the rescued teammate reach cover.

BuiltToLast.name: Built to Last
BuiltToLast.description:
While holding a depleted item, after hiding in a Locker for 14/12/10s, it is recharged to 99%.

Each time you recharge an item this way, it recharges 33% fewer Charges.
descriptionTiers:
While holding a depleted item, after hiding in a Locker for 14s, it is recharged to 99%.

Each time you recharge an item this way, it recharges 33% fewer Charges.

While holding a depleted item, after hiding in a Locker for 12s, it is recharged to 99%.

Each time you recharge an item this way, it recharges 33% fewer Charges.

While holding a depleted item, after hiding in a Locker for 10s, it is recharged to 99%.

Each time you recharge an item this way, it recharges 33% fewer Charges.

beginner.whatItIs: Felix Richter's survivor adaptation perk refills a depleted item to near-full when its holder hides in a locker for a short time. Each recharge permanently lowers how many charges the item can hold, so the item becomes less reliable as the match goes on.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a locker stop from a simple escape into a chance to bring a dead flashlight, pallet, or med kit back to life. That is especially valuable when the trial is running low on useful items and the survivor cannot afford to waste one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the survivor is playing stealthy, locker-hiding routes and wants to stretch the life of their carried items. The recharge only works while hidden in a locker and gets weaker with each use.

Calm_Spirit.name: Calm Spirit
Calm_Spirit.description:
You do not scare Crows or scream.

You bless and cleanse Totems, and unlock Chests silently, but 40/35/30% slower.
descriptionTiers:
You do not scare Crows or scream.

You bless and cleanse Totems, and unlock Chests silently, but 40% slower.

You do not scare Crows or scream.

You bless and cleanse Totems, and unlock Chests silently, but 35% slower.

You do not scare Crows or scream.

You bless and cleanse Totems, and unlock Chests silently, but 30% slower.

beginner.whatItIs: Jake's survivor perk that stops the survivor from scaring Crows or screaming. It also lets them bless, cleanse, and unlock Chests silently, though those actions take a bit longer to complete.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the noise and scream penalty makes totem hunting and chest looting far safer. The killer cannot hear or see the tell that normally gives the survivor's position away.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who wants to work Totems and Chests without alerting the killer. It is particularly useful in a trial where the team needs totem protection but the killer is hunting aggressively.

Camaraderie.name: Camaraderie
Camaraderie.description: While you are struggling on Hook, when another Survivor gets within 16m, the timer is paused for 26/30/34s.
descriptionTiers: While you are struggling on Hook, when another Survivor gets within 16m, the timer is paused for 26s.
While you are struggling on Hook, when another Survivor gets within 16m, the timer is paused for 30s.
While you are struggling on Hook, when another Survivor gets within 16m, the timer is paused for 34s.

beginner.whatItIs: Steve's survivor perk that pauses the hook struggle timer whenever another survivor comes within a reasonable distance of a hooked survivor. The pause only lasts while the ally is nearby, so it is a temporary reprieve rather than a full save.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the hooked survivor a real fighting chance to escape a hook, since even a brief pause can be the difference between being sacrificed and walking away. It also encourages teammates to check on a hooked ally rather than ignoring them.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when playing in a coordinated team where at least one other survivor will be near the hooked teammate. The perk does nothing if the survivor is hooked alone far from allies, so it wants team play to shine.

CorruptIntervention.name: Corrupt Intervention
CorruptIntervention.description: When the trial starts, the 3 farthest Generators from you are blocked for 80/100/120s, or until you down a Survivor.
descriptionTiers: When the trial starts, the 3 farthest Generators from you are blocked for 80s, or until you down a Survivor.
When the trial starts, the 3 farthest Generators from you are blocked for 100s, or until you down a Survivor.
When the trial starts, the 3 farthest Generators from you are blocked for 120s, or until you down a Survivor.

beginner.whatItIs: Plague's killer perk that blocks the farthest generators from the killer at the start of the trial. The block lasts for a set duration or until the first down, whichever comes first.
beginner.whyItMatters: Forcing the team to repair closer generators at the start slows their overall progress and pins them in a smaller area. It gives the killer a wider zone to search and control early on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when running Plague and wanting to dictate where the trial starts. The blocked generators force survivors into a tighter radius while the killer hunts freely outside it.

Coulrophobia.name: Coulrophobia
Coulrophobia.description:
Survivors within your Terror Radius:
  • Heal 20/25/30% slower.
  • While healing, basic Skill Checks spin 50% faster.
descriptionTiers:
Survivors within your Terror Radius:
  • Heal 20% slower.
  • While healing, basic Skill Checks spin 50% faster.

Survivors within your Terror Radius:
  • Heal 25% slower.
  • While healing, basic Skill Checks spin 50% faster.

Survivors within your Terror Radius:
  • Heal 30% slower.
  • While healing, basic Skill Checks spin 50% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Clown's killer perk that slows survivor healing and makes their Skill Checks spin faster. Both effects apply while survivors are inside the killer's Terror Radius.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the killer's mere presence into a direct tax on every healing and repair action. Survivors feel pressure even when the killer is not actively chasing, and are forced to move or stop working.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Clown and wanting to punish a team that camps a healing spot or hovers near a generator while the killer circles. The effect only applies within Terror Radius, so it rewards keeping survivors at arm's length.

CruelConfinement.name: Cruel Limits
CruelConfinement.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You see the Auras of all Windows for 20/25/30s.
  • All Windows are blocked for Survivors for 20/25/30s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You see the Auras of all Windows for 20s.
  • All Windows are blocked for Survivors for 20s.

Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You see the Auras of all Windows for 25s.
  • All Windows are blocked for Survivors for 25s.

Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You see the Auras of all Windows for 30s.
  • All Windows are blocked for Survivors for 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Demogorgon's killer perk that, each time a generator is completed, briefly blocks all windows for survivors. It also reveals the Auras of all windows to the killer during that same window.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the survivors' escape route at the exact moment they would normally use it to break a chase. The aura reveal also helps the killer track survivors hiding in closets or behind pallets.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Demogorgon and wanting to control end-of-chase moments. The window block punishes survivors who rely on vaulting out to escape a cornered position.

Dance_with_me.name: Dance With Me
Dance_with_me.description: Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, medium-vault, or fast-vault, you leave no Scratch Marks for 5s. Cooldown: 25/20/15s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, medium-vault, or fast-vault, you leave no Scratch Marks for 5s. Cooldown: 25s.
Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, medium-vault, or fast-vault, you leave no Scratch Marks for 5s. Cooldown: 20s.
Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, medium-vault, or fast-vault, you leave no Scratch Marks for 5s. Cooldown: 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: Kate's survivor perk that, after a fast locker exit, medium vault, or fast vault, makes the survivor leave no Scratch Marks for a short time. There is a cooldown between uses, so it cannot be spammed on every vault.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hiding Scratch Marks after a vault or locker pop makes it much harder for a tracking killer to follow the survivor's path. It is especially valuable for a survivor who uses vaults and lockers as their main escape tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor whose escape style leans heavily on lockers and window vaults. The stealth window only triggers after those specific actions, so it wants to be in the middle of a chase to matter.

Dark_Sense.name: Dark Sense
Dark_Sense.description: Whenever a Generator is completed, when the Killer gets within 24m of you, you see their Aura for 5/7/10s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Generator is completed, when the Killer gets within 24m of you, you see their Aura for 5s.
Whenever a Generator is completed, when the Killer gets within 24m of you, you see their Aura for 7s.
Whenever a Generator is completed, when the Killer gets within 24m of you, you see their Aura for 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: Revealing the killer's Aura for a short time after any generator is completed, a general perk available to every survivor. The reveal only fires when the killer is within a reasonable distance at the moment of completion.
beginner.whyItMatters: That reveal at a generator finish is exactly when a killer is most likely to strike. It gives the repairing survivor a chance to notice the ambush and react before the attack lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing a repair-heavy survivor who wants an early warning that the killer is closing in. It only fires after a generator is completed, so it wants the killer to be in the area at that moment.

DarkDevotion.name: Dark Devotion
DarkDevotion.description:
Whenever the Obsession takes damage, for 35/40/45s:
  • Your Terror Radius is set to 40m.
  • The Obsession has your Terror Radius.
  • You gain Undetectable.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Obsession takes damage, for 35s:
  • Your Terror Radius is set to 40m.
  • The Obsession has your Terror Radius.
  • You gain Undetectable.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, for 40s:
  • Your Terror Radius is set to 40m.
  • The Obsession has your Terror Radius.
  • You gain Undetectable.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, for 45s:
  • Your Terror Radius is set to 40m.
  • The Obsession has your Terror Radius.
  • You gain Undetectable.

beginner.whatItIs: Plague's killer perk that, whenever the Obsession takes damage, briefly widens the Terror Radius and makes the killer Undetectable. The Obsession also inherits that expanded Terror Radius during the same window.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single hit on the Obsession turns into a wide reveal window for the killer and a moment of full stealth. It rewards aggression on the marked survivor and can catch a whole team off guard.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Plague and planning to focus the Obsession early. The payoff only triggers when the Obsession is hit, and the stealth window works best when the killer is already moving through a building or corridor.

DeadHard.name: Dead Hard
DeadHard.description:
Whenever you are unhooked, while injured and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain Endurance for 0.5s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you are unhooked, while injured and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain Endurance for 0.5s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60s.

Whenever you are unhooked, while injured and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain Endurance for 0.5s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 50s.

Whenever you are unhooked, while injured and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain Endurance for 0.5s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: David King's survivor perk can be activated while injured and running to grant a short burst of Endurance that shrugs off the next hit. Once the charge is spent, it needs real time to come back.
beginner.whyItMatters: That split-second of invulnerability can turn a lost chase into an escape. It buys the extra distance needed to reach a pallet, a window, or a locker before the killer's animation connects.
beginner.whenToUseIt: David King teaches this, so bring it to a chase-heavy build or a team that gets hooked often. Activate it the moment a hit is about to land while still injured and moving, since the brief burst of endurance is meant to shrug off a single swing, not to start a sprint from rest.

DeadMansSwitch.name: Dead Man’s Switch
DeadMansSwitch.description: When you hook a Survivor, the first time a Survivor stops repairing a Generator, it is blocked for 25/30/35s. Cooldown: 25/30/35s.
descriptionTiers: When you hook a Survivor, the first time a Survivor stops repairing a Generator, it is blocked for 25s. Cooldown: 25s.
When you hook a Survivor, the first time a Survivor stops repairing a Generator, it is blocked for 30s. Cooldown: 30s.
When you hook a Survivor, the first time a Survivor stops repairing a Generator, it is blocked for 35s. Cooldown: 35s.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk taught by The Deathslinger that, after hooking a survivor, blocks a generator the first time any survivor stops repairing it. There is a cooldown before it can fire again after each hook.
beginner.whyItMatters: It breaks a team's rhythm by punishing the moment a survivor steps away from a generator. A simple pause becomes a blocked repair that wastes time and forces the team to pick a new target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing The Deathslinger and wanting to control generator flow. The block only fires once per hook, so it works best when the killer hooks early and the team is spread across multiple generators.

Deathbound.name: Deathbound
Deathbound.description:
Whenever a Survivor finishes healing another, they scream. Then, until they take damage, while they are at least 12/8/4m away from that Survivor:
  • They gain Oblivious.
  • They see that Survivor's Aura.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Survivor finishes healing another, they scream. Then, until they take damage, while they are at least 12m away from that Survivor:
  • They gain Oblivious.
  • They see that Survivor's Aura.

Whenever a Survivor finishes healing another, they scream. Then, until they take damage, while they are at least 8m away from that Survivor:
  • They gain Oblivious.
  • They see that Survivor's Aura.

Whenever a Survivor finishes healing another, they scream. Then, until they take damage, while they are at least 4m away from that Survivor:
  • They gain Oblivious.
  • They see that Survivor's Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer trickery and tracking perk taught by The Executioner. When a survivor finishes healing a teammate, that survivor is forced to scream. As long as the healer remains at a distance and has not been hit, they suffer Oblivious while the killer can see their Aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: The forced scream gives the killer a free position ping at a vulnerable moment. The Oblivious effect pushes the healer away from the team, splitting survivors up and making it harder to stack defenses around a hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a build around The Executioner that favors keeping distance while survivors cluster to heal one another. The instant a heal finishes, the healer screams and loses the ability to notice the killer while their own Aura is exposed, opening a wide window to push them before they react.

DecisiveStrike.name: Decisive Strike
DecisiveStrike.description:
Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 40/50/60s: when the Killer picks you up, once per trial, hit a Special Skill check:
  • Stun the Killer for 4s.
  • Become the Obsession.


This is disabled by conspicuous actions. At the start of the trial, you are more likely to be the Obsession.
descriptionTiers:
Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 40s: when the Killer picks you up, once per trial, hit a Special Skill check:
  • Stun the Killer for 4s.
  • Become the Obsession.


This is disabled by conspicuous actions. At the start of the trial, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 50s: when the Killer picks you up, once per trial, hit a Special Skill check:
  • Stun the Killer for 4s.
  • Become the Obsession.


This is disabled by conspicuous actions. At the start of the trial, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 60s: when the Killer picks you up, once per trial, hit a Special Skill check:
  • Stun the Killer for 4s.
  • Become the Obsession.


This is disabled by conspicuous actions. At the start of the trial, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Laurie that arms a Special Skill Check for a short window right after being unhooked, and only while generators are still being completed. If the killer picks the survivor up while that window is still active, once per trial, they can hit the check to stun the killer, but doing so makes them the Obsession for the rest of the trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The one-time stun can break a chase entirely and buy a whole team breathing room. The Obsession penalty, however, means the survivor then becomes the killer's primary target, making it a high-risk escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who is comfortable becoming the Obsession after an escape. The perk only fires on the first pickup after an unhook, and the Obsession status afterward means the killer will hunt that survivor hard until the trial ends.

Deerstalker.name: Deerstalker
Deerstalker.description:
Every 40/35/30s, the Survivor with the least time in chase sees your Aura for 3s.

While a Survivor sees your Aura, you see their Aura.
descriptionTiers:
Every 40s, the Survivor with the least time in chase sees your Aura for 3s.

While a Survivor sees your Aura, you see their Aura.

Every 35s, the Survivor with the least time in chase sees your Aura for 3s.

While a Survivor sees your Aura, you see their Aura.

Every 30s, the Survivor with the least time in chase sees your Aura for 3s.

While a Survivor sees your Aura, you see their Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Deerstalker is a general killer perk in the tracking family. It briefly reveals the killer's own Aura to the survivor who has spent the least time in a chase, and shows that survivor's Aura back to the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: It targets a survivor who avoids danger, so the safer a survivor plays, the more likely their Aura is exposed. That turns a passive survivor's caution into a liability, since staying safe is exactly what triggers the reveal.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants cheap information on a passive survivor. Trading the killer's own visibility for a glimpse of that survivor is usually worth it against someone who camps near a generator.

Deja_Vu.name: Deja Vu
Deja_Vu.description: You see the Auras of the 3 Generators closest to each other and repair them 4/5/6% faster.
descriptionTiers: You see the Auras of the 3 Generators closest to each other and repair them 4% faster.
You see the Auras of the 3 Generators closest to each other and repair them 5% faster.
You see the Auras of the 3 Generators closest to each other and repair them 6% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Deja Vu is a general survivor perk in the perception family. It highlights the Auras of several nearby generators and lets a survivor repair each of them faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: A survivor who knows exactly which generators are nearby can commit to a cluster and work them faster. That speeds the whole board and reduces the need to search for work.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a generator-focused role where the survivor can settle around a group of machines. It pays off most when those highlighted generators are the ones being repaired.

Deliverance.name: Deliverance
Deliverance.description: Once per trial, when you safely unhook another Survivor, you can unhook yourself. When you unhook yourself this way, you gain Broken for 160/140/120s.
descriptionTiers: Once per trial, when you safely unhook another Survivor, you can unhook yourself. When you unhook yourself this way, you gain Broken for 160s.
Once per trial, when you safely unhook another Survivor, you can unhook yourself. When you unhook yourself this way, you gain Broken for 140s.
Once per trial, when you safely unhook another Survivor, you can unhook yourself. When you unhook yourself this way, you gain Broken for 120s.

beginner.whatItIs: Deliverance is a survivor perk taught by Adam. Once a survivor safely unhooks another survivor, it lets that survivor free themselves from a hook as well.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a single successful rescue into a second, self-rescue, which can save a survivor hooked on their own hook. That is especially valuable late in a trial when one more hook would otherwise end the run.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor is built for rescues and wants a backup way to free themselves after safely rescuing a teammate. The self-unhook carries a long broken penalty that is easier to accept in a late trial.

DesperateMeasures.name: Desperate Measures
DesperateMeasures.description:
For each injured, downed, or hooked Survivor:
  • You heal 16/18/20% faster.
  • You unhook 16/18/20% faster.
descriptionTiers:
For each injured, downed, or hooked Survivor:
  • You heal 16% faster.
  • You unhook 16% faster.

For each injured, downed, or hooked Survivor:
  • You heal 18% faster.
  • You unhook 18% faster.

For each injured, downed, or hooked Survivor:
  • You heal 20% faster.
  • You unhook 20% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Desperate Measures is a survivor perk tied to one specific character. It boosts healing and unhooking speed, with the bonus growing as more survivors are hurt, downed, or hooked.
beginner.whyItMatters: The more the team is hurt, the faster healing and rescues become, which matters in a rough trial where many survivors are down or hooked at once. It keeps a struggling team moving instead of stalling on the hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a rescue or support role, since the bonus climbs as the team's condition worsens. A downed or hooked teammate is exactly when it earns its keep.

DetectivesHunch.name: Detective's Hunch
DetectivesHunch.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, for 20s, within 32/48/64m of you:
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.
  • You see the Auras of Totems.

Whenever a Generator is completed, for 20s, within 48m of you:

Whenever a Generator is completed, for 20s, within 64m of you:
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.
  • You see the Auras of Totems.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Detective Tapp. When a generator is finished, it briefly reveals the Auras of chests, generators, and totems around the survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: It surfaces hidden items, totems, and unworked generators the moment a machine is completed. That lets a survivor pivot straight to the next useful objective without guessing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a survivor who wants to react to each completed generator by finding the nearest chest, totem, or unworked machine. The reveal is timed around generator finishes, so it suits a reactive playstyle.

Discordance.name: Discordance
Discordance.description:
Within 64/96/128m of you, whenever a Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you are alerted.

While that Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you see its Aura. When it is no longer being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, this ends after 4s.
descriptionTiers:
Within 64m of you, whenever a Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you are alerted.

While that Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you see its Aura. When it is no longer being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, this ends after 4s.

Within 96m of you, whenever a Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you are alerted.

While that Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you see its Aura. When it is no longer being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, this ends after 4s.

Within 128m of you, whenever a Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you are alerted.

While that Generator is being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, you see its Aura. When it is no longer being repaired by at least 2 Survivors, this ends after 4s.

beginner.whatItIs: Discordance is a killer perk taught by Legion. It alerts the killer when two or more survivors are working the same generator and keeps that generator's Aura visible.
beginner.whyItMatters: It flags coordinated generator work, so a killer can rush to stop two survivors who are stacking progress on one machine. Breaking up that teamwork is where it earns its place on a killer's loadout.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants to counter a coordinated push, since the alert fires whenever two or more survivors are repairing the same generator. It suits a killer who plays off teamwork more than raw speed.

Distortion.name: Distortion
Distortion.description:
When the trial starts, and after being chased for 15s, you earn 1 Token, up to 2.

While not downed, whenever the Killer attempts to see your Aura, spend 1 Token. Then, for the next 8/10/12s:
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.
descriptionTiers:

While not downed, whenever the Killer attempts to see your Aura, spend 1 Token. Then, for the next 8s:
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

When the trial starts, and after being chased for 15s, you earn 1 Token, up to 2.

While not downed, whenever the Killer attempts to see your Aura, spend 1 Token. Then, for the next 10s:
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

When the trial starts, and after being chased for 15s, you earn 1 Token, up to 2.

While not downed, whenever the Killer attempts to see your Aura, spend 1 Token. Then, for the next 12s:
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: Distortion is a survivor perk taught by Jeff. It builds up tokens while surviving chases, and those tokens can be spent to hide the survivor's Aura and stop scratch marks for a while.
beginner.whyItMatters: Spending a token blinds the killer's view of the survivor and erases scratch marks, which helps a survivor who keeps getting caught out in the open. It is a clean way to break a chase or slip away without being tracked by trail.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Save the tokens for the moment a chase looks likely to end badly, or when the survivor wants to slip away unseen. Each token is earned by surviving a chase, so it is a limited resource best spent at a crunch.

Distressing.name: Distressing
descriptionTiers: Your Terror Radius is 20% larger.
Your Terror Radius is 25% larger.
Your Terror Radius is 30% larger.

beginner.whatItIs: Distressing is a general killer perk in the trickery family. It widens the killer's terror radius, so chases begin at a greater distance than usual.
beginner.whyItMatters: A wider terror radius means chases start sooner, which pressures survivors who walk in the open. It makes crossing exposed ground riskier and rewards a killer who stays patient.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants earlier chases and to punish careless movement. The bigger radius rewards any survivor who carelessly crosses open ground, so it suits a patient, zone-control playstyle.

Diversion.name: Diversion
Diversion.description:
After hiding for 30/25/20s within the Killer's Terror Radius, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to throw a pebble 20m away:
  • The Killer is alerted.
  • The pebble leaves Scratch Marks.
descriptionTiers:
After hiding for 30s within the Killer's Terror Radius, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to throw a pebble 20m away:

  • The pebble leaves Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: Diversion is a survivor perk taught by Adam. After hiding crouched inside the killer's terror radius, it lets the survivor throw a pebble away to draw the killer's attention and leave scratch marks.
beginner.whyItMatters: A pebble that leaves scratch marks can pull the killer away from a generator or a healing survivor. That buys a teammate time to finish their task while the killer investigates the sound.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a survivor who camps in lockers or vents near generators, since hiding inside the terror radius first is what unlocks the pebble throw. It suits a support role that distracts the killer for the team.

DragonsGrip.name: Dragon’s Grip
DragonsGrip.description:
Whenever you damage a Generator, for the next 30s, the first Survivor that repairs that Generator:
  • They scream, then you are alerted to their position for 4s.
  • They gain Exposed for 60s.


Cooldown: 60/45/30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Dragon's Grip is a killer perk tied to one specific character. Whenever the killer damages a generator, it flags the first survivor who later repairs it, making them scream, become exposed, and reveal their position.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a damaged generator into a trap on the next repairer, exposing them and alerting the killer. That deters survivors from rushing to fix a wounded machine.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants to punish repair-after-damage, since the first survivor who works a hurt generator pays the price. It rewards a killer who chokes down a team's repair output.

Dying_Light.name: Dying Light
Dying_Light.description:
Whenever you hook a Survivor that is not the Obsession, earn 1 token.

While the Obsession is alive, for each Token:
  • Other Survivors heal 2/2.5/3% slower.
  • Other Survivors repair 2/2.5/3% slower.
  • Other Survivors sabotage Hooks 2/2.5/3% slower.


The Obsession:
  • Heals other Survivors 33% faster.
  • Unhooks other Survivors 33% faster.

The Obsession:

beginner.whatItIs: Dying Light is a killer perk taught by Shape. It builds up a token each time the killer hooks a survivor who is not the obsession. While the obsession is alive, those tokens slow healing, repair, and hook sabotage for every other survivor, while the obsession heals and unhooks other survivors faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: It weakens the team around a protected obsession, so a killer who keeps the obsession alive can slow every other survivor's healing, repair, and hook sabotage at once. That keeps a killer's preferred target safe while the rest of the team stalls.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a killer who can keep one survivor pinned as the obsession, since the slowing effect on the other survivors grows as more hooks are collected. It suits a killer who commits to a single target and lets the team crumble around them.

Empathy.name: Empathy
Empathy.description: Within 64/96/128m, you see the Auras of injured Survivors.
descriptionTiers: Within 64m, you see the Auras of injured Survivors.
Within 96m, you see the Auras of injured Survivors.
Within 128m, you see the Auras of injured Survivors.

beginner.whatItIs: Empathy is a survivor perk taught by Claudette. It lets a survivor see the Auras of injured survivors within a wide radius, so a hurt teammate is easier to spot.
beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing where hurt teammates are lets a survivor rush to heal or rescue them. That keeps the team functional in a rough trial where people are falling over one by one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a support or healing role, since it pays off when a survivor wants to track down injured teammates quickly. It suits a survivor who prioritizes keeping the team alive over pushing generators.

Enduring.name: Enduring
Enduring.description: While not carrying a Survivor, Pallet-stuns are 40/45/50% shorter.
descriptionTiers: While not carrying a Survivor, Pallet-stuns are 40% shorter.
While not carrying a Survivor, Pallet-stuns are 45% shorter.
While not carrying a Survivor, Pallet-stuns are 50% shorter.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk taught by The Hillbilly that shortens how long a pallet stun lasts while the killer is not carrying a survivor. That lets the killer get moving again and close the distance sooner after a pallet drop.
beginner.whyItMatters: Shorter pallet-stuns let the killer re-engage faster after a survivor drops a pallet. That helps close out a chase that should have ended at the pallet.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a killer who relies on pallet fights, since it pays off whenever a survivor drops a pallet to break the chase. It rewards a killer who wants to punish a survivor's escape attempt.

FireUp.name: Fire Up
FireUp.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token:
  • You basic-break Pallets and Breakable Walls 4/5/6% faster.
  • You damage Generators 4/5/6% faster.
  • You pick-up and drop Survivors 4/5/6% faster.
  • You basic-vault Windows 4/5/6% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Fire Up is a killer perk taught by Nightmare. It builds up a handful of tokens as generators are completed. Each token then makes the killer break pallets and walls faster, damage generators faster, vault windows faster, and pick survivors up and drop them faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Speeding up pallets, walls, windows, and generator damage lets the killer keep pressure on across the map. That is useful for a map-control style of play that rarely loses momentum.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a killer who wants to move faster between objectives and hold the chase, since the bonus builds as generators are completed. It suits a killer who plays the whole board and wants to stay ahead of the survivors' pace.

Fixated.name: Fixated
Fixated.description:
While walking, you gain 10/15/20% Haste.

You see your own Scratch Marks.
descriptionTiers:

You see your own Scratch Marks.

You see your own Scratch Marks.

While walking, you gain 20% Haste.

You see your own Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: Fixated is a survivor perk taught by Nancy. It grants extra walking speed while moving at a walk and lets the survivor see their own scratch marks.
beginner.whyItMatters: Extra walking speed and self-visible scratch marks help a survivor manage their own trail. That is handy for anyone who wants to control where they leave signs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a survivor who values stealth and careful movement, since walking speed and self-trail visibility both serve a cautious playstyle. It suits a survivor who wants to stay hidden and move deliberately.

FlipFlop.name: Flip-Flop
FlipFlop.description: While downed, whenever the Killer picks you up, 50% of your recovery progress is added to your wiggle progress, up to 40/45/50%.
descriptionTiers: While downed, whenever the Killer picks you up, 50% of your recovery progress is added to your wiggle progress, up to 40%.
While downed, whenever the Killer picks you up, 50% of your recovery progress is added to your wiggle progress, up to 45%.
While downed, whenever the Killer picks you up, 50% of your recovery progress is added to your wiggle progress, up to 50%.

beginner.whatItIs: Flip-Flop is a survivor perk taught by Ash. While downed, it carries part of a survivor's recovery progress over into their wiggle progress the moment the killer picks them up.
beginner.whyItMatters: Carrying recovery progress into the wiggle bar means a survivor who has already been recovering needs less effort to escape the killer's arms. That turns a caught survivor's prior struggle into a real chance of breaking free.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a survivor expects to be picked up and wants a fighting chance to wiggle free, since it converts some of their recovery progress into escape progress the instant the hook is engaged. It rewards a downed survivor who kept working before being caught, so it fits a playstyle that stays active near generators rather than crouching in safety.

ForcedPenance.name: Forced Penance
ForcedPenance.description: Whenever a Survivor takes a protection hit, they gain Broken for 60/70/80s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor takes a protection hit, they gain Broken for 60s.
Whenever a Survivor takes a protection hit, they gain Broken for 70s.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk tied to a single character that punishes survivors for leaning on protective effects, marking anyone who absorbs a protection hit with Broken for a long stretch of time. Because the penalty outlasts the moment of the save, teammates who shield one another end up trading a small reprieve for a lingering debuff.
beginner.whyItMatters: Punishing a survivor who uses a protection hit keeps defenders from freely stacking protection. That weakens a team that leans on that kind of cover to hold a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer expects the opposing team to lean on protection perks, since the Broken penalty applies the moment a protection hit lands on a survivor. It punishes teams that rely on safety nets, so it fits a playstyle that pressures survivors to commit to offense rather than hiding behind defensive layers.

ForThePeople.name: For the People
ForThePeople.description:
While healthy and healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit, use Active Ability button to heal them instantly:
  • You take damage.
  • You gain Broken for 80/70/60s.
  • You become the Obsession.


When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Zarina Kassir teaches a bare-handed heal that finishes in an instant. The cost is steep: whoever triggers it drops a health state, carries Broken for a stretch afterwards and becomes the Obsession. In exchange, being picked as the Obsession at the opening of a trial is less likely.
beginner.whyItMatters: An instant heal can save a teammate in a crunch when no other option is available. The trade of damage, broken, and obsession makes it a high-risk, high-reward rescue tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a survivor built around healing who is willing to sacrifice themselves to save a teammate, since the instant heal is the payoff for taking the hit. It suits a selfless support role more than a generator pusher.

FranklinsLoss.name: Franklin's Demise
FranklinsLoss.description:
Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack, they drop their item.

Within 32/48/64m, you see the Auras of dropped items.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack, they drop their item.

beginner.whatItIs: Franklin's Demise is a killer perk taught by Cannibal. Whenever the killer hits a survivor with a basic attack, it makes the survivor drop their item, and it reveals the Aura of dropped items nearby.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stripping a survivor of their item on a basic attack removes their safety net. Revealing dropped items then lets the killer reclaim or track them around the map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a killer who wants to punish item use and control dropped loot, since both effects fire around the killer's attacks. It suits a killer who wants survivors playing without a safety net.

FurtiveChase.name: Furtive Chase
FurtiveChase.description:
Whenever you hook the Obsession:
  • You gain 10% Haste for 14/16/18s.

Whenever the Obsession is unhooked, the Survivor who unhooked them becomes the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Furtive Chase is a killer perk taught by Ghostface. Whenever the killer hooks the obsession, it grants haste and undetectable for a while. It also makes the survivor who later unhooks the obsession become the new obsession.
beginner.whyItMatters: Granting haste and undetectable after a hook lets the killer slip away and reposition. Passing the obsession to the rescuer keeps pressure on the whole team.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Suited to a killer who plans to hook the Obsession and reposition quickly, since the Haste and Undetectable burst rewards staying mobile after every hook. The obsession transfer on unhook keeps pressure spreading across the team, so it fits a playstyle that rotates targets and never stays in one loop.

Gearhead.name: Gearhead
Gearhead.description: Whenever a Survivor takes damage, for the next 30s, whenever a Survivor repairing a Generator hits a good basic Skill Check, you see their Aura for 6/7/8s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor takes damage, for the next 30s, whenever a Survivor repairing a Generator hits a good basic Skill Check, you see their Aura for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: The Deathslinger's killer perk watches for tracking opportunities tied to Skill Checks. It reveals a survivor's Aura for a short window whenever they land a good basic Skill Check during a generator repair, but only if that survivor has recently taken damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the repair process into a tracking moment, since the killer can pinpoint where a survivor is working the instant they clean a Skill Check. The damage precondition means it rewards an aggressive approach that hurts survivors before hunting them down at generators.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that chases hard and damages survivors before closing in on generator work. A killer who plays aggressively around the map will get the most value out of the brief Aura window it provides.

GeneratorOvercharge.name: Overcharge
GeneratorOvercharge.description:
Whenever you damage a Generator:
  • Its regression speed will go from 85% to 130% over the next 30s.
  • The next Survivor who starts repairing it gets a special Skill Check. If they miss it, they lose 2/3/4% more progress.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you damage a Generator:
  • Its regression speed will go from 85% to 130% over the next 30s.
  • The next Survivor who starts repairing it gets a special Skill Check. If they miss it, they lose 2% more progress.

Whenever you damage a Generator:
