beginner.whatItIs: It punishes survivor investment in a generator by making the next damage to it regress progress much faster than normal for a short period. It also forces the next survivor who starts repairing that damaged generator to pass a special Skill Check, and missing it costs extra progress.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes generators feel fragile and risky to work on, since a single hit can throw away a meaningful chunk of progress. Survivors must think harder about when to repair and who gets the first Skill Check after damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in any build that wants to slow the pace and make each generator feel costly to the survivor team. It is taught by a masked slasher character and fits naturally into any killer's routine since damaging generators is part of every killer's loop.

HangmansTrick.name: Scourge Hook: Hangman's Trick
HangmansTrick.description:
When the trial starts, 4 random Hooks become Scourge Hooks.

While carrying a Survivor, you see the Auras of Survivors within 12/14/16m of Scourge Hooks.

Whenever a Survivor starts sabotaging a Hook, you are alerted.
descriptionTiers:

beginner.whatItIs: An obstruction tool for the Pig that converts random hooks at trial start into Scourge Hooks. While carrying a survivor, the killer sees the Auras of other survivors near those Scourge Hooks, and gets an alert whenever a survivor starts sabotaging a hook.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a way to track survivors during a carry, which is normally a blind moment. The sabotage alert also makes hook rescue attempts easier to anticipate and punish.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if a carry-heavy style fits the killer's play, since the Aura reveal only works while holding a survivor. The Pig teaches it, and it suits any build that wants extra information during its most vulnerable phase.

HeadOn.name: Head On
HeadOn.description: After hiding in a Locker for 3s, fast-exit to stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m, then gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers: After hiding in a Locker for 3s, fast-exit to stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m, then gain Exhausted for 60s.
After hiding in a Locker for 3s, fast-exit to stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m, then gain Exhausted for 50s.
After hiding in a Locker for 3s, fast-exit to stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m, then gain Exhausted for 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor adaptation taught by Jane that lets a locker fast-exit stun the killer for a short moment if they are close by, at the cost of a long Exhausted debuff afterward. The survivor must hide in the locker for a few seconds before the exit is ready.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a locker from a hiding spot into an offensive tool, since a well-timed exit can freeze the killer and create a window to escape or heal. The Exhausted trade-off means the survivor loses speed for a long stretch after using it, so it is a high-risk, high-reward play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when a killer is visibly hunting the same corridor and the survivor is already in a locker, rather than as a first-mover in a chase. The long Exhausted penalty means saving it for a moment where the stun actually creates a real escape window is the way to play it.

Hex_Devour_Hope.name: Hex: Devour Hope
Hex_Devour_Hope.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least 24m away, earn 1 Token, up to 5:
  • 2 Tokens | 10s after hooking a Survivor, gain 3/4/5% Haste for 10s.
  • 3 Tokens | Survivors gain Exposed.
  • 5 Tokens | You can Kill downed Survivors.

Whenever a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least 24m away, earn 1 Token, up to 5:

  • 5 Tokens | You can Kill downed Survivors.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least 24m away, earn 1 Token, up to 5:
  • 2 Tokens | 10s after hooking a Survivor, gain 4% Haste for 10s.
  • 3 Tokens | Survivors gain Exposed.
  • 5 Tokens | You can Kill downed Survivors.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least 24m away, earn 1 Token, up to 5:
  • 2 Tokens | 10s after hooking a Survivor, gain 5% Haste for 10s.
  • 3 Tokens | Survivors gain Exposed.
  • 5 Tokens | You can Kill downed Survivors.

beginner.whatItIs: Earn a Token every time a survivor is unhooked while the killer is far away, up to a cap. At lower thresholds the killer gains a short Haste boost after hooking, at a middle threshold all survivors become Exposed, and at the cap the killer can instantly kill downed survivors.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards the killer for not being at the hook when a rescue happens, turning a normally positive survivor moment into a point source. The top effect is extremely punishing since an instant kill on a downed survivor removes any chance of a follow-up rescue.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The Hag teaches it, and it fits a build that wants to punish rescue attempts and reward hooking pressure. Equip it when the survivor team is rescue-heavy and you want their own unhooking to hand the killer escalating advantages.

Hex_HauntedGround.name: Hex: Haunted Ground
Hex_HauntedGround.description:
When the trial starts, 2 Dull Totems ignite.

When either of those Hex Totems is blessed or cleansed:
  • All Survivors gain Exposed for 40/50/60s.
  • The other Totem is extinguished.
descriptionTiers:

  • All Survivors gain Exposed for 40s.

When the trial starts, 2 Dull Totems ignite.

  • The other Totem is extinguished.

When the trial starts, 2 Dull Totems ignite.

When either of those Hex Totems is blessed or cleansed:
  • All Survivors gain Exposed for 60s.
  • The other Totem is extinguished.

beginner.whatItIs: Dual Dull Totems ignite at trial start, and blessing or cleansing either one makes all survivors Exposed for a long window while also extinguishing the other. The Spirit teaches it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns Totem removal into a double-edged act for the survivor team, since removing one totem reveals everyone and eliminates the second as well. Survivors must weigh the benefit of clearing a Hex against the exposure and the loss of the other totem.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that wants to discourage hasty totem removal and reward patience. It suits a trickery playstyle where the killer wants survivors to second-guess every cleanse.

Hex_HuntressLullaby.name: Hex: Huntress Lullaby
Hex_HuntressLullaby.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, earn 1 Token. For each Token, Basic Skill Check warnings appear later and good success zones are smaller.

While you have 5 Tokens, Basic Skill Check warnings don't appear.

Whenever a Survivor misses a basic Skill Check, they lose 2/4/6% more progress.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, earn 1 Token. For each Token, Basic Skill Check warnings appear later and good success zones are smaller.

While you have 5 Tokens, Basic Skill Check warnings don't appear.

Whenever a Survivor misses a basic Skill Check, they lose 2% more progress.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, earn 1 Token. For each Token, Basic Skill Check warnings appear later and good success zones are smaller.

While you have 5 Tokens, Basic Skill Check warnings don't appear.

Whenever a Survivor misses a basic Skill Check, they lose 4% more progress.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, earn 1 Token. For each Token, Basic Skill Check warnings appear later and good success zones are smaller.

While you have 5 Tokens, Basic Skill Check warnings don't appear.

Whenever a Survivor misses a basic Skill Check, they lose 6% more progress.

beginner.whatItIs: As the killer hooks survivors, Tokens accumulate and each one makes Basic Skill Check warnings appear later and success zones smaller. At the full cap, warnings disappear entirely and missing a basic check costs extra progress. The Huntress teaches it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gradually makes every Skill Check harder for survivors as the trial progresses, so late-game generator repairs and healing become increasingly punishing. The escalating pressure means the survivor team feels the Hex more and more the longer the trial lasts.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a hook-heavy build where the killer regularly cycles survivors through the hook. It rewards a kill-or-hook strategy and punishes survivor teams that lean on multiple rescues to stay alive.

Hex_Ruin.name: Hex: Ruin
Hex_Ruin.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

While a Generator is not being repaired, it regresses at 100/125/150% speed.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

While a Generator is not being repaired, it regresses at 100% speed.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

While a Generator is not being repaired, it regresses at 125% speed.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

While a Generator is not being repaired, it regresses at 150% speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Generators that sit idle without an active repairer regress at an increased speed for as long as the Hex Totem remains. The Hag teaches it, and the Dull Totem it ignites is the source of the effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes survivor teams that stagger their repairs, since every generator that is not actively being worked on keeps losing progress. Survivors must stay at generators or accept the constant bleed, which makes map control and repair planning much harder.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor team splits up and leaves generators unattended between repair bursts. It fits an obstruction build that wants to make map management feel urgent and unforgiving.

Hex_The_Third_Seal.name: Hex: The Third Seal
Hex_The_Third_Seal.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic or special-attack, they gain Blindness.

This applies for up to 2/3/4 Survivors.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic or special-attack, they gain Blindness.

This applies for up to 2 Survivors.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic or special-attack, they gain Blindness.

This applies for up to 3 Survivors.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic or special-attack, they gain Blindness.

This applies for up to 4 Survivors.

beginner.whatItIs: The Hag teaches a killer Hex that blinds survivors whenever they are struck by a basic or special attack. A Dull Totem ignites at the start of the trial to anchor the effect, which can spread to a small group of survivors throughout the match.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes every hit visually disorienting for the survivor, since Blindness scrambles their view and makes vaulting, healing, and repair much harder to perform. Survivors who get hit early and often will struggle to keep up with their tasks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that deals frequent hits and wants each one to carry extra weight. It suits a cruelty-focused playstyle where the goal is to make every interaction with the killer feel costly.

Hex_Thrill_Of_The_Hunt.name: Hex: Thrill of the Hunt
Hex_Thrill_Of_The_Hunt.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

For each Dull and Hex Totem remaining, you have 1 Token.

For each Token, Survivors bless and cleanse totems 8/9/10% slower.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

For each Dull and Hex Totem remaining, you have 1 Token.

For each Token, Survivors bless and cleanse totems 8% slower.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

For each Dull and Hex Totem remaining, you have 1 Token.

For each Token, Survivors bless and cleanse totems 9% slower.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

For each Dull and Hex Totem remaining, you have 1 Token.

For each Token, Survivors bless and cleanse totems 10% slower.

beginner.whatItIs: Every Dull and Hex Totem still standing on the map acts as a Token that slows down the survivor team's blessing and cleansing speed. It is a general Hex available to any killer, not tied to a specific character.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes Totem removal a slower, more vulnerable act for survivors, since each one takes longer to finish. The more totems remain, the stronger the effect, so it rewards the killer for letting totems sit while punishing the team that tries to clear them quickly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a killer wants survivors to struggle with totem cleansing and blessing, since each surviving Dull or Hex Totem adds pressure to those actions. Because no specific character teaches it, it slots into any killer's playstyle that leans on totem control.

HexBloodFavor.name: Hex: Blood Favor
HexBloodFavor.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor, Upright Pallets within 24/28/32m of them are blocked for 15s.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor, Upright Pallets within 24m of them are blocked for 15s.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor, Upright Pallets within 28m of them are blocked for 15s.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever you damage a Survivor, Upright Pallets within 32m of them are blocked for 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: Igniting at trial start, its Dull Totem anchors the perk's chasing effect. Every time the killer damages a survivor, upright pallets near that survivor get blocked for a short period, making vault routes less reliable.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the safety of pallet loops the moment a survivor is hit, since the killer's own damage is what locks the pallets down. Survivors who rely on looping the same tiles will find their routes suddenly unavailable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by a hooded killer and suits a chase-focused build that wants to punish survivors for leaning on pallet-heavy routes. Equip it when the survivor team is visibly looping and you want to collapse their escape options.

HexRetribution.name: Hex: Retribution
HexRetribution.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor starts blessing or cleansing a Totem, they gain Oblivious for 40/50/60s.

Whenever a Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20s.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor starts blessing or cleansing a Totem, they gain Oblivious for 40s.

Whenever a Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20s.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor starts blessing or cleansing a Totem, they gain Oblivious for 50s.

Whenever a Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20s.

When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a Survivor starts blessing or cleansing a Totem, they gain Oblivious for 60s.

Whenever a Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, you see the Auras of all Survivors for 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Hex: Retribution comes from The Deathslinger and lights a Dull Totem the moment a trial opens. Touching any Totem, to bless it or to cleanse it, saddles whoever started the job with Oblivious. Should a Hex Totem go down, every survivor's Aura is exposed for a moment.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes Totem removal twice: first by blinding the survivor who did it, then by revealing the entire team's position. The Oblivious debuff makes the cleanser vulnerable to a follow-up hit, while the Aura reveal lets the killer redirect pressure elsewhere.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor team is stacking on Totem removal and the goal is to make that act feel dangerous. It fits a trickery-focused build that wants both information and punishment from the same survivor action.

HexUndying.name: Hex: Undying
HexUndying.description:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

When another Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, it replaces this one and keeps any Tokens it had.

You see the Auras of Survivors within 2/3/4m of Dull Totems.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, a Dull Totem ignites.

When another Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, it replaces this one and keeps any Tokens it had.

You see the Auras of Survivors within 2m of Dull Totems.

When another Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, it replaces this one and keeps any Tokens it had.

When another Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, it replaces this one and keeps any Tokens it had.

You see the Auras of Survivors within 4m of Dull Totems.

beginner.whatItIs: Its Dull Totem catches the effect of a different Hex Totem the moment that other one is blessed or cleansed elsewhere, carrying over any Tokens it had onto a fresh Dull Totem. The killer also sees the Auras of survivors who stand near Dull Totems.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the reward for removing Hex Totems, since the survivor's effort just resets the totem in place. The Aura feed near Dull Totems also helps the killer find survivors who are loitering or working near totem positions.
beginner.whenToUseIt: A hooded killer teaches it, and it suits a build that wants to frustrate Totem-removal attempts without sacrificing information. Equip it when the survivor team is aggressive about cleansing and you want their effort to feel wasted.

Hope.name: Hope
Hope.description: When all Generators are completed, you gain 3/4/5% Haste.
descriptionTiers: When all Generators are completed, you gain 3% Haste.
When all Generators are completed, you gain 4% Haste.
When all Generators are completed, you gain 5% Haste.

beginner.whatItIs: Once every generator is completed, the survivor gains a small Haste boost for the remainder of the trial. It is a general survivor perk, not tied to a specific character.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes the endgame chase faster for the survivor, which is exactly when the team is most vulnerable after the generator race ends. The speed bump can be the difference between reaching a locker or an exit gate and getting caught in the open.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on any survivor who expects to be in chases after the generators are done, since the late-trial speed boost is its only function. It is a simple, reliable pick that does not compete for Bloodweb space the way a tool-based perk would.

ImAllEars.name: I'm All Ears
ImAllEars.description: Whenever a Survivor fast-enters or fast-exits a Locker, or medium or fast-vaults within 48m of you, you see their Aura for 8s. Cooldown: 60/45/30s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor fast-enters or fast-exits a Locker, or medium or fast-vaults within 48m of you, you see their Aura for 8s. Cooldown: 60s.
Whenever a Survivor fast-enters or fast-exits a Locker, or medium or fast-vaults within 48m of you, you see their Aura for 8s. Cooldown: 45s.
Whenever a Survivor fast-enters or fast-exits a Locker, or medium or fast-vaults within 48m of you, you see their Aura for 8s. Cooldown: 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: I'm All Ears comes from The Ghost Face and punishes careless movement. Rushing into or out of a Locker, or vaulting at medium or fast speed close enough by, lights up that survivor's Aura briefly. A cooldown sits between triggers, so it rewards patience rather than constant pings.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards the killer for being close to active survivor movement, since lockers and fast vaults are the two most common escape tools. The Aura reveal after a vault or locker use gives the killer a brief window to redirect and punish.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that hunts near lockers and vault routes, since the perk only triggers when survivors use those specific actions. It suits an aggressive playstyle that wants to punish escape attempts with immediate positional information.

InfectiousFright.name: Infectious Fright
InfectiousFright.description: Whenever a Survivor is downed, Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and you are alerted for 4/5/6s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor is downed, Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and you are alerted for 4s.
Whenever a Survivor is downed, Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and you are alerted for 5s.
Whenever a Survivor is downed, Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and you are alerted for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: When a survivor goes down, nearby survivors within the terror radius scream and the killer is alerted to their position for a short window. The Plague teaches it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a down event into a tracking ping, since the killer instantly knows where the rescuing or healing survivor is. Survivors who camp near downed allies to prepare a rescue will find their position revealed the moment the down happens.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when catching the scream that fires the instant a survivor hits the floor is what the build needs, since nearby teammates all cry out at once. The Plague teaches it, and it suits a tracking style that closes the distance the moment a survivor is downed.

InnerStrength.name: Inner Strength
InnerStrength.description: Whenever you cleanse a Totem, while injured and not Broken, after hiding in a Locker for 10/9/8s, you become healthy instantly.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you cleanse a Totem, while injured and not Broken, after hiding in a Locker for 10s, you become healthy instantly.
Whenever you cleanse a Totem, while injured and not Broken, after hiding in a Locker for 9s, you become healthy instantly.
Whenever you cleanse a Totem, while injured and not Broken, after hiding in a Locker for 8s, you become healthy instantly.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Nancy that lets an injured survivor heal fully and instantly by hiding in a locker for a few seconds right after cleansing a Totem, as long as they are not affected by the Broken status. It turns a totem cleanse into a self-heal opportunity without needing a Med-Kit or a healing partner.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the need for a med kit or a healing partner, since the survivor can self-heal at a locker after removing a Totem. This makes the survivor much harder to lock down with injuries, since every chase that ends in a locker can reset their health.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who can reach lockers after chases and is comfortable removing Totems as part of their routine. It turns the locker from a hiding spot into a full heal station, which changes how the killer must approach every chase.

Insidious.name: Insidious
Insidious.description: After being idle for 3/2/1s, you gain Undetectable until you act.
descriptionTiers: After being idle for 3s, you gain Undetectable until you act.
After being idle for 2s, you gain Undetectable until you act.
After being idle for 1s, you gain Undetectable until you act.

beginner.whatItIs: Stand still for a short moment and the killer becomes Undetectable until they act again. It is a general killer perk available to every killer, not tied to a specific character.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets the killer reset a chase and hide their position, since Undetectable removes the noise and visual cues that survivors use to track them. A well-timed use can end a chase, let the killer reposition, or set up a scare.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in any build that wants a free stealth reset, since it costs nothing but a brief pause. It is especially useful for killers who want to drop a chase and re-engage from a different angle.

InTheDark.name: Knock Out
InTheDark.description: Whenever a Survivor drops a Pallet, for the next 6s, if they move 6m away from it, they gain 5% Hindered for 3/4/5s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor drops a Pallet, for the next 6s, if they move 6m away from it, they gain 5% Hindered for 3s.
Whenever a Survivor drops a Pallet, for the next 6s, if they move 6m away from it, they gain 5% Hindered for 4s.
Whenever a Survivor drops a Pallet, for the next 6s, if they move 6m away from it, they gain 5% Hindered for 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Dropping a pallet becomes a trap for the survivor who placed it: if they move a short distance away from it, they gain a brief Hindered debuff. The Cannibal teaches it, and the effect only triggers within a few seconds of the drop.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes the most common pallet-loop escape, since the survivor who drops the pallet to block the killer is the one who gets slowed when they move on. It makes the drop-and-run tactic feel riskier and less reliable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a trickery build that wants survivors to second-guess their pallet drop, because sprinting away from a dropped pallet slows them down for a short window. The Cannibal teaches it. It rewards a killer who pressures the drop decision at close range.

Iron_Grasp.name: Iron Grasp
Iron_Grasp.description:
While carrying a Survivor:
  • They wiggle 4/8/12% slower.
  • Their wiggle is 75% weaker.
descriptionTiers:
While carrying a Survivor:

  • Their wiggle is 75% weaker.

  • Their wiggle is 75% weaker.

While carrying a Survivor:
  • They wiggle 12% slower.
  • Their wiggle is 75% weaker.

beginner.whatItIs: While carrying a survivor, their wiggle progress is slower and their wiggle speed is significantly weakened. It is a general perk that every killer can unlock, with no specific character required to teach it.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes hook time feel longer for the survivor, since the usual escape via wiggle is heavily suppressed. Survivors who rely on wiggling out of the hook will find the window much tighter, which gives the killer more room to position at the next hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a build that hooks survivors frequently and wants to minimize the chance of a wiggle-out. It is a straightforward pick for any killer who wants their carries to feel more secure.

Iron_Will.name: Iron Will
Iron_Will.description: While injured and not Exhausted, your Grunts of Pain are 80/90/100% quieter.
descriptionTiers: While injured and not Exhausted, your Grunts of Pain are 80% quieter.
While injured and not Exhausted, your Grunts of Pain are 90% quieter.
While injured and not Exhausted, your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk taught by Jake that makes grunts of pain noticeably quieter while injured, as long as the survivor is not in an Exhausted state. It fits the concealment category and rewards a survivor who stays put after taking a hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Quieter noise means a killer cannot track the group by sound while they huddle behind a generator or work a healing session. It pays off in a concealment build where staying out of a killer earshot is the whole point.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the goal is to stay hidden after a hit and recover near the action instead of sprinting across the map. Jake teaches it, so it fits any survivor slot where noise reduction during recovery is the priority.

Ironmaiden.name: Iron Maiden
Ironmaiden.description:
Whenever a Survivor exits a Locker:
  • They gain Exposed for 30s.
  • They scream, then you are alerted to their location for 4s.


You open Lockers 30/40/50% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Taught by Legion, a killer perk that punishes survivors the moment they exit a locker by giving them a brief Exposed state and forcing a scream that reveals their position. It also speeds up locker opening for the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every locker use becomes a gamble, because the noise and exposed window give the killer a real chance to hit them right after they slip out. Faster locker opening means the killer clears hiding spots quicker when hunting.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if catching survivors at the exact moment they feel safe is the pressure a build wants. Legion teaches it, so it pairs with any killer build that applies pressure around hiding spots.

K22P01.name: Hoarder
K22P01.description:
When the trial starts, 2 more Chests appear.

Whenever a Survivor picks-up an Item or starts unlocking a Chest within 32/48/64m of you, you are alerted.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, 2 more Chests appear.

Whenever a Survivor picks-up an Item or starts unlocking a Chest within 32m of you, you are alerted.

When the trial starts, 2 more Chests appear.

Whenever a Survivor picks-up an Item or starts unlocking a Chest within 48m of you, you are alerted.

When the trial starts, 2 more Chests appear.

Whenever a Survivor picks-up an Item or starts unlocking a Chest within 64m of you, you are alerted.

beginner.whatItIs: A tracking perk taught by The Twins that seeds the trial with extra Chests and sounds an alert whenever a survivor nearby picks up an item or begins cracking open a Chest. Every scavenging action within range becomes a visible event the killer can chase down.
beginner.whyItMatters: The instant alert means no quiet looting near the killer, forcing the group to think about where they loot, not just what. It shifts how a trial plays out by making item pickups a visible commitment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build wants early awareness of where survivors are hunting for items and Chests before committing to a push. The Twins teach it, and it suits a style that makes scavenging feel exposed for the whole group.

K22P02.name: Oppression
K22P02.description: Whenever you damage a Generator, up to 4 other Generators start regressing. Survivors repairing them get a special Skill Check. Cooldown: 45/40/35s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you damage a Generator, up to 4 other Generators start regressing. Survivors repairing them get a special Skill Check. Cooldown: 45s.
Whenever you damage a Generator, up to 4 other Generators start regressing. Survivors repairing them get a special Skill Check. Cooldown: 40s.
Whenever you damage a Generator, up to 4 other Generators start regressing. Survivors repairing them get a special Skill Check. Cooldown: 35s.

beginner.whatItIs: An obstruction perk from The Twins that ripples regression across several other generators whenever one takes damage, and forces survivors at those machines to pass a special Skill Check to keep working. A single strike on one machine sets off a chain reaction the group must scramble to contain.
beginner.whyItMatters: One generator hit can slow several repair teams at once, dragging out the trial and keeping exit gates locked longer. Survivors must decide whether to keep working a regressing generator or abandon it, and either choice costs time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants generator hits to echo broadly and force the group to keep swapping targets. The Twins teach it, and it rewards a style that keeps repair momentum from ever settling.

K22P03.name: Coup de Grâce
K22P03.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 2 Tokens, up to 5.

Whenever you lunge-attack, spend 1 Token to make it 70/75/80% longer.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 2 Tokens, up to 5.

Whenever you lunge-attack, spend 1 Token to make it 70% longer.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 2 Tokens, up to 5.

Whenever you lunge-attack, spend 1 Token to make it 75% longer.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 2 Tokens, up to 5.

Whenever you lunge-attack, spend 1 Token to make it 80% longer.

beginner.whatItIs: A cruelty perk taught by The Twins that banks tokens each time a generator finishes, then burns one to make the next lunge reach further than usual. Survivors who rely on a fast dodge to escape the lunge now find the extended range closes the gap before they can react.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer attack range makes escape-by-distance much harder, which is the usual tactic in a chase. It turns the moment a survivor thinks a gap is enough into a moment where they are still in danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build wants every lunge to land deeper and catch survivors who try to slip away with a quick sidestep. The Twins teach it, and it rewards aggressive pressure that converts close misses into solid connections.

K23P01.name: Starstruck
K23P01.description:
While carrying a Survivor, Survivors within your Terror Radius gain Exposed. This ends 26/28/30s after:
  • They leave your Terror Radius.
  • You drop or Hook the carried Survivor.


Cooldown: 60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Starstruck belongs to The Trickster and marks every survivor inside the Terror Radius with Exposed while the killer holds a carried survivor. The exposure lifts the moment the carried survivor is hooked or set down, or when nearby survivors slip out of range.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes the group for rushing to help a carried teammate, because nearby survivors are exposed while the carry lasts. That discourages the usual intercept and makes the carry phase more controlled for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants survivors who linger near a hook while someone is being carried to reveal their own position. The Trickster teaches it, and it suits a rhythm built around long carries that turn every rescue attempt into a risky call.

K23P02.name: Hex: Crowd Control
K23P02.description:
The first time a Survivor medium or fast-vaults a Window, a Dull Totem ignites.

The last 4/5/6 Windows Survivors medium or fast-vault are blocked.

You basic-vault blocked Windows 15% faster.

You see the Auras of blocked Windows within 24m.

beginner.whatItIs: Hex: Crowd Control is The Trickster's chasing perk that seals off the most recently vaulted windows after the first medium or fast vault in the trial lights a Dull Totem. While the totem stands, the killer moves through those sealed windows with a speed boost and spots their auras from across the map.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stripping away a survivor's favorite vault routes forces longer detours or riskier basic vaults, stretching every chase and making tight loops much harder to sustain. It is a powerful tool for any chase-focused build that wants to control loop geometry.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build wants to shut down the specific windows survivors keep reusing and force them to find new routes mid-chase. The Trickster teaches it, and it rewards a relentless pursuit that starves the group of their preferred loop paths.

K23P03.name: No Way Out

beginner.whatItIs: An obstruction perk from The Trickster that awards a token the first time each survivor is hooked, then converts those tokens into extra lockout time on exit gates once all generators are done. The killer hears an alert the instant a survivor starts prying open a sealed gate.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blocking gates delays the trial end and gives the killer a final window to hook the last survivors, turning the ending into a tense scramble rather than a quick escape. It is a strong way to spike the last moments of a match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build already locks down the endgame and the goal is to stretch that final window even further. Every hook collected earlier in the trial feeds the lockout, so a killer who works steadily from opener to gate sees the most value here. The Trickster teaches it, and the payoff lands the instant a survivor touches the gate wheel after the last generator hums to life.

K24P01.name: Lethal Pursuer
K24P01.description:

Whenever you see a Survivor's Aura for a duration, it is 2s longer.

beginner.whatItIs: Lethal Pursuer is The Nemesis's tracking perk that flashes every survivor's aura on screen at the start of the trial and then stretches that visibility window further each time any aura is spotted from any source. The initial read keeps paying off as the match goes on, rewarding a killer who stays mobile and keeps peeling back new auras.
beginner.whyItMatters: Opening with full visibility lets the killer pick a target and plan a route before the first chase begins. The stacking extension means the perk grows more valuable the longer the trial lasts, since every piece of information feeds the next window.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants the opening seconds to hand over a full map of where the group is and to keep that lead growing with every subsequent glance. The Nemesis teaches it, and it rewards a measured killer who charts routes from the intel gathered in those first moments.

beginner.whatItIs: Hysteria is The Nemesis's trickery perk that slaps Oblivious onto every already-injured survivor the instant a healthy one takes a hit. The effect has a short cooldown before it can trigger again on the next injury.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a moment where a chunk of the group loses part of their normal awareness right when they are most likely to be regrouping around a fresh injury. The perk is strongest right after the first hit, since it catches the whole already-injured half of the team at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants the first clean hit of a chase to blind everyone already injured and open up paths the group thought they had mapped. The Nemesis is behind it, and it rewards a killer who strings early downs into a long stretch of free movement.

K24P03.name: Eruption
K24P03.description:
Whenever you damage a Generator, when you down a Survivor, all Generators damaged this way:

beginner.whatItIs: An obstruction perk from The Nemesis that detonates every generator it previously damaged the moment a survivor is downed, wiping progress and sending those machines into regression. Survivors who are mid-repair at that instant scream aloud and flash their auras for a short stretch.
beginner.whyItMatters: Downing someone becomes a map-wide event that scatters repair teams and gives the killer a brief look at where they worked. It is a powerful combo of chase pressure and generator disruption, since a single down can unravel the group's repair plan.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants a single down to detonate all the progress the group has spread across the map and force a scramble to rebuild. The Nemesis teaches it, and it suits a killer who tracks which machines carry the most work and times the down to hurt the most.

K25P01.name: Deadlock
K25P01.description: Whenever a Generator is completed, the Generator with the most progress is blocked for 15/20/25s.

beginner.whatItIs: Deadlock is The Cenobite's perk that locks down the generator closest to completion each time the group finishes another machine. The constant interruption forces the survivors to abandon their rhythm and scramble to a less-advanced generator, bleeding time from the whole repair pace.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every completed generator immediately locks the next most-advanced one, forcing survivors to scatter and work from lower progress. This stretches the endgame and makes the final stretch of a trial feel longer and more tense.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants every generator finish to trigger a fresh lockout and force the group to reset their priorities. The Cenobite teaches it, and it rewards a killer who prefers dragging out the final stretch over racing to a clean end.

beginner.whatItIs: Hex: Plaything is The Cenobite's perk that brands a survivor with a hex the first time they land on a hook, igniting a Dull Totem that no other survivor can cleanse for a stretch of time right after. The hexed survivor carries Oblivious the whole time the hex is active, and can spot the totem's aura when standing close enough.
beginner.whyItMatters: It locks the group out of removing the negative effect, so the hex persists longer than a normal Dull Totem would. The Oblivious on the hooked survivor adds confusion to the moment after a hook, making it harder for them to react to what happens next.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants each first hook to leave a hex the rest of the group simply cannot scrub off, stretching the penalty well past the rescue moment. The Cenobite is behind it, and it suits a killer who spaces hooks to keep the group impaired for longer stretches.

beginner.whatItIs: Scourge Hook: Gift of Pain is The Cenobite's perk that upgrades a handful of random hooks at the start of the trial. Any survivor rescued from one of those carries Hemorrhage and Mangled, and once healed their repair and healing speed drops until they take their next hit, turning the rescue moment into the start of a fresh penalty stack.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the brief calm after a hook into a window where bleeding, slowed healing, and reduced repair speed all press on the survivor at once. The group loses more than a hooked teammate; they lose time and safety in the seconds following a rescue.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build wants every rescue to hand the freed survivor new debuffs and slow their contribution for the rest of that stretch. The Cenobite teaches it, and it fits a killer who treats each hook placement as the seed of a longer sequence of trouble.

Accumulate enough tokens and the same step-away stretches the blackout dramatically while also flashing the Obsession's aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: Leaving a hook becomes a map-wide generator freeze, so the group loses time whenever the killer repositions. The extended block with the Obsession reveal adds a scouting bonus on top of pure obstruction, making it a strong late-trial tool.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build already chains hooks back to back and wants every step away from a hook to stall generator progress across the whole map. Once tokens stack up, walking away from a hook extends the block dramatically and hands the killer a read on the Obsession's position.

beginner.whatItIs: Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance is The Artist's killer perk that converts several hooks into Scourge Hooks before the trial begins and hands the killer a small pool of tokens to spend. The first time each survivor lands on one of those hooks, a token is consumed and the generator with the highest progress detonates, sheds ground, and starts sliding backward while the survivor still on it screams out their position.
beginner.whyItMatters: It ties hooks directly to generator damage, so every new survivor hooked on a Scourge Hook costs the group real progress. The scream alert means the killer knows exactly where the repair team is, turning a hook into both a damage event and a scouting opportunity.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the kill plan spreads hooks across the map and wants each first hook to punish the generator race. The detonation triggers only once per survivor, so a style that funnels every survivor through a Scourge Hook lands a burst on the generator each time. The Artist teaches it, a fit for a killer who uses hook placement to hit repair progress first.

beginner.whatItIs: Hex: Pentimento is a killer perk from The Artist that reveals cleansed totems and gives the killer the ability to rekindle each one. Each rekindled totem slows the group's healing and repair pace, and the penalty compounds as more totems stay lit simultaneously. Light every totem at the same moment and the entire set locks down.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a way to bring back negative effects the group already removed, so a cleansed Totem is not a permanent fix. The stacking slowdown means the longer the rekindled state lasts, the more it grinds the group's progress down.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it when the build treats totem cleanses as a real threat and wants to weaponize that rhythm against the group. The penalty from rekindled totems compounds, so a killer who holds a tight orbit around totem positions and catches cleanses early stacks the slowdown before the group can finish any other task. The Artist teaches it, suited to a style that turns every cleanse into a chance to re-light the board.

beginner.whatItIs: Scourge Hook: Floods of Rage is a killer perk from The Onryo that marks a few hooks as Scourge Hooks before the trial even begins. beginner.whyItMatters: It gives the killer a peek at where the rest of the group is right after a rescue, a moment of high information value because survivors often scatter in the chaos following a hook. Knowing where everyone is in that window makes it much easier to pick the next target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the build wants each Scourge Hook rescue to yield a burst of positional information. The aura reveal fires the instant a survivor is freed from the hook, so a killer who hooks during a chase and then backs off to reposition gets a clear read on the whole group. The Onryo teaches it, a good match for a killer who reads the hook as an information trigger first.

beginner.whatItIs: Call of Brine belongs to The Onryo and accelerates regression on any generator the killer damages, holding that penalty for a set window. While that window stays active, every clean Skill Check landed on the same machine pings the killer with a position alert, keeping repair pace under constant watch.
beginner.whyItMatters: The alert means the killer knows the exact moment a survivor is making a successful repair push, so they can redirect attention to that generator in time. Combined with the faster regression, a damaged generator becomes a ticking clock the group must race against.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it when the build opens with generator damage and wants a continuous information feed as the group works to finish the machine. The alert fires on each clean Skill Check, so a killer who re-hits the generator to keep the regression window running can watch repair pace tick by tick. The Onryo teaches it, suited to a killer who sees generator damage as the opening move of an information loop.

beginner.whatItIs: Merciless Storm belongs to The Onryo and swaps in harder Skill Checks the first time a generator nears full completion. One missed check or any pause in repair locks that machine for a stretch, stalling the group right as the generator was about to finish.
beginner.whyItMatters: It adds real tension right before a generator is done, because a single missed check can lock the whole generator for a stretch and stall the group right when they are closest to finishing. This is a strong way to spike the endgame and keep the trial alive even when the group is close to done.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build has burned through its blocks and now wants to seize the final stretch of the repair race. The trigger fires once per generator near the finish line, so a killer who has already slowed the group and is watching the final repairer get on a machine is the natural fit. The Onryo teaches it, rewarding a style that controls early tempo and then strikes when the group is closest to completion.

beginner.whyItMatters: It pressures pallet-heavy chases by quietly removing the escape route a survivor leans on during a loop. The effect only arms itself after a hit, so it rewards landing early blows and then cutting off the usual vault away.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when hunting through buildings full of pallets or tight loop corridors and wanting to strip a survivor's favorite escape. It favors a killer who lands the first hit and then controls where the vault leads.

beginner.whyItMatters: It helps with tracking, since survivors who hide in lockers near a cluster become easy to spot for a short window. The catch is the cooldown, so each locker search is a one-shot opportunity rather than something to spam.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a survivor is playing lockers and hiding, and check lockers on purpose to flush their position. It pairs well with a killer who patrols locker-dense corners and wants early information on where the group is hiding.

beginner.whatItIs: It is a killer perk that punishes healing. A survivor mending inside the killer's terror radius suffers a blind and an exhausted state that lingers for a stretch after they stop.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about disrupting the heal that keeps a team alive, because a blinded or exhausted mender slows down and becomes easy to find again. The condition is proximity to the killer, so it only bites when a survivor chooses to heal close to where the danger stands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer is already inside or near a survivor group and wants to pressure any heal attempt. It suits a hunting playstyle that stays close enough to the mender to keep the debuff alive.

K29P01.name: Superior Anatomy
K29P01.description: Whenever a Survivor fast-vaults within 12m of you, the next time you basic-vault a window, it is 30/35/40% faster. Cooldown: 25s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor fast-vaults within 12m of you, the next time you basic-vault a window, it is 30% faster. Cooldown: 25s.

beginner.whatItIs: The killer gains a faster window vault for a short time whenever a survivor fast-vaults nearby, turning the survivor's own movement into the killer's speed boost. It is a killer perk tied to a specific character.
beginner.whyItMatters: It helps with chase pacing, since a killer who mirrors a survivor's vault can close distance and keep pressure on pallets and window loops. The trigger is the survivor's own fast vault, so it rewards staying close rather than hunting blind.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a survivor is vault-heavy and keeps looping windows or pallets. It suits a killer who wants faster recovery after each vault instead of raw chase speed.

K29P02.name: Awakened Awareness
K29P02.description: While carrying a Survivor, within 16/18/20m of you, you see the Auras of other Survivors.

beginner.whatItIs: While the killer is carrying a survivor, the auras of all other survivors appear within a wide radius. The read persists for the full length of the carry, making rescue and healing attempts fully visible.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about information during the carry, since a killer who would otherwise hunt blind can now spot a mending survivor or a hook helper before reaching the area. It turns the carry phase, usually a blind run, into a scouting opportunity.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer likes to carry and wants to keep pressure on the rest of the team while moving a survivor. A hook-heavy playstyle benefits most, since the goal is to keep locating the next target instead of guessing.

K29P03.name: Terminus
K29P03.description:
When all Generators are completed: all injured, downed, and hooked Survivors gain Broken.

When an Exit Gate is opened, this ends after 35/40/45s.
descriptionTiers:

beginner.whatItIs: Once every generator reaches completion, Terminus slaps Broken onto each survivor who is injured, downed, or hooked, draining their stamina. The condition persists until an exit gate is activated and a brief countdown expires.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is an endgame tool, since it punishes any survivor who is still hurt, down, or hooked at the moment the trial flips. It turns the final gate phase into a risk for a wounded team rather than a clean escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer is closing out the trial and wants to punish a team that finished the generators while still injured or hooked. It suits a killer who wants extra pressure exactly when the survivors think the run is over.

K30P01.name: Nowhere to Hide
K30P01.description: Whenever you damage a Generator, for 3/4/5s, you see the Auras of Survivors within 18m of you.

beginner.whyItMatters: It is about tracking, since damaging a generator is something a killer does constantly, so the aura flashes keep coming throughout the trial. It suits a killer who wants steady information instead of a single big reveal.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer is fighting generators and wants constant reads on where survivors are repairing. It pairs well with a playstyle that chases generator damage for information as much as for slowing progress.

K30P02.name: Hex: Face the Darkness
K30P02.description:
Whenever you damage a Survivor, they are hexed and a Dull Totem ignites.

Every 35/30/25s, other Survivors not within your Terror Radius scream, then you see their Auras for 2s.

When the hexed Survivor is downed or becomes healthy, the Hex Totem is extinguished.

beginner.whyItMatters: It feeds tracking, since the recurring screams force survivors to reveal themselves over and over while the hex stays lit. It keeps a killer informed even from a distance, as long as the hexed survivor is neither downed nor fully healed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants ongoing aura information on a spreading survivor group. It suits a hex-focused playstyle that wants to keep the team's positions on display for as long as the hex persists.

K30P03.name: Hubris
K30P03.description: Whenever you are stunned by a Survivor, they gain Exposed for 20/25/30s. Cooldown: 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Hubris punishes the survivor who stuns the killer by marking them Exposed, leaving their aura visible for a sustained stretch. A cooldown separates consecutive stuns, so the exposure refreshes only after a meaningful pause.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about countering defensive play, because a survivor who reaches for a stun or an item to break the chase hands back information. The cooldown means it is a recurring reward rather than a one-time flash.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when survivors keep using stuns, flash, or items to break chases and the killer wants a payoff for it. It suits a killer who expects to get stunned often and wants that moment to work back in their favor.

K31P01.name: Game Afoot
K31P01.description:
While chasing the Obsession, whenever you basic-break Pallets or Breakable Walls, or damage Generators, you gain 7% Haste for 8/9/10s.

Whenever you damage the Survivor with the most chase time with a basic-attack, they become the Obsession.

Hitting the survivor who has accumulated the most chase time with a basic attack also forces the Obsession marker onto them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about chasing, since the more the killer breaks things while in pursuit, the faster it gets for a short window. It rewards a killer who stays glued to one survivor and keeps the pressure on through pallets and generators alike.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants a chase that accelerates with every broken pallet and wall. A relentless pursuer who keeps moving and breaking things rather than resetting to a hook gets the most from it.

K31P02.name: THWACK!
K31P02.description:
When the trial starts, you earn 3 Tokens, up to 3.

Whenever you hook a Survivor, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you break a Pallet or Breakable Wall, spend 1 Token. Then, all Survivors within 36m scream and you see their Auras for 4/5/6s.

beginner.whatItIs: THWACK! stocks a small pool of tokens at trial start and tops one up with every hook, while smashing a pallet or breakable wall consumes a token to make all nearby survivors scream and reveal their auras briefly. The capped pool means each shatter is a deliberate commitment, best spent when the killer wants to flush multiple survivors at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about tracking and area denial at once, since breaking a pallet now has a loud, information-rich payoff that reaches far beyond the tile. It rewards a killer who breaks many pallets, because each one can become a reveal.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants to make pallet breaking part of the hunt rather than just a way to clear a loop. It suits a killer who breaks a lot and wants that action to also flush the rest of the team.

K31P03.name: Leverage
K31P03.description: Whenever a Survivor unhooks another or themselves, they heal 20/25/30% slower for 60s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever a Survivor unhooks another or themselves, they heal 20% slower for 60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Leverage drags down the healing speed of whichever survivor just performed an unhook, whether they freed a downed partner or pulled themselves free. The slow persists long enough to disrupt the rescue chain and force the remaining survivors to reconsider their next target.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about punishing the unhook, which is usually the fastest way to get a teammate back on their feet. The long slowdown keeps the pressure on a team that relies on quick rescues to keep rotating.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when survivors keep unhooking each other and the killer wants those rescues to cost something. A hook-heavy playstyle gets the most, since the unhook then feels slower and riskier for the team.

K32P01.name: Genetic Limits

beginner.whatItIs: Genetic Limits slaps Exhausted onto any survivor the moment they take damage, sapping their sprint stamina for a short window. The effect re-triggers on each new hit, keeping a survivor who gets clipped repeatedly sluggish and unable to break away.
beginner.whyItMatters: It sharpens chasing, since an exhausted survivor cannot keep sprinting and is forced to slow down after every hit. It makes each landed blow a bigger deal by turning it into a stamina problem on top of the injury.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants every hit to also sap a survivor's ability to run. It rewards a killer who lands steady damage, since survivors can no longer rely on pure speed to escape.

beginner.whyItMatters: It is about punishing the response to a down, because the survivors who rush to help are the ones made slower. It turns the natural reaction to a down into a smaller, riskier window for the killer to work with.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants to tax the team's rescue play each time someone goes down. It rewards a killer who downs survivors close to their friends, since those friends then move slower while they commit.

beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants generators to feed its own chase speed and stealth. It rewards a killer who damages generators on purpose, since the payout lands right when the survivors finish them.

beginner.whyItMatters: It builds chasing speed, since every clean hit extends the killer's speed for a short moment and keeps the pressure rolling. The trade is giving up bloodlust, so it suits a killer who would not lean on that state anyway.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer lands basic attacks steadily and wants each one to extend the chase. A consistent-hit playstyle gets the most, since it values that speed over the bloodlust boost.

beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer wants hooks to also locate a distant survivor. It rewards a killer who hooks to create a target and then hunts whoever ran far.

beginner.whyItMatters: It is about countering defensive tools, because a survivor who blinks or stuns the killer hands back a blind of their own. It turns the killer's own stuns into recurring payback for the team.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor team leans heavily on blind and stun effects during chases, so each defensive play costs them a moment of their own vision. It suits a totem-focused build that wants to tax the team ability to interrupt the killer repeatedly.

beginner.whatItIs: Friends 'Til the End shifts the killer hook pressure every time it triggers. Hooking a non-obsession survivor exposes the obsession and briefly reveals their aura, while hooking the obsession transfers it to a screaming teammate. The mechanic keeps the team attention scattered across multiple survivors.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is about controlling the obsession, since hooks keep redirecting the team's focus and flashing the obsession's position. It rewards a killer who wants the obsession to keep changing and the team to keep scrambling.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the team keeps funneling their efforts onto a single survivor, since each hook on that survivor bounces the obsession onto someone else. It suits a killer who wants to force the group to spread their attention and never settle into a predictable focus pattern.

beginner.whyItMatters: The extra speed helps a killer cover ground quickly between generators, making chase pressure feel constant even during map traversal. It rewards a playstyle that keeps the killer moving from one finished machine to the next, since the boost only applies near completed generators. The short fade-out window means the killer should already be moving when the effect drops.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a killer build focuses on map control and constant pressure, since the perk pays off most in a trial where generators finish early and the killer has to cross open ground. It suits a patient killer who chases from a position of speed rather than raw pursuit.

K35P01.name: Unbound

beginner.whatItIs: Unbound turns window vaults into a speed boost for a stretch of time right after a healthy survivor first gets hurt, not for as long as anyone stays hurt, and The Unknown teaches it. Each vault inside that window grants a burst of extra pace, and the window renews whenever another survivor is freshly injured. It rewards a killer who presses the chase hard right after landing the opening hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed from vaulting helps a killer keep up with survivors who loop through windows during a chase. It is most noticeable in chases that wind through tight corridors or window-rich areas, where each vault adds a fresh kick of pace. The condition that a survivor must be injured means the perk sits dormant until the first hit lands.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a killer wants a chase tool that rewards aggressive window play, since the perk only activates after the first injury. It pairs well with a playstyle that loops survivors through tight window areas rather than open ground.

beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a killer wants to vanish after every generator hit and re-appear elsewhere, since the perk rewards a hit-and-run rhythm. It suits a killer who prefers to control the pace of the match by appearing and disappearing around the map.

When the hexed Generator is repaired, the next farthest Generator is hexed.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer hex from The Krasue that ignites a Dull Totem at trial start and marks the most distant Generator as hexed. While a Survivor works that cursed machine long enough, the killer gains Undetectable and their Terror Radius snaps to the Generator. Finishing it passes the curse onward to the next farthest machine.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes early generator progress by hiding the killer from Survivor detection and keeping them locked to one machine, which makes it hard to spread out and repair elsewhere. Once the hexed Generator is finished, the curse moves to the next farthest one, keeping pressure on the survivors' repair plans.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with an opener style where The Krasue lets Survivors work the cursed machine while the killer circles a different part of the map unseen. Commitment to that single Generator opens up the rest of the map, giving the killer time to reposition before re-engaging.

K42P01.name: Turn Back The Clock
K42P01.description: After hooking a Survivor, for the next 40/50/60s, use Active Ability button to make target Generator you can see within 20m explode, lose 10% progress and start regressing.
descriptionTiers: After hooking a Survivor, for the next 40s, use Active Ability button to make target Generator you can see within 20m explode, lose 10% progress and start regressing.
After hooking a Survivor, for the next 50s, use Active Ability button to make target Generator you can see within 20m explode, lose 10% progress and start regressing.
After hooking a Survivor, for the next 60s, use Active Ability button to make target Generator you can see within 20m explode, lose 10% progress and start regressing.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk from The First that hands the killer an active button after each hook, usable to detonate a Generator in sight and force its progress backward into regression. The press window is short, so it must land before time runs out.
beginner.whyItMatters: It hits right after a hook, which is exactly when survivors expect the killer to hook again or chase another target. That unexpected generator damage can erase a large chunk of progress and force survivors to split their attention between rescue and repair.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a build around The First that hooks often, since every hook refreshes the detonation window and opens another chance to claw progress off a mid-completion Generator. A tempo that spreads hooks across the map catches machines at varying stages of completion.

K42P02.name: Secret Project
K42P02.description:
Whenever a totem is blessed or cleansed, a random unblocked Generator is blocked for 20/25/30s.

Whenever 1 or more Generators are blocked, you gain Undetectable for 30s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a totem is blessed or cleansed, a random unblocked Generator is blocked for 20s.

Whenever 1 or more Generators are blocked, you gain Undetectable for 30s.

Whenever a totem is blessed or cleansed, a random unblocked Generator is blocked for 25s.

Whenever 1 or more Generators are blocked, you gain Undetectable for 30s.

Whenever a totem is blessed or cleansed, a random unblocked Generator is blocked for 30s.

Whenever 1 or more Generators are blocked, you gain Undetectable for 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk from The First that blocks a random unblocked Generator the moment a Survivor blesses or cleanses a totem. While any Generator sits locked, the killer holds Undetectable, so a single totem commit can mask a reposition and stall a repair at the same time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns totem interactions, which survivors expect to be positive, into a trap that locks a Generator and hides the killer at the same time. Survivors must weigh the risk of blessing a totem against losing access to a machine and losing their chance to spot the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it alongside The First when survivors lean heavily on totem interactions, since each totem trip hands the killer a locked machine and a stealth window. Spot Survivors walking toward a totem and slip in close while they stay occupied.

K42P03.name: Hex: Hive Mind
K42P03.description:
The first time you hook a Survivor, a Dull Totem ignites.

The Auras of Generators show their progress.

When 1 Generator remains:
  • All Generators explode, lose 6/8/10% progress and start regressing.
  • The Hex Totem is extinguished.
descriptionTiers:

The Auras of Generators show their progress.

When 1 Generator remains:
  • All Generators explode, lose 6% progress and start regressing.
  • The Hex Totem is extinguished.

The first time you hook a Survivor, a Dull Totem ignites.

The Auras of Generators show their progress.

When 1 Generator remains:
  • All Generators explode, lose 8% progress and start regressing.
  • The Hex Totem is extinguished.

The first time you hook a Survivor, a Dull Totem ignites.

The Auras of Generators show their progress.

When 1 Generator remains:
  • All Generators explode, lose 10% progress and start regressing.
  • The Hex Totem is extinguished.

beginner.whatItIs: Taught by The First, Hex: Hive Mind lights a Dull Totem at the first hook and paints live progress onto every Generator Aura. The moment only a single Generator remains, all machines detonate, shed progress, and begin regressing as the hex itself burns out.
beginner.whyItMatters: The progress reveal removes a key piece of information that survivors rely on to plan their repair order. The end-game explosion can undo a lot of work in a single moment, making the last Generator feel much closer and much further at the same time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The Aura reveal and the endgame detonation suit The First well in a tempo where the killer hooks early and reads Generator progress all trial long. Survivors who commit to the final machine get hit by the blast at the worst possible instant, punishing any late-game push hard.

K43P01.name: Hex: Scared to Death
K43P01.description:
After you hook 3 different Survivors, a Dull Totem ignites.

While chasing a Survivor, whenever you basic-break a Pallet, Survivors within 11/12/13m:
  • Scream.
  • Gain 11/12/13% Hindered for 3s.
descriptionTiers:

While chasing a Survivor, whenever you basic-break a Pallet, Survivors within 11m:

While chasing a Survivor, whenever you basic-break a Pallet, Survivors within 12m:

While chasing a Survivor, whenever you basic-break a Pallet, Survivors within 13m:
  • Scream.
  • Gain 13% Hindered for 3s.

beginner.whatItIs: Once The Slasher has hooked enough distinct Survivors, a Dull Totem takes fire and every pallet broken mid-chase thereafter sets nearby Survivors screaming and briefly Hindered. The hex carries this pressure through the rest of the trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a normal pallet break into a crowd-control moment, scattering nearby Survivors and slowing them down at the same time. The setup cost of hooking three different survivors means it comes online late enough that early hooks feel worth the wait.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with a chase rhythm that drives targets through tight, pallet-heavy corridors, because every shattered board sends a scream and a Hindered ripple across nearby Survivors. The more the killer funnels a target back through the same narrow gap, the wider the panic spreads.

K43P02.name: Silent Shadow
K43P02.description:
Whenever you hook a Survivor, you gain Undetectable for 11/12/13s.

When all Generators are completed, you gain Undetectable.
descriptionTiers:

When all Generators are completed, you gain Undetectable.

When all Generators are completed, you gain Undetectable.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk from The Slasher that grants Undetectable to the killer for a short stretch after every hook. Once all Generators are complete, that stealth state locks in for the remainder of the trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The hook-triggered invisibility gives a killer a clean window to reposition, set up the next chase, or sneak to a hook without being tracked. The end-game permanent Undetectable makes it even more valuable in the final phase, where Survivors are searching for the killer to unhook or reach a gate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it alongside The Slasher for a build that hooks repeatedly and needs to slip between encounters without being tracked. In the late game, with every Generator finished, the permanent stealth lets the killer dictate the timing and entry angle of the last pursuit.

K43P03.name: Rampage
K43P03.description:
Whenever you basic-break a Pallet or Breakable Wall, you earn 1 Token, up to 13.

Whenever you are blinded or Pallet-stunned, for the next 13s you gain 1% Haste for each Token. Cooldown: 30/25/20.
descriptionTiers:

Whenever you are blinded or Pallet-stunned, for the next 13s you gain 1% Haste for each Token. Cooldown: 30.

Whenever you are blinded or Pallet-stunned, for the next 13s you gain 1% Haste for each Token. Cooldown: 25.

Whenever you basic-break a Pallet or Breakable Wall, you earn 1 Token, up to 13.

Whenever you are blinded or Pallet-stunned, for the next 13s you gain 1% Haste for each Token. Cooldown: 20.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk from The Slasher that banks a Token each time the killer basic-breaks a Pallet or Breakable Wall, capped at a set maximum. Suffering a blind or Pallet-stun then converts the stored Tokens into a burst of Haste, with a cooldown gating the next conversion.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the punishment of a pallet stun or blind into a speed advantage, so the very thing meant to escape the killer instead makes the killer faster. The longer the chase before the stun, the more Tokens are banked, meaning a well-looped Survivor can hand the killer a large Haste burst.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It rewards a chase rhythm that already shatters plenty of Pallets and Breakable Walls, because every break feeds the Token stack. The real payoff arrives in long chases where a large stack is sitting when a flash or Pallet-stun finally lands.

K44P01.name: Celestial Witness
K44P01.description: Every 30s, if the Obsession is at least 40m away from you, you see their Aura for 2/2.5/3s. Otherwise, the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession.
descriptionTiers: Every 30s, if the Obsession is at least 40m away from you, you see their Aura for 2s. Otherwise, the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession.
Every 30s, if the Obsession is at least 40m away from you, you see their Aura for 2.5s. Otherwise, the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession.
Every 30s, if the Obsession is at least 40m away from you, you see their Aura for 3s. Otherwise, the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: The Judgment's perk that periodically reveals the Obsession's Aura when that Survivor sits far enough away to pose a tracking problem. Should the marked Survivor already be close, the designation reassigns itself to whichever other Survivor stands farthest from the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: It keeps the killer's target locked onto a Survivor who is trying to hide at range, which is the classic survival strategy of staying away from the action. The reassignment mechanic means a Survivor who runs far from the killer will keep attracting attention rather than finding safety in distance.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it alongside The Judgment when Survivors camp at range and the Obsession marker becomes the main tracking tool. A stalking rhythm that follows the periodic pings across the map works well here, since it removes reliance on last-seen memory.

K44P02.name: Hex: Under Your Thumb
K44P02.description:
The first time a Survivor gains a Hook State, a Dull Totem ignites.

Whenever a running Survivor gains Haste within 32m of you, you are alerted.

Running Survivors cannot gain more than 25/20/15% Haste at a time.
descriptionTiers:

Running Survivors cannot gain more than 25% Haste at a time.

beginner.whatItIs: Ignites a Dull Totem at the trial's first hook, after which The Judgment is alerted whenever a running Survivor nearby picks up Haste. Any speed boost those Survivors gain is also clamped below its normal ceiling.
beginner.whyItMatters: It directly counters chase-survival tools by limiting how fast a Survivor can run, and the alert lets the killer react to speed bursts in real time. Together those effects make it much harder for Survivors to escape a chase with a single speed item.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the survivor team piles on multiple Haste sources, because both the alert and the cap bite harder in that setup. Wide-open chases see the biggest effect, since without the cap a speed burst would let a Survivor break free in an instant.

K44P03.name: Lay Waste
K44P03.description: Whenever you damage a Generator, for each Charge it has, it regresses 2% faster. Cooldown: 55/50/45s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you damage a Generator, for each Charge it has, it regresses 2% faster. Cooldown: 55s.
Whenever you damage a Generator, for each Charge it has, it regresses 2% faster. Cooldown: 50s.
Whenever you damage a Generator, for each Charge it has, it regresses 2% faster. Cooldown: 45s.

beginner.whatItIs: Damaging a Generator while Lay Waste is active makes it regress faster, with the added rate scaling to how many Charges the machine already holds. A cooldown gates reactivation so it does not fire on every single hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It amplifies the pain of a generator hit by making the regression hit harder on charged machines, which are the ones survivors care about most. A single well-timed hit on a high-charge Generator can erase a large amount of progress that would take a long time to rebuild.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it alongside The Judgment when the plan is to chip away at charged Generators over time rather than contesting one repair sprint. Spreading damage across multiple machines suits this approach well, since the regression penalty deepens as the machine's progress grows.

Kindred.name: Kindred
Kindred.description:
While you are hooked, all Survivors see each others' Auras. While the Killer is within 8/12/16m, all Survivors sees the Killer's Aura.

While another Survivor is hooked, you see the Auras of other Survivors. While the Killer is within 8/12/16m of the hooked Survivor, you see the Killer's Aura.
descriptionTiers:
While you are hooked, all Survivors see each others' Auras. While the Killer is within 8m, all Survivors sees the Killer's Aura.

While another Survivor is hooked, you see the Auras of other Survivors. While the Killer is within 8m of the hooked Survivor, you see the Killer's Aura.

While you are hooked, all Survivors see each others' Auras. While the Killer is within 12m, all Survivors sees the Killer's Aura.

While another Survivor is hooked, you see the Auras of other Survivors. While the Killer is within 12m of the hooked Survivor, you see the Killer's Aura.

While you are hooked, all Survivors see each others' Auras. While the Killer is within 16m, all Survivors sees the Killer's Aura.

While another Survivor is hooked, you see the Auras of other Survivors. While the Killer is within 16m of the hooked Survivor, you see the Killer's Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Any survivor can unlock Kindred, a general perception perk that reveals the Auras of all other Survivors while one is hooked and shows the killer's Aura to everyone when the killer closes the distance. It requires no setup and is available to every character in the roster.
beginner.whyItMatters: It solves the information blackout that happens during a hook, when the hooked Survivor cannot see anything and teammates cannot tell where the killer is standing. Knowing where the killer is lets the remaining Survivors choose a rescue timing or a safe unhook approach.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on any survivor build that wants better awareness during hooks, since it requires no character and no setup. It is especially valuable in games where the killer hooks early and often, because each hook becomes a moment of shared information for the whole team.

Leader.name: Leader
Leader.description:
Within 10m of you, other Survivors:
  • Cleanse Totems 20/25/30% faster.
  • Heal 20/25/30% faster.
  • Open Exit Gates 20/25/30% faster.
  • Sabotage Hooks 20/25/30% faster.
  • Unhook Survivors 20/25/30% faster.
  • Unlock Chests 20/25/30% faster.


After they leave your range, this ends after 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Dwight's support perk that speeds up nearby Survivors' totem cleansing, healing, gate opening, hook sabotage, unhooking, and chest unlocking while they are in range. The bonus persists briefly after a teammate leaves the radius, so the speed boost carries a little distance.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns one survivor into a mobile support hub, making every rescue, heal, or gate-open noticeably faster when teammates work near that survivor. The lingering bonus after a teammate steps out of range means the perk keeps paying off for a short while even during movement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Dwight in a coordinated team where Survivors cluster around tasks. It shines in games with multiple hooks to sabotage or totems to cleanse, since every one of those actions gets a speed boost while happening close by.

LeftBehind.name: Left Behind
LeftBehind.description: When all other Survivors are dead, while within 24/28/32m of the Hatch, you see its Aura.
descriptionTiers: When all other Survivors are dead, while within 24m of the Hatch, you see its Aura.
