beginner.whatItIs: Bill's last-survivor perk that reveals the Hatch's Aura when all other Survivors are dead and the carrier is within a certain range. It activates only in the solo phase, making it a pure end-game tool.
beginner.whyItMatters: In the most desperate moment of a trial, when a survivor is alone and the killer is hunting, knowing where the Hatch is without searching saves precious time and reduces the risk of being caught out in the open. It turns the final escape into a straight run instead of a blind search.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when playing Bill and wanting a safety net for solo survival. It is the natural choice for a survivor who accepts the possibility of being the last one standing, since the payoff arrives exactly when it is needed most.

Lightborn.name: Lightborn
Lightborn.description:
Whenever a Survivor attempts to blind you, you see their Aura for 6/8/10s.

You cannot be blinded.

beginner.whatItIs: An enhancement from HillBilly that makes the killer immune to blinding and reveals the Aura of any Survivor who attempts a blind. The reveal lasts for a short period after each failed blind attempt.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes an entire escape tool from the Survivor's kit, since blinding was a key way to break a chase. The Aura reveal on top means that every failed blind attempt actually makes the Survivor easier to find, turning their escape attempt into a gift.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing HillBilly and wanting to completely neutralize blind-based escapes. It fits a chase-heavy build that does not want any random chance to interrupt a pursuit, and it pairs well with any killer strategy that relies on sustained pursuit.

Lightweight.name: Lightweight
Lightweight.description: Your Scratch Marks disappear 3/4/5s faster and appear more spread out.
descriptionTiers: Your Scratch Marks disappear 3s faster and appear more spread out.

beginner.whatItIs: Lightweight is a general survivor perk, meaning any character can unlock it from the Bloodweb. While it is active, Scratch Marks fade away sooner and spread further apart across the ground, thinning the trail left behind during sprints and vaults.
beginner.whyItMatters: Both effects make it harder for a killer to track a Survivor's recent path, since the marks vanish sooner and do not form a tight trail. In a chase or a close pursuit, that extra noise in the trail can be the difference between being found and slipping away.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on any survivor who covers a lot of ground between objectives, because the faster-fading and wider-spaced Scratch Marks leave less of a trail behind. It suits a stealthy, far-from-the-action playstyle where not leaving a clear path for the killer to follow is the whole point.

Lithe.name: Lithe

Whenever you medium or fast-vault:

beginner.whatItIs: Feng's vault perk that grants a short Haste burst after a medium or fast vault, at the cost of a long Exhausted period afterward. The speed boost is brief but can cover a critical gap in a chase.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed burst from a vault can carry a Survivor past a killer's reach in a critical moment, such as escaping a pallet or crossing open ground. The long Exhausted downside means it is a one-time tool rather than something to rely on repeatedly, so timing the vault matters a lot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Feng and building around vault-based escapes. It is best used in a chase where a well-timed vault through a window or over a pallet creates the gap needed to break the killer's line of sight.

LuckyBreak.name: Lucky Break
LuckyBreak.description:
While injured, for up to 40/50/60s:

beginner.whatItIs: Yui's concealment perk that, while injured, leaves no Pools of Blood and no Scratch Marks for a duration that recharges with each second spent healing another Survivor. The concealment only applies while the survivor is injured.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the two most common ways a killer tracks an injured Survivor, making it much harder to find someone who is hiding after a hit. The healing recharge means that a survivor who keeps helping teammates effectively keeps the concealment active almost indefinitely.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when playing Yui and wanting to stay hidden while injured. It pairs naturally with a healer playstyle, since the more time spent patching up teammates, the longer the trail-suppression lasts.

MadGrit.name: Mad Grit
MadGrit.description:
While carrying a Survivor:

beginner.whatItIs: Legion's carry perk that shortens the cooldown after a missed swing while carrying a Survivor and locks the carried Survivor's wiggle progress for a brief moment after each hit. Both effects only apply while a Survivor is being carried.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes the carrying phase much more forgiving, since a missed swing no longer creates a long vulnerability window. The wiggle lock on the carried Survivor punishes any attempt to wiggle free, making the carry feel much more secure for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Legion and wanting to dominate the carry phase. It suits a build that hooks Survivors frequently and wants to minimize the risk of dropping a carried target mid-carry.

MakeYourChoice.name: Make your Choice
MakeYourChoice.description:
Whenever a Survivor unhooks another or themselves while you are at least 32m away:
  • They scream.

Cooldown: 40/50/60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Make your Choice is a killer perk taught by Pig that punishes unhooking done from a distance. When a survivor frees themselves or a teammate far away from the killer, they are forced to scream and become Exposed for a stretch of time, and a cooldown between activations keeps it from firing on the very next unhook.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes the classic unhook-from-far-away strategy by revealing the unhooking Survivor's position and making them vulnerable to a chase for an extended period. The long Exposed window means a Survivor who tries to unhook from safety is actually placing themselves in danger.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when running Pig and wanting to stop Survivors from unhooking without consequence. It is especially effective in a game where the killer is playing far from the hooks, since every remote unhook becomes a free chase.

Mindbreaker.name: Mindbreaker

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk taught by the Demogorgon that blinds survivors and drains their stamina while they work at a generator. The debuffs linger for a short moment after they step away, punishing quick retreats.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the core survivor activity into a punishing risk, since survivors feel pressure to abandon their repair station the moment the killer shows up. The lingering effect means they cannot simply step away and immediately heal or vault; they are still slowed and disoriented for a short moment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if chasing and pressure around generators is the feel you want, and it is taught by Demogorgon. It rewards a killer who already knows how to commit to one target and make them pay for every second spent on a generator panel.

MonitorAndAbuse.name: Monitor & Abuse
MonitorAndAbuse.description:
While chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 5/10/15% bigger.

While not chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 15/20/25% smaller.
descriptionTiers:
While chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 5% bigger.

While not chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 15% smaller.

While chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 10% bigger.

While not chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 20% smaller.

While chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 15% bigger.

While not chasing a Survivor, your Terror Radius is 25% smaller.

beginner.whatItIs: It is a killer perk assigned to one character that widens the Terror Radius during a chase and shrinks it while roaming between targets. The detection footprint shifts depending on whether the killer is actively pursuing someone.
beginner.whyItMatters: A larger radius during chases means survivors who vault or pause near the killer get caught earlier than expected, while a smaller idle radius lets the killer move through fog or corridors with less accidental detection. The swing between the two states makes it harder for survivors to predict when they are truly safe.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It suits a killer who plays aggressively in chases and wants that extra reach around pallets and windows. It is tied to one specific killer rather than being a general unlock, so equip it on that character when you want every chase to feel slightly more inescapable.

Monstrous_Shrine.name: Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine
Monstrous_Shrine.description:
When the trial starts:
  • 4 random Hooks become Scourge Hooks.
  • The Basement Hooks become Scourge Hooks.


While you are at least 24m away from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, they are sacrificed 10/15/20% faster.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts:
  • 4 random Hooks become Scourge Hooks.
  • The Basement Hooks become Scourge Hooks.


While you are at least 24m away from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, they are sacrificed 10% faster.

When the trial starts:
  • 4 random Hooks become Scourge Hooks.
  • The Basement Hooks become Scourge Hooks.


While you are at least 24m away from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, they are sacrificed 15% faster.

When the trial starts:
  • 4 random Hooks become Scourge Hooks.
  • The Basement Hooks become Scourge Hooks.


While you are at least 24m away from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, they are sacrificed 20% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A general killer unlock that converts a handful of hooks into Scourge Hooks the moment the trial begins, including every hook in the basement. Survivors hanging on those hooks lose health faster while the killer stays at a distance from them.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pressures survivors to unhook their teammates quickly, because leaving someone on a Scourge Hook means they are consumed faster than normal. The distance condition means the killer does not have to camp the hook; they can push the game elsewhere while the sacrifice clock runs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it whenever a hook-heavy strategy feels right, since it is available to any killer without needing a specific character. It pairs well with a killer who likes to chase survivors toward hooks and then step back to let the game punish hesitation.

Nemesis.name: Nemesis
Nemesis.description:
Whenever a Survivor blinds you, Locker-stuns or Pallet-stuns you, they become the Obsession.

Whenever a Survivor becomes the Obsession:
  • They gain Oblivious for 40/50/60s.
  • You see their Aura for 8s.

Whenever a Survivor becomes the Obsession:

  • You see their Aura for 8s.

Whenever a Survivor blinds you, Locker-stuns or Pallet-stuns you, they become the Obsession.

Whenever a Survivor becomes the Obsession:

  • You see their Aura for 8s.

Whenever a Survivor blinds you, Locker-stuns or Pallet-stuns you, they become the Obsession.

Whenever a Survivor becomes the Obsession:

  • You see their Aura for 8s.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk taught by the Oni that marks a survivor as the Obsession the instant they blind, locker-stun, or pallet-stun the killer. The marked survivor becomes Oblivious for a sustained stretch while the killer briefly catches a glimpse of their aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: Survivors who rely on blinds or pallet stuns to escape or reposition suddenly pay a heavy price for those actions, since the Oblivious window forces them to fumble through the rest of the map. The brief aura reveal also lets the killer find the marked survivor even after losing track in fog or through walls.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on Oni when playing a hunt that rewards punishing cleverness, because it turns every defensive trick a survivor pulls into a signal that they are now the target. It fits a killer who wants to make survivors think twice before reaching for a blind or a pallet swing.

No_One_Escapes_Death.name: Hex: No One Escapes Death
No_One_Escapes_Death.description:
When all Generators are completed, a Dull Totem ignites:
  • Survivors gain Exposed.
  • You gain 2/3/4% Haste.


Within 4m, Survivors see the Hex Totem's Aura, expanding to 24m over 30s.

When all Generators are completed, a Dull Totem ignites:
  • Survivors gain Exposed.
  • You gain 2% Haste.


Within 4m, Survivors see the Hex Totem's Aura, expanding to 24m over 30s.

When all Generators are completed, a Dull Totem ignites:
  • Survivors gain Exposed.
  • You gain 3% Haste.


Within 4m, Survivors see the Hex Totem's Aura, expanding to 24m over 30s.

When all Generators are completed, a Dull Totem ignites:
  • Survivors gain Exposed.
  • You gain 4% Haste.


Within 4m, Survivors see the Hex Totem's Aura, expanding to 24m over 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: General killer unlock that ignites a Dull Totem the moment every generator is complete, marking each survivor as Exposed and granting the killer a speed bonus. Survivors in range can perceive the Hex Totem's aura, and that visible radius keeps widening over time.
beginner.whyItMatters: It extends the killer's advantage into the endgame, where survivors are typically focused on unlocking the exit gates. The speed bonus keeps up chase pressure even after generators stop being the central activity, and the Exposed state makes it harder for survivors to hide or heal safely.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer's playstyle already pushes hard in the late game, since the perk only activates after all generators are complete. It is available to any killer, so pair it with builds that want to keep the endgame feeling dangerous rather than letting survivors breathe during the exit phase.

No_One_Left_Behind.name: No One Left Behind
No_One_Left_Behind.description:
When all Generators are completed:
  • You heal 50/75/100% faster.
  • You unhook other Survivors 50/75/100% faster.
  • Whenever you unhook a Survivor, they gain 10% more Haste.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.
descriptionTiers:
When all Generators are completed:
  • You heal 50% faster.
  • You unhook other Survivors 50% faster.
  • Whenever you unhook a Survivor, they gain 10% more Haste.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.

When all Generators are completed:
  • You heal 75% faster.
  • You unhook other Survivors 75% faster.
  • Whenever you unhook a Survivor, they gain 10% more Haste.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.

When all Generators are completed:
  • You heal 100% faster.
  • You unhook other Survivors 100% faster.
  • Whenever you unhook a Survivor, they gain 10% more Haste.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.

beginner.whatItIs: General survivor unlock that, once every generator is finished, accelerates both healing and unhooking for the carrier while granting each rescued survivor a burst of Haste. The survivor wearing it also picks up the auras of every other survivor for the rest of the trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The endgame becomes faster and more coordinated, since a team can cycle hooks and heals without the usual long waits. The revealed survivor auras remove the guesswork of finding downed teammates near exit gates, and the speed boost helps the freshly unhooked survivor escape the killer's reach.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team composition already has strong endgame healing or unhooking, since the perk multiplies what those roles already do. It is a general survivor unlock, so any survivor can carry it, and it shines most when two or three survivors are clustered near the gates.

NoMither.name: No Mither
NoMither.description:
When the trial starts, you become injured, then:
  • You gain Broken.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 15/20/25% faster.
  • You can fully recover.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, you become injured, then:
  • You gain Broken.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 15% faster.
  • You can fully recover.

When the trial starts, you become injured, then:
  • You gain Broken.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 20% faster.
  • You can fully recover.

When the trial starts, you become injured, then:
  • You gain Broken.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 25% faster.
  • You can fully recover.

beginner.whatItIs: David King's survivor perk starts the trial with the wearer already hurt and carrying the Broken condition. In exchange, pain sounds are fully silenced, no blood trail is left behind, and recovery from a downed state happens faster than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: The quieter grunts and absence of blood trails make the survivor far harder to track through dark areas or after a chase ends. Starting injured means the first real hit sends them down quickly, so the perk rewards a survivor who can avoid being caught rather than relying on a full health bar.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the plan leans on careful, quiet generator work rather than aggressive healing or long chases, since David King teaches this perk. It suits facing a killer who tracks by blood trails or pain sounds, since both of those tools are weakened here.

NurseCalling.name: A Nurse's Calling
NurseCalling.description: Within 28/30/32m of Survivors who are healing or being healed, you see their Auras.
descriptionTiers: Within 28m of Survivors who are healing or being healed, you see their Auras.
Within 30m of Survivors who are healing or being healed, you see their Auras.
Within 32m of Survivors who are healing or being healed, you see their Auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk taught by the Nurse that reveals the auras of any survivor who is healing or being healed within a wide radius. Every medical interaction becomes a visible beacon that the killer can spot from a distance.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the uncertainty of where survivors are regrouping, since the moment someone starts a heal the killer gets a direct line to them. The effect is especially disruptive when survivors try to heal in the open between generator runs or while waiting near a hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by Nurse and suits a killer who likes to shut down healing rather than just chase. Bring it when the opposing survivors are known for aggressive unhook-then-heal loops, because it turns their safest moment into the most visible one.

ObjectOfObsession.name: Object of Obsession
ObjectOfObsession.description:
While you are the Obsession, every 30s, the Killer sees your Aura for 3s.

While the Killer sees your Aura:
  • You see their Aura.
  • You cleanse totems 2/4/6% faster.
  • You heal 2/4/6% faster.
  • You repair 2/4/6% faster.


When the trial starts, you are more likely to be the Obsession.
descriptionTiers:
While you are the Obsession, every 30s, the Killer sees your Aura for 3s.

  • You repair 2% faster.

While you are the Obsession, every 30s, the Killer sees your Aura for 3s.

While the Killer sees your Aura:

  • You heal 6% faster.
  • You repair 6% faster.


When the trial starts, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk taught by Laurie that periodically flashes the wearer's aura to the killer while they hold the Obsession title. During each flash the survivor spots the killer's aura and works noticeably faster on totems, healing, and repairs, with a raised chance of becoming the Obsession when the trial begins.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades a small amount of safety for a broad productivity boost, since the survivor is doing more work per second across every activity they touch. The mutual aura visibility means the survivor always knows where the killer is while they are the marked target, which reduces the fear of being caught mid-repair.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by Laurie and suits a survivor who wants to be the one doing the most work in a trial. Equip it when the team needs a dedicated generator grinder or totem cleaner who does not mind being the killer's primary focus.

OffTheRecord.name: Off the Record
OffTheRecord.description:
Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 30/35/40s:
  • You gain Endurance.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 30s:

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 35s:
  • You gain Endurance.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 40s:
  • You gain Endurance.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 100% quieter.
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk taught by Zarina that triggers on every unhook before the final generator is complete, granting Endurance, silencing pain grunts, and hiding the survivor's aura from the killer for a set window. Each new rescue refreshes the protection, making repeated hooks especially valuable.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Endurance means the survivor can survive a chase that would normally end with a hit, and the quiet plus invisible state makes them extremely hard to find after they break free from the hook. It is a powerful reset tool for a team that gets hooked early and often.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by Zarina and fits a survivor who expects to be hooked at least once per trial. Bring it when the killer is aggressive on hooks, since the post-unhook window turns a usually vulnerable moment into a chance to slip away and regroup.

Open_Handed.name: Open-Handed
Open_Handed.description: All Survivors see Auras that have a range from 8/12/16m farther.
descriptionTiers: All Survivors see Auras that have a range from 8m farther.
All Survivors see Auras that have a range from 12m farther.
All Survivors see Auras that have a range from 16m farther.

beginner.whatItIs: Ace teaches a survivor perk that widens the aura-detection range for every survivor in the trial. Each teammate picks up on auras from further away than usual, improving overall map awareness without any active input.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every survivor benefits, so the team collectively has better awareness of generators, totems, chest locations, and the killer's position. It turns a group of individually average survivors into a team that simply has more information at all times.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who wants to contribute to the whole team rather than just their own survival, since the bonus is shared equally across all four. It is taught by Ace and works well in any composition that already has a reason to see farther.

OverwhelmingPresence.name: Overwhelming Presence
OverwhelmingPresence.description:
Whenever a Survivor uses an item within 32m of you, they gain Exhausted for 15s.

Whenever a Survivor within 32m of you gains Exhausted, you see the closest Exhausted Survivor's Aura for 2/3/4s. Cooldown: 25s.

beginner.whatItIs: Overwhelming Presence, a killer perk from The Doctor, causes survivors to gain Exhausted the moment they use an item while close to the killer. The instant one of those survivors already carries the Exhausted state, the killer catches a brief glimpse of their aura. A short internal cooldown limits how often that glimpse can fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes item use a risky act in the killer's neighborhood, since popping a gas trap or using an item can expose a survivor's position. The Exhausted trigger also means that natural stamina loss from chases can reveal a survivor to the killer if they are close enough.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is tied to one specific killer and suits a pressure playstyle that wants survivors to think twice before using items near the action. Equip it when the killer's chase already ends with survivors fleeing on low stamina, because the aura reveal punishes exactly that moment.

Pharmacy.name: Pharmacy
Pharmacy.description:
Whenever you unlock a Chest, it will contain a rare Med-Kit.

You unlock Chests 75/100/125% faster.

The range at which the Killer hears you unlocking Chests is 12m shorter.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you unlock a Chest, it will contain a rare Med-Kit.

beginner.whatItIs: Quentin teaches a survivor perk that guarantees a rare Med-Kit inside every Chest in the trial. Unlocking a Chest is faster than normal, and the radius from which the killer hears the lock being picked is reduced, so the opener enjoys a quieter moment to finish.
beginner.whyItMatters: It guarantees a steady supply of strong healing items, which keeps the team's health pool topped up throughout the trial. The quieter unlock range means the survivor can open chests even when the killer is closer than usual without giving away their exact position as loudly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by Quentin and suits a survivor who acts as the team's medic and wants to minimize downtime between heals. Bring it when the trial map has enough chests to justify the investment, and when the killer is not a heavy hook threat that would waste the Med-Kits.

Play_With_Your_Food.name: Play With Your Food
Play_With_Your_Food.description:
Whenever you stop chasing the Obsession, you earn 1 Token, up to 3. Cooldown: 10s.


For each Token, gain 3/4/5% Haste.


Whenever you attack, lose 1 Token.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk taught by the Shape that awards a Token each time the Obsession chase ends, capped at a small maximum. Every Token contributes a modest Haste bonus, and landing an attack burns one away.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards a chase style that involves repeated starts and stops, since the killer builds up speed by breaking and resuming pursuit. The speed bonus makes each subsequent chase slightly faster, creating a rhythm where the killer feels progressively more dangerous within a single trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It is taught by Shape and suits a killer who plays a cat-and-mouse game with the Obsession rather than a pure chase. Equip it when the killer's power naturally creates situations where chases end and restart, since the tokens accumulate in those gaps.

Plunderers_Instinct.name: Plunderer's Instinct
Plunderers_Instinct.description:
Within 32/48/64m of locked Chests and dropped items, you see their Auras.


Whenever you unlock a Chest, you are 50% more likely to find an item of higher rarity.
descriptionTiers:
Within 32m of locked Chests and dropped items, you see their Auras.

Within 64m of locked Chests and dropped items, you see their Auras.

beginner.whatItIs: Available to every survivor, it reveals the Auras of locked Chests and dropped items from a generous distance. Each unlocked Chest also carries a better chance of yielding a higher-rarity item.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the wasted running to empty chests and helps the survivor find useful items without guessing. The improved chest odds mean the survivor is more likely to pull a strong item early, which can define their playstyle for the rest of the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: It guides a survivor's item-hunting toward the right Chests faster, making it a natural fit for builds that lean on scavenged gear. Any character can carry it, so pair it with a survivor who already plans to open many Chests in a trial.

Poised.name: Poised
Poised.description:
The first time you start repairing each Generator, you see the Killer's Aura for 8s.


Whenever a Generator is completed, you leave no Scratch Marks for 20/25/30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Jane Romero teaches a survivor perk that reveals the killer's aura the first time a repair begins at each generator. After a generator is finished, it suppresses Scratch Marks for a stretch, letting you slip between objectives without leaving a trail.
beginner.whyItMatters: The initial aura reveal helps a survivor gauge the killer's approach before committing to a repair, reducing the chance of being caught flat-footed. The scratch-mark silence after a completed generator lets the survivor move around the map without giving the killer a visual trail.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Jane teaches the perk, so equip it on a build that favors careful Generator work over aggressive chases. It rewards a survivor who moves deliberately between objectives, since the scratch-mark silence after each completed Generator keeps the trail cold.

pop_goes_the_weasel.name: Pop Goes the Weasel
pop_goes_the_weasel.description: Whenever you hook a Survivor, for the next 35/40/45s, when you damage a Generator, it explodes and loses 15% more progress.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you hook a Survivor, for the next 35s, when you damage a Generator, it explodes and loses 15% more progress.
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for the next 40s, when you damage a Generator, it explodes and loses 15% more progress.
Whenever you hook a Survivor, for the next 45s, when you damage a Generator, it explodes and loses 15% more progress.

beginner.whatItIs: A killer perk taught by the Clown that activates after hooking a Survivor. For a window of time afterward, any damage dealt to a Generator makes it explode and lose extra progress beyond the normal amount.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes aggressive generator play during the window that follows each hook, letting a killer interrupt a repair that would otherwise finish. It rewards a playstyle that alternates between hooking and damaging generators rather than chasing a Survivor across the board.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if you play the Clown and want extra pressure on repairs right after securing a hook. It fits a loop of hooking a Survivor, then swinging back to hit a Generator while the window is open, since the bonus only lasts for a limited stretch after the hook lands.

Predator.name: Predator
Predator.description: When you stop chasing a Survivor, you see their Aura for 4s. Cooldown: 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers: When you stop chasing a Survivor, you see their Aura for 4s. Cooldown: 60s.
When you stop chasing a Survivor, you see their Aura for 4s. Cooldown: 50s.
When you stop chasing a Survivor, you see their Aura for 4s. Cooldown: 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: The Wraith's killer perk briefly reveals a survivor's aura the moment a chase breaks off. A cooldown separates each use, so it cannot fire after every single encounter.
beginner.whyItMatters: It closes the information gap in the seconds after a chase, when survivors typically try to slip away and regroup. The survivor does not get a clean reset; the killer still has a short window to re-engage or redirect toward another target.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on The Wraith when the plan is to keep pressure on even after a chase fails. The brief aura reveal punishes a survivor who tries to break line of sight and quietly slip away.

Premonition.name: Premonition
Premonition.description: While the Killer is within 36m of you and inside a 45 degree cone, whenever you look at them, you hear a sound cue. Cooldown: 60/45/30s.
descriptionTiers: While the Killer is within 36m of you and inside a 45 degree cone, whenever you look at them, you hear a sound cue. Cooldown: 60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Available to every survivor, it plays a sound cue whenever the killer is close enough and positioned within a forward-facing cone. It functions as an early audio warning that lets the survivor pinpoint the killer's direction before turning.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a silent kill into a survivable one by giving the survivor a fraction of a second to react, turn, or vault before the attack lands. The directional nature of the cone means the warning is most useful when the killer is approaching head-on rather than from behind.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when a survivor wants an audio safety net during chases or while walking blind corners, since it works passively without any button press. It is a general survivor unlock and pairs well with any build that values early warning over raw escape speed.

Prove_Thyself.name: Prove Thyself
Prove_Thyself.description: For each other Survivor within 4m of you, all Survivors repair 6/8/10% faster.
descriptionTiers: For each other Survivor within 4m of you, all Survivors repair 6% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Dwight teaches the survivor perk, which grants every survivor on the team a repair speed bonus that scales with how many allies stand close by. A solo survivor gains nothing extra, so it only pays off in grouped work.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards teamwork and makes coordinated generator work meaningfully faster than isolated repair. A team that can get two or three survivors on the same generator early gains a substantial pace advantage over the rest of the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Dwight teaches the perk, and it rewards a survivor who coordinates closely with teammates at the Generator. Equip it when the team already has multiple survivors comfortable sharing a repair station, since the bonus only activates with nearby allies.

QuickQuiet.name: Quick & Quiet
QuickQuiet.description: You hide in Lockers and vault silently. The Killer is not alerted. Cooldown: 25/20/15s.
descriptionTiers: You hide in Lockers and vault silently. The Killer is not alerted. Cooldown: 25s.
You hide in Lockers and vault silently. The Killer is not alerted. Cooldown: 20s.
You hide in Lockers and vault silently. The Killer is not alerted. Cooldown: 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: Meg teaches the survivor perk, which lets the survivor drop into Lockers and vault through windows or gates without producing a sound the killer can detect. A short cooldown separates each use, so the silence cannot be chained indefinitely.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes one of the killer's most reliable tracking tools, the sound of a vault or the visual tell of a locker entry. A survivor who vaults silently can reset a chase or reposition without the killer knowing exactly where they went.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Meg teaches the perk, making it a strong fit for survivors who treat Lockers and vaults as their primary escape route. Equip it in matches where noisy movement would tip off the killer, since the silence strips away a key signal from the killer's awareness.

Rancor.name: Rancor
Rancor.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You are alerted to the position of all Survivors for 3s.
  • The Obsession sees your Aura for 5/4/3s.


When all Generators are completed:
  • The Obsession gains Exposed.
  • You can Kill the Obsession.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You are alerted to the position of all Survivors for 3s.
  • The Obsession sees your Aura for 5s.


When all Generators are completed:
  • The Obsession gains Exposed.
  • You can Kill the Obsession.

Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You are alerted to the position of all Survivors for 3s.
  • The Obsession sees your Aura for 4s.


When all Generators are completed:
  • The Obsession gains Exposed.
  • You can Kill the Obsession.

Whenever a Generator is completed:
  • You are alerted to the position of all Survivors for 3s.
  • The Obsession sees your Aura for 3s.


When all Generators are completed:
  • The Obsession gains Exposed.
  • You can Kill the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer-side tracking perk taught by Spirit that pulses with each generator completion, briefly revealing where every survivor is and showing the Obsession the killer's own aura. Once all generators are done it strips the Obsession of hiding and opens them to a lethal hit.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the moments between chases when the killer loses sight of everyone, because every finished generator becomes a free map-wide ping. The late-game escalation matters most when survivors are rushing the gates and the killer needs a reason to commit to the most active one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer build that struggles to find survivors after the early game, since each generator finish hands back positional information. Spirit teaches it, so it pairs naturally with hunting loops that reward knowing where the Obsession stands.

RedHerring.name: Red Herring
RedHerring.description:
After you repair a Generator for at least 1s, you see its Aura.

When you hide in a Locker, the Killer is alerted to the Generator. Cooldown: 25/20/15s.
descriptionTiers:
After you repair a Generator for at least 1s, you see its Aura.

When you hide in a Locker, the Killer is alerted to the Generator. Cooldown: 25s.

After you repair a Generator for at least 1s, you see its Aura.

When you hide in a Locker, the Killer is alerted to the Generator. Cooldown: 20s.

After you repair a Generator for at least 1s, you see its Aura.

When you hide in a Locker, the Killer is alerted to the Generator. Cooldown: 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor-side concealment perk from Zarina that keeps a generator's aura visible after a short repair and, when a locker is entered, sends the killer looking at that generator instead. A cooldown gates repeated use.
beginner.whyItMatters: It helps in the tense moment of hiding, because the killer's attention is pulled toward a generator rather than the locker a survivor just stepped into. The visible generator aura also makes it easier to track repair progress across the trial without re-walking to each one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor build leans on lockers for escape, since the misdirection buys a beat of safety while the killer checks the wrong spot. Zarina teaches it, so it slots into builds that already favor concealment over raw chase speed.

RememberMe.name: Remember Me
RememberMe.description:
Whenever the Obsession takes damage, you earn 1 Token, up to 3/4/5.


For each Token, Survivors who are not the Obsession open Exit Gates 18/24/30% slower.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Obsession takes damage, you earn 1 Token, up to 3.


For each Token, Survivors who are not the Obsession open Exit Gates 18% slower.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, you earn 1 Token, up to 4.


For each Token, Survivors who are not the Obsession open Exit Gates 24% slower.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, you earn 1 Token, up to 5.


For each Token, Survivors who are not the Obsession open Exit Gates 30% slower.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer-side obstruction perk from Nightmare that converts damage dealt to the Obsession into tokens, and each token slows every other survivor when they work an exit gate. The slow scales with how many tokens are banked.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes the moment the killer lands a hit on the most active survivor, because that single hit makes the gate rush harder for everyone else. The more damage traded in a chase, the heavier the tax on teammates trying to escape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer who chases hard and wants the damage to pay off later at the gates, since every hit on the Obsession feeds the slowdown. Nightmare teaches it, which suits a build that already commits to extended chases rather than quick drops.

RepressedAlliance.name: Repressed Alliance
RepressedAlliance.description: After repairing Generators for 55/50/45s, while repairing a Generator alone, use Active Ability button to block that generator for 15s.
descriptionTiers: After repairing Generators for 55s, while repairing a Generator alone, use Active Ability button to block that generator for 15s.
After repairing Generators for 50s, while repairing a Generator alone, use Active Ability button to block that generator for 15s.
After repairing Generators for 45s, while repairing a Generator alone, use Active Ability button to block that generator for 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: A strategy perk for survivors that, after sustained repair time, lets a lone survivor on a generator activate a short block on that generator. The ability only triggers while repairing alone, so it is a reactive tool for the moment a killer arrives mid-repair.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the vulnerable window of being alone on a generator with a killer closing in, because the block buys a brief pocket of safety without needing to run. Survivors who tend to get caught repairing solo get an extra button to press in that panic moment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor build already favors long solo repair sessions, since the sustained-time requirement means it rewards staying at a generator rather than constantly rotating. It suits a playstyle that accepts a bit of risk on the generator to get a defensive button in return.

Resilience.name: Resilience
Resilience.description:
While injured:
  • You bless and cleanse Totems 3/6/9% faster.
  • You heal 3/6/9% faster.
  • You open Exit Gates 3/6/9% faster.
  • You repair 3/6/9% faster.
  • You sabotage Hooks 3/6/9% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 3/6/9% faster.
  • You unlock chests 3/6/9% faster.
  • You vault 3/6/9% faster.
descriptionTiers:
While injured:
  • You bless and cleanse Totems 3% faster.
  • You heal 3% faster.
  • You open Exit Gates 3% faster.
  • You repair 3% faster.
  • You sabotage Hooks 3% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 3% faster.
  • You unlock chests 3% faster.
  • You vault 3% faster.

While injured:
  • You bless and cleanse Totems 6% faster.
  • You heal 6% faster.
  • You open Exit Gates 6% faster.
  • You repair 6% faster.
  • You sabotage Hooks 6% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 6% faster.
  • You unlock chests 6% faster.
  • You vault 6% faster.

While injured:
  • You bless and cleanse Totems 9% faster.
  • You heal 9% faster.
  • You open Exit Gates 9% faster.
  • You repair 9% faster.
  • You sabotage Hooks 9% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 9% faster.
  • You unlock chests 9% faster.
  • You vault 9% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A general perk available to any survivor that accelerates a wide range of actions while injured, including repairing, healing, vaulting, hooking, opening chests, and working exit gates. The more a survivor leans on these tasks while hurt, the more the speed bonus is felt.
beginner.whyItMatters: It smooths out the penalty of being injured by making every task a little quicker, which matters most in the late trial when an injured survivor still needs to finish generators, heal teammates, or rush a gate. It turns the hurt state from a full stop into a manageable slowdown.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on any survivor who expects to spend time injured, since the broad coverage means it pays off no matter which task the trial demands next. Because it is general, it can drop into any build without conflicting with a specific character's kit.

S24P01.name: Appraisal
S24P01.description:
When the trial starts, you earn 4 Tokens.

Spend 1 Token to rummage an empty Chest, up to 2 times per Chest.

You rummage Chests 40/60/80% faster.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, you earn 4 Tokens.

Spend 1 Token to rummage an empty Chest, up to 2 times per Chest.

You rummage Chests 40% faster.

When the trial starts, you earn 4 Tokens.

Spend 1 Token to rummage an empty Chest, up to 2 times per Chest.

You rummage Chests 60% faster.

When the trial starts, you earn 4 Tokens.

Spend 1 Token to rummage an empty Chest, up to 2 times per Chest.

You rummage Chests 80% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A support perk taught by a specific survivor that starts the trial with a small token pool and lets a survivor rummage empty chests multiple times, each rummage faster than normal. The tokens gate how many extra rummages are possible per chest.
beginner.whyItMatters: It helps in the early minutes when chests are still unopened, because the ability to search an already-empty chest means an item can be pulled from a location that looks done. The speed bonus on rummaging also trims the time a survivor is exposed while searching.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor build wants extra items without taking extra time at chests, since the token system rewards revisiting locations. It pairs well with builds that already have a reason to cross the map multiple times.

S24P02.name: Deception
S24P02.description:
Whenever you attempt to fast-enter a Locker:
  • You do not enter the Locker.
  • The Killer is alerted.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood for 5s.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks for 5s.


Cooldown: 25/20/15s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you attempt to fast-enter a Locker:
  • You do not enter the Locker.
  • The Killer is alerted.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood for 5s.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks for 5s.


Cooldown: 25s.

Whenever you attempt to fast-enter a Locker:
  • You do not enter the Locker.
  • The Killer is alerted.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood for 5s.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks for 5s.


Cooldown: 20s.

Whenever you attempt to fast-enter a Locker:
  • You do not enter the Locker.
  • The Killer is alerted.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood for 5s.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks for 5s.


Cooldown: 15s.

beginner.whatItIs: Concealment-oriented survivor perk that fakes a locker entry: the killer hears the locker but the survivor never actually steps inside, and for a short window afterward no blood pools or scratch marks are left. A cooldown prevents spamming the fake.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the split-second decision of whether to hide or keep running, because the fake entry buys a clean escape window without the commitment of actually locking in. The absence of traces afterward means a survivor who fakes and then sprints is harder to track than one who hides and gets found.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who often finds themselves near lockers with a killer close behind, since the fake gives a third option between hiding and running. It suits a reactive, read-the-killer playstyle over one that commits to hiding early.

S24P03.name: Power Struggle
S24P03.description:
While carried by the Killer, while you have at least 25/20/15% wiggle and next to an Upright Pallet, you can drop it to stun the Killer.

While downed, you see the Auras of Upright Pallets.
descriptionTiers:
While carried by the Killer, while you have at least 25% wiggle and next to an Upright Pallet, you can drop it to stun the Killer.

While downed, you see the Auras of Upright Pallets.

While carried by the Killer, while you have at least 20% wiggle and next to an Upright Pallet, you can drop it to stun the Killer.

While downed, you see the Auras of Upright Pallets.

While carried by the Killer, while you have at least 15% wiggle and next to an Upright Pallet, you can drop it to stun the Killer.

While downed, you see the Auras of Upright Pallets.

beginner.whatItIs: An adaptation perk that gives a carried survivor a way to break free early: if enough wiggle has been built and an upright pallet is nearby, the survivor can drop the pallet on the killer to stun them. While downed, the survivor can see which pallets are still upright.
beginner.whyItMatters: It changes the dynamics of being carried by turning a helplessly transported survivor into one who can fight back at a pallet, breaking the killer's rhythm of carrying to a hook. The pallet aura while downed also helps a survivor plan their next move before they are back on their feet.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor build wants a self-rescue option during the carry phase, since the wiggle requirement means it rewards staying active in the struggle. It fits a build that accepts the risk of being carried in exchange for a chance to turn the tables at a pallet.

S25P01.name: Fast Track
S25P01.description:
Whenever you unhook another Survivor, you earn 1 Token, up to 1/2/3.

While repairing, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 5% permanent progress.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you unhook another Survivor, you earn 1 Token, up to 1.

While repairing, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 5% permanent progress.

Whenever you unhook another Survivor, you earn 1 Token, up to 2.

While repairing, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 5% permanent progress.

Whenever you unhook another Survivor, you earn 1 Token, up to 3.

While repairing, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 5% permanent progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Token-based strategy perk that earns a token each time a survivor unhooks a teammate, then spends those tokens during repair to lock in permanent generator progress after a great skill check. The more unhooks that happen before a repair session, the more progress can be banked.
beginner.whyItMatters: It rewards the hook-rescue role by turning a risky unhook into lasting generator value, so a survivor who saves teammates is not just protecting a life but also banking map progress. The permanent progress means the benefit stays even as the trial goes on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who already plans to unhook teammates, since the token earning is passive and the spending happens naturally during repair. It suits a support-forward build that values map progress over individual chase performance.

S25P02.name: Smash Hit
S25P02.description:
Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 30/25/20s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 30s.

Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 25s.

Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Haste-granting navigation perk that fires the instant a survivor pallet-stuns the killer, giving a burst of extra speed for a short window. The same trigger applies a fatigue debuff that lasts longer than the speed boost, so the survivor must plan where to go while fast.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the critical beat right after a pallet drop, when a survivor is closest to danger and needs to put maximum distance before the killer recovers. The fatigue afterward is the trade-off: the survivor is fast for the escape but slower for the next stretch, so the route matters.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who chases well and wants the pallet-stun to be a hard escape rather than a brief breather, since the speed burst is the whole point. It fits an aggressive pallet playstyle that accepts the post-stun slowdown as the cost of a clean get-away.

S25P03.name: Self-Preservation
S25P03.description: Whenever another Survivor is hooked, you gain Elusive for 20/25/30s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever another Survivor is hooked, you gain Elusive for 20s.
Whenever another Survivor is hooked, you gain Elusive for 25s.
Whenever another Survivor is hooked, you gain Elusive for 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Elusive-granting concealment perk that triggers whenever another survivor is hooked, making the triggering survivor harder to track for a meaningful window. The protection is passive and automatic, requiring no button press or positioning.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the dangerous moment right after a teammate is hooked, when the killer is likely to pivot toward the next target. Being harder to see in that window gives a survivor time to finish a repair, hide, or reposition before the killer finishes at the hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor in a team where hooks are expected, since the trigger is entirely dependent on a teammate getting caught. It suits a build that plays near the action and wants a safety net when the killer commits to a hook.

S26P01.name: Counterforce
S26P01.description:
When the trial starts, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you cleanse a Totem, earn 1 Token, then, you see the Aura of the farthest Totem for 10/12/14s.

For each Token, you cleanse Totems 25% faster.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you cleanse a Totem, earn 1 Token, then, you see the Aura of the farthest Totem for 10s.

For each Token, you cleanse Totems 25% faster.

When the trial starts, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you cleanse a Totem, earn 1 Token, then, you see the Aura of the farthest Totem for 12s.

For each Token, you cleanse Totems 25% faster.

When the trial starts, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you cleanse a Totem, earn 1 Token, then, you see the Aura of the farthest Totem for 14s.

For each Token, you cleanse Totems 25% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Totem-tracking perception perk that starts with one token and earns another each time a totem is cleansed, then reveals the aura of the farthest remaining totem for a brief window. Each banked token also makes future cleanses quicker.
beginner.whyItMatters: It helps a survivor who struggles to find all the totems in a trial, because the farthest-totem reveal guides them toward what they have not yet cleansed. The cleansing speed bonus compounds: the more totems handled, the faster the next one goes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who already has a reason to cleanse totems, since the token system rewards consistent totem interaction. It suits a build that wants a steady information feed rather than a single big reveal.

S26P02.name: Resurgence
S26P02.description: Whenever you are unhooked, you gain 50/60/70% healing progress.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you are unhooked, you gain 50% healing progress.
Whenever you are unhooked, you gain 60% healing progress.
Whenever you are unhooked, you gain 70% healing progress.

beginner.whatItIs: An adaptation perk that, the moment a survivor is unhooked, fills their health bar partway so they are not starting from fully injured. The progress is immediate and requires no further action.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shrinks the vulnerable window after a rescue, because a survivor who would otherwise be badly hurt and scrambling is instead already partway to stable. That extra progress means less time spent healing and more time back on a generator or gate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who expects to be hooked and rescued, since the benefit only fires at the moment of unhooking. It suits a build that accepts hook risk in exchange for a faster return to the action.

S26P03.name: Blast Mine
S26P03.description:
After repairing 40% of Generators, while next to a Generator, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 100/110/120s. All Survivors see that Generator's Aura for that time.

When the Killer damages that Generator, the trap explodes, then:
  • They are stunned for 4s.
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.
descriptionTiers:
After repairing 40% of Generators, while next to a Generator, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 100s. All Survivors see that Generator's Aura for that time.

When the Killer damages that Generator, the trap explodes, then:
  • They are stunned for 4s.
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.

After repairing 40% of Generators, while next to a Generator, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 110s. All Survivors see that Generator's Aura for that time.

When the Killer damages that Generator, the trap explodes, then:
  • They are stunned for 4s.
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.

After repairing 40% of Generators, while next to a Generator, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 120s. All Survivors see that Generator's Aura for that time.

When the Killer damages that Generator, the trap explodes, then:
  • They are stunned for 4s.
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.

beginner.whatItIs: Generator-trap adaptation perk that, after a significant share of generators is complete, lets a survivor arm a trap on the generator they are standing next to. When the killer later damages that generator, the trap detonates, stunning the killer and blinding everyone nearby who is looking.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a generator into a defensive position, because the killer now faces a punishment for attacking it rather than a free sabotage. The blind effect also gives nearby survivors a brief moment of cover to escape or finish their own task.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who wants a way to protect a specific generator, since the trap is placed deliberately and lasts for a long window. It suits a build that accepts a mid-trial commitment in exchange for a hard counter to generator sabotage.

S27P01.name: Bite the Bullet
S27P01.description:
While healing, you and the healed Survivor make no noises or Grunts of Pain. Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check:
  • You lose only 3/2/1% progress.
  • The Killer is not alerted.
descriptionTiers:
While healing, you and the healed Survivor make no noises or Grunts of Pain. Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check:
  • You lose only 3% progress.
  • The Killer is not alerted.

While healing, you and the healed Survivor make no noises or Grunts of Pain. Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check:
  • You lose only 2% progress.
  • The Killer is not alerted.

While healing, you and the healed Survivor make no noises or Grunts of Pain. Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check:
  • You lose only 1% progress.
  • The Killer is not alerted.

beginner.whatItIs: Healing-adjacent safeguard perk that silences both the healer and the healed survivor during a heal, and reduces the penalty for a missed basic skill check during repair. A missed check costs only a sliver of progress and does not alert the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers two tense moments at once: the quiet heal that would otherwise give away position, and the fumbled skill check that would normally spike progress and ping the killer. Both effects make a survivor harder to catch in the act of repairing or healing.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who plans to spend long stretches healing teammates or grinding generators, because the muted grunts and the gentler penalty for failed checks both add up over a full match. The Survivor who teaches it fits naturally into any build that wants to stay busy without leaking noise.

S27P02.name: Flashbang
S27P02.description:
After repairing 50/45/40% of Generators, while hiding in a Locker, use Active Ability button to craft a Flashbang.

When you use the Flashbang:
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.
  • The Killer is alerted.
descriptionTiers:
After repairing 50% of Generators, while hiding in a Locker, use Active Ability button to craft a Flashbang.

When you use the Flashbang:
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.
  • The Killer is alerted.

After repairing 45% of Generators, while hiding in a Locker, use Active Ability button to craft a Flashbang.

When you use the Flashbang:
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.
  • The Killer is alerted.

After repairing 40% of Generators, while hiding in a Locker, use Active Ability button to craft a Flashbang.

When you use the Flashbang:
  • Everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded.
  • The Killer is alerted.

beginner.whatItIs: Flashbang is a survivor adaptation perk from a specific character. Once enough generator work has been completed on the map, the holder can craft a charge while hiding in a locker and then detonate it. The burst blinds everyone nearby who is facing it, and the killer is drawn to the location.
beginner.whyItMatters: It gives a survivor in a locker an offensive option, turning a passive hiding spot into a place from which to create a blind. The blind window is the escape: a survivor who steps out during the killer's disorientation has a clean path to run.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who hides in lockers and wants more than just concealment, since the Flashbang rewards the hiding position with an active tool. It suits a cautious build that turns defensive moments into brief windows of aggression.

S27P03.name: Rookie Spirit
S27P03.description: After you hit 5/4/3 basic repair Skill Checks, while a Generator is regressing, you see its Aura.
descriptionTiers: After you hit 5 basic repair Skill Checks, while a Generator is regressing, you see its Aura.
After you hit 4 basic repair Skill Checks, while a Generator is regressing, you see its Aura.
After you hit 3 basic repair Skill Checks, while a Generator is regressing, you see its Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Regression-detection perception perk that, after a handful of basic repair skill checks are landed, lets a survivor see the aura of any generator that is currently regressing. The reveal is passive and persists while the regression is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the frustrating moment when a generator silently loses progress and a survivor has no idea where the hit came from. Seeing the regressing generator's aura lets a survivor rush to defend it or at least know which one is under attack.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who wants to react to sabotage in real time, since the trigger is purely reactive to a regression happening. It suits a build that plays close to generators and values information over active tools.

S28P01.name: Clairvoyance
S28P01.description:
Whenever you bless or cleanse a Totem, while not holding an item, use Use Item button to, for up to 10/11/12s and within 64m:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Exit Gate Switches.
  • See the Auras of Generators.
  • See the Aura of the Hatch.
  • See the Auras of Hooks.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you bless or cleanse a Totem, while not holding an item, use Use Item button to, for up to 10s and within 64m:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Exit Gate Switches.
  • See the Auras of Generators.
  • See the Aura of the Hatch.
  • See the Auras of Hooks.

Whenever you bless or cleanse a Totem, while not holding an item, use Use Item button to, for up to 11s and within 64m:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Exit Gate Switches.
  • See the Auras of Generators.
  • See the Aura of the Hatch.
  • See the Auras of Hooks.

Whenever you bless or cleanse a Totem, while not holding an item, use Use Item button to, for up to 12s and within 64m:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Exit Gate Switches.
  • See the Auras of Generators.
  • See the Aura of the Hatch.
  • See the Auras of Hooks.

beginner.whatItIs: Totem-activated survivor perk that, when a survivor blesses or cleanses a totem without holding an item, reveals the auras of chests, generators, exit gate switches, the hatch, and hooks for a sustained window. The reveal covers most interactive objects on the map at once.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the guesswork from late-trial navigation, because a single totem cleanse can reveal where every chest, gate switch, and the hatch are simultaneously. A survivor who cleanses a totem at the right moment can plan a full route without wasting time searching.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who already cleanses totems as part of their rotation, since the reveal is a bonus on top of a normal action. It suits a build that wants map-wide information at a moment's notice and does not mind the empty-hands requirement.

S28P02.name: Boon: Circle of Healing
S28P02.description:
While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • While healing without a Med-Kit, they heal others 50/75/100% faster.
  • While injured, other Survivors see their Aura.
descriptionTiers:
While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • While healing without a Med-Kit, they heal others 50% faster.
  • While injured, other Survivors see their Aura.

While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • While healing without a Med-Kit, they heal others 75% faster.
  • While injured, other Survivors see their Aura.

While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • While healing without a Med-Kit, they heal others 100% faster.
  • While injured, other Survivors see their Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Boon-combining support perk that, when activated next to a totem, creates a unique Boon Totem merging all of a survivor's Boons into one field. Survivors inside the field heal others faster when not using a Med-Kit, and injured survivors become visible to their teammates.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a totem into a team hub, because the combined Boon field makes healing more efficient and keeps injured survivors from going dark. In a team that struggles to coordinate heals, the visibility alone can prevent a survivor from being left behind.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who already runs Boon totems, since the combining effect only matters if multiple Boons are present. It suits a support build that wants to consolidate its totem effects into one strong field rather than spreading thin.

S28P03.name: Boon: Shadow Step
S28P03.description:
While next to a Totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons. Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • Leave no Scratch Marks.
  • Their Auras cannot be seen by the Killer.


When leaving the range, this ends after 2/3/4s.

While survivors stand within its field, their scratch marks vanish and their auras become invisible to the killer. Once someone leaves the range, the concealment fades after a brief delay.
beginner.whyItMatters: It covers the open-ground stretch between objectives, because the scratch-mark removal and aura hiding make a survivor nearly invisible to a killer who relies on tracking cues. The short fade after leaving the field means a survivor must plan their exit from the Boon zone deliberately.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who runs Boon totems and wants a stealth field rather than a healing one, since the combining effect pools all Boons into the shadow effect. It suits a cautious build that crosses open ground often and wants to minimize the traces left behind.

S29P01.name: Overcome
S29P01.description:
Whenever you take damage:
  • You retain your speed boost for 2s longer.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you take damage:

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk that extends any active speed bonus for a brief moment after the survivor takes a hit. The trade-off is a long period of Exhausted, a speed penalty that keeps the survivor moving slowly for a while.
beginner.whyItMatters: That brief burst of extra speed can carry a survivor past a pallet or window before the killer recovers, turning a would-be down into a clean escape. The slowdown that follows means it is a one-shot tool, not a sustained advantage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a chase-focused build that relies on speed boosts from items or other perks, since it stretches the window when those boosts are most valuable. It triggers passively on hit, so no timing skill is needed beyond already being in a chase.

S29P02.name: Corrective Action
S29P02.description:
When the trial starts, you earn 1/2/3 Tokens, up to 5.

Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, earn 1 Token.

Whenever another Survivor misses a basic Skill Check, spend 1 Token:
  • The missed Skill Check becomes a good Skill Check.
  • You see that Survivor's Aura for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk that banks tokens from landing great skill checks and from the start of the trial. Spend one token the moment a teammate fails a basic skill check to upgrade their result to a successful one, which also flashes their aura for a short time.
beginner.whyItMatters: A teammate's botched skill check on a generator or healing channel otherwise wastes precious time and may draw the killer's attention through sound. Spending a token rescues that attempt, preserving the progress the team already put in.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a support or repair-heavy build where teammates regularly miss skill checks, since the token pool grows with consistent accuracy. It shines most when a generator or healing session is nearly done and a miss would undo the whole effort.

S29P03.name: Boon: Exponential
S29P03.description:
While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon totem that combines all your Boons.

Downed Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • Recover 90/95/100% faster.
  • Can fully recover.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk that lets the survivor bless a nearby totem with an active ability, merging all active boons into a single zone. Downed teammates inside that zone recover at an accelerated pace and can heal all the way up to full health.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single totem blessing becomes a wide-area healing zone, which helps when multiple teammates are downed near each other and a healer would be stretched thin. The chance to fully recover a downed survivor skips the hook entirely, removing them from the killer's board.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a totem-blessing build where a second or third boon is needed, since it amplifies every other boon a survivor already carries. It rewards positioning the totem near common downed spots like close to hooks or in off-map corners.

S30P01.name: Parental Guidance
S30P01.description:
Whenever you stun the Killer, for 5/6/7s:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk that silences the carrier the instant they stun the killer. For a short window after that stun, no Grunts of Pain, Pools of Blood, or Scratch Marks are left behind.
beginner.whyItMatters: A stun normally broadcasts the survivor's position through sound and visual cues, so removing those signals can let the stunner slip out of a loop the killer already knows. It is most useful in tight indoor chases where the killer can hear through walls.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pair it with stun sources like items or other perks to maximize the value of each stun. It suits a survivor who relies on stuns as the primary escape rather than vaults or pallets.

S30P02.name: Empathic Connection
S30P02.description:
You heal other Survivors 25/30/35% faster.

Injured Survivors see your Aura.
descriptionTiers:

Injured Survivors see your Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Perk for the survivor side that speeds up every heal performed on a teammate. Injured survivors also gain a clear sightline to the healer's aura, making it simple to locate the source of incoming help.
beginner.whyItMatters: Faster healing means less time kneeling in the open, which is dangerous when the killer is hunting nearby. The aura reveal helps teammates find the healer without calling over voice chat, which matters in solo or muted sessions.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a dedicated healing role, especially in matches where teammates struggle to locate the healer during a chase. The trade-off is that injured teammates can see the healer through walls, so position the healing spot away from the killer's likely path.

beginner.whatItIs: While a blessed totem is active, it grants a modest speed boost to any survivor standing inside the zone. The effect fades shortly after a survivor steps out, so it rewards staying near the totem during a chase.
beginner.whyItMatters: A small speed bonus in a known area helps survivors who must cross open ground between generators or totems, since the extra pace can close the distance before the killer reacts. The effect fades after stepping out, so it rewards positioning inside the zone during a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a totem-blessing build that wants a passive speed source near a known route, such as the path between two generators. It is less useful in tight indoor maps where survivors rarely need extra running speed.

S31P01.description:
Whenever the Killer damages another Survivor, you see the Killer's Aura for 6/8/10s.

You see other Survivors' Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: The killer's aura lights up the instant they injure a different survivor, giving a brief window of positioning. Other survivors' Scratch Marks also become visible, laying out a trail of where teammates have been running.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing where the killer was just moments ago helps predict their next move, especially when they pop out of fog or around a corner. Reading scratch marks from teammates also clarifies who ran where, which aids coordination during a multi-survivor chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a support build that reacts to teammate hits rather than chasing on its own. It pairs well with perks that reward seeing the killer's aura, since the reveal window is brief and must be acted on immediately.

S31P02.name: Residual Manifest
S31P02.description:
Whenever you blind the Killer, they gain Blindness for 20/25/30s.

You can rummage Chests 1 time. The first time you rummage a Chest, it will contain an uncommon Flashlight.
descriptionTiers:

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk that extends the killer's Blindness every time a Flashlight is triggered against them. It also grants a single guaranteed chest rummage that always yields an uncommon Flashlight regardless of the chest's default contents.
beginner.whyItMatters: A longer blind window gives the team more time to escape a chase or finish a repair without the killer seeing through fog. The guaranteed Flashlight removes the frustration of opening a chest and finding nothing useful, especially early in the match.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor carries a blinding item and wants that blind to last long enough to matter in a chase. The chest guarantee makes it appealing for any survivor who plans to visit a chest before the first hook.

S31P03.name: Overzealous
S31P03.description: Whenever you bless or cleanse a Totem, until you take damage, you repair 8/9/10% faster. If that Totem was a Hex Totem, the effect is doubled.

beginner.whatItIs: Perk that rewards totem work with a repair speed boost lasting until the survivor takes a hit. The bonus strengthens noticeably if the totem blessed or cleansed was a Hex Totem.
beginner.whyItMatters: Blessing a totem is a natural pause in a generator push, so the repair bonus turns that downtime into productive work. The doubled effect on hex totems makes the payoff especially strong when a survivor clears a hex and returns to repairs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a totem-and-generator hybrid build that alternates between cleansing and repairing. It suits a survivor who tends to bless or cleanse early and then immediately runs to a generator.

S32P01.name: Wiretap
S32P01.description:
After repairing 40% of Generators, while next to a Generator, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 100/110/120s or until the Killer damages that Generator. All Survivors see that Generator's Aura for that time.

While the Killer is within 14m of that Generator, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk that unlocks an active ability once enough generators have seen meaningful progress. Triggering it beside a machine exposes that generator's location to the entire team, and any killer who draws close becomes visible to everyone as well.
beginner.whyItMatters: The generator aura removes the guesswork of which machine the team should push next, especially in fog or on dark maps. Seeing the killer's aura when they are close to that generator helps the whole squad avoid running into them mid-repair.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a coordinated team build that wants a shared target marker without voice chat. Activate it once a few generators are underway, then focus the team on completing the marked one together.

S32P02.name: Reactive Healing
S32P02.description: While injured, whenever another Survivor within 32m of you takes damage, you gain 40/45/50% missing healing progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Perk that converts a teammate's injury into a burst of self-healing for the survivor carrying it. The effect only triggers while the carrier is already injured, rewarding those who stay close and survive long enough to benefit.
beginner.whyItMatters: Normally a survivor must kneel and channel healing, which is risky in the open. The perk turns a teammate's bad luck into a self-heal opportunity, so the healer can top themselves up without exposing themselves during a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a support build that stays close to teammates rather than working alone. It is most effective when the healer is already injured and positioned near the action, such as beside a downed survivor or during a generator push.

S32P03.name: Low Profile
S32P03.description:
When all other Survivors are downed or hooked, for 70/80/90s:

  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: Low Profile is a general survivor perk that Ada Wong unlocks in the Bloodweb. Once every other survivor on the map is downed or hooked, the holder stops producing the audible cues and physical traces that would otherwise mark their path for the killer to follow.
beginner.whyItMatters: As the last survivor standing, every footstep and grunt gives away position, so the killer loses their main tracking tools. The extended duration means the silence lasts through multiple loops rather than just one vault.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a solo-survivor build where the goal is to outlast the killer after all teammates fall. It is less useful in coordinated play where teammates are still standing and can distract the killer.

beginner.whyItMatters: The healed survivor becomes a mobile support hub, able to cleanse totems or pop chests much quicker while the buff is active. It chains well with totem-heavy strategies because the bonus applies to cleansing specifically.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a healing-first build that wants each heal to create a follow-up window for the teammate. It suits matches where totems are numerous and a second survivor can handle cleansing while the healer works the next injury.

S33P02.name: Reassurance

beginner.whatItIs: Pauses the sacrifice countdown on a hooked ally when a dedicated ability button is pressed while standing nearby, firing once per hook state. It creates a window to reach and free the hooked survivor before the sacrifice completes.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every second on the hook brings a teammate closer to being sacrificed, so stalling the timer creates room for a save. It is especially useful when the killer is camping the hook and a direct rescue looks impossible.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a rescue-focused build where saving hooked teammates is a priority. Stand near the hook, activate the ability to buy time, then coordinate a save with a stun or distraction from another perk.

S33P03.description:
Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

For each Token, basic Skill Checks:
  • Appear 4% more often.
  • Spin 4% faster.
  • Whenever you hit a great, give 10/20/30% more progress.


Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, hit a good Skill Check, or stop healing or repairing, lose all Tokens.
