beginner.whatItIs: Builds a token pool from each great basic skill check, with every token making subsequent checks appear more often and spin faster. Losing a check, landing only a good result, or stopping work drains the entire bank at once, so steady focus keeps it rolling.
beginner.whyItMatters: More frequent basic checks mean more chances to land a great and keep the token pool alive, creating a feedback loop that compounds over a long repair. The penalty for a miss or a pause means the effect punishes hesitation and demands steady, focused play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a high-skill-cap build where a survivor already lands great checks reliably during repairs and healing. It is less forgiving for newer players, since one bad check erases the entire pool.

S34P01.name: Potential Energy
S34P01.description:
While repairing, use Active Ability button 2 to earn Tokens instead of progress, up to 10/15/20 Tokens.

Whenever you take damage, lose all Tokens.

Whenever you take damage, lose all Tokens.

beginner.whatItIs: Converts generator work into a storable token pool while repairing, so progress banks up instead of applying immediately. A single press of its ability button cashes the whole pool into a burst of progress, but any hit received empties the bank out completely.
beginner.whyItMatters: Storing progress as tokens means a mid-repair hit does not waste the work already done, since the tokens can be spent after the chase ends. The burst of progress at the end of a session can also finish a generator faster than a steady pace would.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a risk-tolerant repair build that expects to be interrupted and wants to bank work in the meantime. Activate the token dump right after a chase to recover lost time and push the generator toward completion.

S34P02.name: Fogwise

beginner.whyItMatters: Seeing the killer while repairing is a constant source of stress, since a repairer is blind to what is happening around them. The perk turns each great check into a moment of awareness, helping the survivor spot the killer approaching and stop in time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a repair-focused build that wants situational awareness without a dedicated info perk. It is most useful in foggy or dark trials where the killer can sneak up from a distance.

While being chased, the auras of every other survivor become visible, and those teammates also repair faster. If the owner takes damage, the perk rests before it can kick back in.
beginner.whyItMatters: A chase normally freezes the team, but the repair bonus keeps other survivors productive by giving them a speed bump on generators. It also helps the chased survivor find a safe exit since teammate positions are visible through walls.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a build where one survivor expects to tank chases while the rest keep working. The repair bonus for teammates means the cost of a chase is partially offset by their faster progress.

S35P01.name: Cut Loose
S35P01.description:
While chased by the Killer, whenever you medium or fast-vault:
  • For up to 4/5/6s, your medium and fast vaults are silent.
  • During that time, whenever you medium or fast-vault, the timer is reset.


Cooldown: 45s.
descriptionTiers:
While chased by the Killer, whenever you medium or fast-vault:
  • For up to 4s, your medium and fast vaults are silent.
  • During that time, whenever you medium or fast-vault, the timer is reset.


Cooldown: 45s.

While chased by the Killer, whenever you medium or fast-vault:
  • For up to 5s, your medium and fast vaults are silent.
  • During that time, whenever you medium or fast-vault, the timer is reset.


Cooldown: 45s.

While chased by the Killer, whenever you medium or fast-vault:
  • For up to 6s, your medium and fast vaults are silent.
  • During that time, whenever you medium or fast-vault, the timer is reset.


Cooldown: 45s.

beginner.whatItIs: Cut Loose is a concealment perk that a specific character teaches to survivors. During a chase, medium and fast vaults play silent for a short stretch, and each new vault crossed renews the quiet window so a long obstacle run can be passed without noise. When the window lapses, the effect rests before it returns.
beginner.whyItMatters: Vault noise is one of the clearest tells a killer uses to track a survivor through obstacles, so removing it forces the killer to rely on sight alone. The reset on each vault means the silence can chain across multiple obstacles in a single chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a vault-heavy chase build that relies on window sills and low barriers to break line of sight. It is less useful on maps with few vaultable obstacles or when the killer is already in close visual range.

S35P02.name: Friendly Competition
S35P02.description: Whenever you finish repairing a Generator with at least 1 other Survivor, Survivors who finished repairing it repair 5% faster for 100/110/120s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you finish repairing a Generator with at least 1 other Survivor, Survivors who finished repairing it repair 5% faster for 100s.
Whenever you finish repairing a Generator with at least 1 other Survivor, Survivors who finished repairing it repair 5% faster for 110s.
Whenever you finish repairing a Generator with at least 1 other Survivor, Survivors who finished repairing it repair 5% faster for 120s.

beginner.whatItIs: Friendly Competition is a strategy perk taught to survivors by one character. Finishing a generator alongside at least another survivor grants a repair speed boost to everyone who helped bring it online, and that bonus carries over onto the next generator those survivors attack.
beginner.whyItMatters: Coordinated generator completion becomes more rewarding when both survivors get a bonus on the next machine, encouraging the team to stay together rather than split up. It also reduces the time gap between generators, keeping the team's pace tight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a coordinated team build where two or three survivors work the same generator together. It suits a playstyle that prioritizes finishing machines as a group and immediately moving to the next one.

S35P03.name: Teamwork: Power of Two
S35P03.description: Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while you stay within 8/12/16m of each other, you both gain 5% Haste. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while you stay within 8m of each other, you both gain 5% Haste. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while you stay within 12m of each other, you both gain 5% Haste. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while you stay within 16m of each other, you both gain 5% Haste. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor support perk that rewards staying close to a teammate after a heal is finished, granting both of you a short burst of extra movement speed while within range. The bonus ends a few moments after the pair drifts apart.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a completed heal into a shared escape window so the pair can sprint toward a pallet, window, or chest together instead of scattering. That keeps both survivors moving and harder to split.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the role is to keep a teammate alive after a down, then hold position nearby for a few seconds to bank the speed bonus. Split up once the bonus has done its job.

S36P01.name: Background Player
S36P01.description:
Whenever the Killer picks-up another Survivor, for the next 10s, when you start running:
  • Gain 50% Haste for 5s.
  • Gain Exhausted for 30/25/20s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Killer picks-up another Survivor, for the next 10s, when you start running:
  • Gain 50% Haste for 5s.
  • Gain Exhausted for 30s.

Whenever the Killer picks-up another Survivor, for the next 10s, when you start running:
  • Gain 50% Haste for 5s.
  • Gain Exhausted for 25s.

Whenever the Killer picks-up another Survivor, for the next 10s, when you start running:
  • Gain 50% Haste for 5s.
  • Gain Exhausted for 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor navigation perk that reacts to the killer carrying another teammate, letting the runner sprint away with a huge speed burst the moment movement starts. The burst is followed by a long period of Exhausted.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a teammate's bad moment into an escape chance because the sudden pace puts real distance between a survivor and the killer. The killer has to turn around and catch up again.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the team tends to get picked up often, since it gives a guaranteed burst of speed the instant that happens. Keep moving afterward because the follow-on fatigue lasts a long time.

S36P02.name: Blood Rush
S36P02.description:
Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 40/50/60s, while Exhausted, use Active Ability button to lose Exhausted instantly.

This is disabled by conspicuous actions.
descriptionTiers:
Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 40s, while Exhausted, use Active Ability button to lose Exhausted instantly.

This is disabled by conspicuous actions.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 50s, while Exhausted, use Active Ability button to lose Exhausted instantly.

This is disabled by conspicuous actions.

Until all Generators are completed, whenever you are unhooked, for the next 60s, while Exhausted, use Active Ability button to lose Exhausted instantly.

This is disabled by conspicuous actions.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor strategy perk that stays active while any generator remains, granting a button to burn off Exhausted instantly right after being unhooked. It stops working if a conspicuous action is performed.
beginner.whyItMatters: It removes the worst part of a rescue, the exhausted slow crawl, so a freshly unhooked survivor can move normally instead of being an easy target. That extra mobility in the first few seconds after a save is often what keeps a life.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for builds that lean on being saved often, then wait until the rescue lands and press the ability while still Exhausted. Spend it at the exact moment a run is needed rather than idling it.

S36P03.name: Teamwork: Collective Stealth
S36P03.description: Whenever another Survivor finishes healing you, while within 8/12/16m of each other, you both leave no Scratch Marks. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever another Survivor finishes healing you, while within 8m of each other, you both leave no Scratch Marks. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
Whenever another Survivor finishes healing you, while within 12m of each other, you both leave no Scratch Marks. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.
Whenever another Survivor finishes healing you, while within 16m of each other, you both leave no Scratch Marks. When either of you leaves the range, this ends after 4s.

beginner.whatItIs: Support perk that mutes Scratch Marks whenever a teammate finishes a heal, as long as the pair stays within a close range of each other. The silence fades a short time after the two separate.
beginner.whyItMatters: It hides the sound trail after a heal, which is the moment a killer most often hears a survivor pair and rushes in to break them up. A quiet pair is simply harder to find and punish.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the job is to heal and keep moving quietly, then hold near the healer for a short time to bank the silence. Drift apart only once the immediate danger has passed.

S37P01.name: Troubleshooter
S37P01.description:
While chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Aura of the Generator with the most progress.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, you see the Killer's Aura for 4/5/6s.


When the Killer stops chasing you, this ends after 6/8/10s.
descriptionTiers:
While chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Aura of the Generator with the most progress.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, you see the Killer's Aura for 4s.


When the Killer stops chasing you, this ends after 6s.

While chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Aura of the Generator with the most progress.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, you see the Killer's Aura for 5s.


When the Killer stops chasing you, this ends after 8s.

While chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Aura of the Generator with the most progress.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, you see the Killer's Aura for 6s.


When the Killer stops chasing you, this ends after 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: Chase-focused strategy perk that, during a pursuit, reveals the aura of the most-progress generator and briefly exposes the killer when a pallet is dropped. The effects fade a few seconds after the chase ends.
beginner.whyItMatters: It answers the two questions a chased survivor always has, where the work is and where the threat is. A single pallet drop becomes both an escape and a read on the map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if chase survival that also feeds generator information sounds right, then drop pallets deliberately to peek the killer's position. Use each drop as both a save and a scouting tool.

S37P02.name: Made for This
S37P02.description:
While injured, whenever you finish healing another Survivor, you gain Endurance for 6/8/10s.

While you have Deep Wound, you gain 1/2/3% Haste.
descriptionTiers:
While injured, whenever you finish healing another Survivor, you gain Endurance for 6s.

While you have Deep Wound, you gain 1% Haste.

While injured, whenever you finish healing another Survivor, you gain Endurance for 8s.

While you have Deep Wound, you gain 2% Haste.

While injured, whenever you finish healing another Survivor, you gain Endurance for 10s.

While you have Deep Wound, you gain 3% Haste.

beginner.whatItIs: Guarded safeguard perk that grants Endurance after healing a teammate while already injured, and adds a steady speed boost as long as Deep Wound is present. The speed bonus grows with the severity of the wound.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a wounded survivor keep working through the pain, turning a fragile injured state into a window where extra healing or a risky vault can still happen. Staying functional while hurt is the core of the perk.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for builds that want to push through an injury, then keep healing others while wounded to bank the endurance. Do not collapse into a corner; keep trading heals.

S37P03.name: Scavenger
S37P03.description:
While repairing and while your Toolbox is empty, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you earn 1 Token.

When you have 5 Tokens, spend them all:
  • Your Toolbox is recharged instantly.
  • You repair 50% slower for 40/35/30s.


You can rummage Chests 1 time. The first time you rummage a Chest, it will contain an uncommon Toolbox.
descriptionTiers:

  • Your Toolbox is recharged instantly.

You can rummage Chests 1 time. The first time you rummage a Chest, it will contain an uncommon Toolbox.

beginner.whatItIs: Repair adaptation perk that builds up Tokens from great basic Skill Checks while the Toolbox is empty, and once enough Tokens are banked the Toolbox refills instantly. It also allows a Chest to be rummaged once for a rare Toolbox.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes a lucky repair streak directly pay for a full Toolbox, which is exactly the resource a survivor needs when the work demands it most. The brief slowdown in repair speed is the price for that refill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when relying on the Toolbox matters, since it rewards great Skill Checks with a refill. Treat a clean repair streak as fuel for a full toolbox rather than letting it slip.

S38P01.name: Dramaturgy
S38P01.description:
While healthy and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.


Then, one happens at random:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exposed for 12s.
  • You gain a random rare item with random add-ons.
  • You scream, but nothing happens.


The same effect cannot happen twice in a row.

  • You gain Exposed for 12s.
  • You gain a random rare item with random add-ons.
  • You scream, but nothing happens.


The same effect cannot happen twice in a row.

While healthy and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 50s.


Then, one happens at random:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exposed for 12s.
  • You gain a random rare item with random add-ons.
  • You scream, but nothing happens.


The same effect cannot happen twice in a row.

While healthy and running, use Active Ability button:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 40s.


Then, one happens at random:
  • You gain 25% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exposed for 12s.
  • You gain a random rare item with random add-ons.
  • You scream, but nothing happens.


The same effect cannot happen twice in a row.

beginner.whatItIs: Movement perk that, while healthy and running, spends a button to dash with a speed burst and a long fatigue cost, then rolls a random effect that could be more haste, exposure, a rare item, or a silent scream. The same result cannot repeat back to back.
beginner.whyItMatters: It packages an escape dash with a gamble, so the same button press might save a chase or hand the killer a new lead depending on the roll. That uncertainty makes it a tool for a single desperate moment.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the situation is urgent enough to gamble, since the random outcome can help or hurt. Save the button for the one moment a dash is truly needed.

S38P02.name: Scene Partner
S38P02.description:
While you are within the Killer's Terror Radius, whenever you look at them:
  • Scream, then see the Killer's Aura for 4/5/6s.
  • There is a 50% chance you will scream again. If you do, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s more.


Cooldown: 40s.
descriptionTiers:
While you are within the Killer's Terror Radius, whenever you look at them:
  • Scream, then see the Killer's Aura for 4s.
  • There is a 50% chance you will scream again. If you do, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s more.


Cooldown: 40s.

While you are within the Killer's Terror Radius, whenever you look at them:
  • Scream, then see the Killer's Aura for 5s.
  • There is a 50% chance you will scream again. If you do, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s more.


Cooldown: 40s.

While you are within the Killer's Terror Radius, whenever you look at them:
  • Scream, then see the Killer's Aura for 6s.
  • There is a 50% chance you will scream again. If you do, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s more.


Cooldown: 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Navigation perk that fires whenever a survivor looks at the killer inside the Terror Radius, screaming and briefly revealing the killer's aura. There is a chance of a second scream that extends the reveal.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the killer's own proximity into a source of information, so simply facing the threat can show where it is for a few seconds. The scream is the trade-off for that glimpse.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for a survivor who wants to read the killer's position at range, then use it carefully because the scream makes the trade-off loud. It resets on a long cooldown, so spend it sparingly.

S38P03.name: Plot Twist
S38P03.description:
While injured, crouched and idle, use Active Ability button 2 to be downed silently.

While downed this way, once per trial:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 25% faster.
  • You can fully recover.


Whenever you recover this way:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 2/3/4s.
  • You are healed instantly.


When all Generators are completed, you can use this ability once again.
descriptionTiers:

  • You can fully recover.


Whenever you recover this way:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 2s.
  • You are healed instantly.


When all Generators are completed, you can use this ability once again.

While injured, crouched and idle, use Active Ability button 2 to be downed silently.

While downed this way, once per trial:

  • You recover 25% faster.
  • You can fully recover.


Whenever you recover this way:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 3s.
  • You are healed instantly.


When all Generators are completed, you can use this ability once again.

While injured, crouched and idle, use Active Ability button 2 to be downed silently.

While downed this way, once per trial:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You recover 25% faster.
  • You can fully recover.


Whenever you recover this way:
  • You gain 50% Haste for 4s.
  • You are healed instantly.


When all Generators are completed, you can use this ability once again.

beginner.whatItIs: Concealment perk that, while injured and crouched, spends a button to go down silently, trading a public hook for a quiet state that hides grunts and blood pools. Once recovered this way, it grants a speed burst and a full heal.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets an injured survivor control the moment of going down, removing the screams and blood trail that normally tell the killer exactly where to keep the body. That quiet drop-and-recover loop is the heart of the perk.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when surviving a hook matters more than the drama of one, then crouch quietly in a safe spot and spend the button to drop silently. Come out faster and fully healed, and the option resets once the generators are done.

S39P01.name: Lucky Star
S39P01.description:
While hiding in a Locker, you make no Grunts of Pain.

Whenever you exit a Locker, for 30s:
  • You see the Aura of the closest Generator.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.


Cooldown: 35/30/25s.
descriptionTiers:
While hiding in a Locker, you make no Grunts of Pain.

Whenever you exit a Locker, for 30s:
  • You see the Aura of the closest Generator.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.


Cooldown: 35s.

While hiding in a Locker, you make no Grunts of Pain.

Whenever you exit a Locker, for 30s:
  • You see the Aura of the closest Generator.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.


Cooldown: 30s.

While hiding in a Locker, you make no Grunts of Pain.

Whenever you exit a Locker, for 30s:
  • You see the Aura of the closest Generator.
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors.
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.


Cooldown: 25s.

beginner.whatItIs: Locker-focused perk that silences grunts while hiding in a locker and, after stepping out, reveals the closest generator and other survivors while leaving no blood pools. The whole effect runs on a cooldown.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes hiding in a locker a genuine stealth moment rather than a risky one, and the post-exit reveal helps a lone survivor find their way back to the work. Quiet in, informed out is the whole idea.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Lucky Star suits a route that favors early locker drops, because it silences the noise a hiding survivor would otherwise make and then reveals the nearest unfinished generator once you step out. Equip it on maps where a quiet locker moment pays off more than staying in the open, since the perk is taught by a specific survivor character and builds around that loop.

S39P02.name: Chemical Trap
S39P02.description:
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 40/50/60s. All Survivors see that Pallet's Aura for that time.

When the Killer breaks that Pallet, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 4s.
descriptionTiers:
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 40s. All Survivors see that Pallet's Aura for that time.

When the Killer breaks that Pallet, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 4s.

After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 50s. All Survivors see that Pallet's Aura for that time.

When the Killer breaks that Pallet, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 4s.

After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Dropped Pallet, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 60s. All Survivors see that Pallet's Aura for that time.

When the Killer breaks that Pallet, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 4s.

beginner.whatItIs: Map control perk that, after some generator progress, spends a button next to a dropped pallet to trap it, and when the killer breaks that pallet they are briefly Hindered by the burst. All survivors can see the trapped pallet's aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns a dropped pallet into a one-time speed penalty for the killer, which is useful at a spot the survivor just escaped through and wants to keep contested. The aura marker keeps the team aware of the trap.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when escaping a chase through a specific pallet and wanting to slow the killer if they try the same path again. Set it the moment the escape is done and the pallet is in place.

S39P03.name: Light-footed
S39P03.description:
While healthy and running, your footsteps are silent to the Killer.

Whenever you do a fast-action, cooldown: 14/12/10s.
descriptionTiers:
While healthy and running, your footsteps are silent to the Killer.

Whenever you do a fast-action, cooldown: 14s.

While healthy and running, your footsteps are silent to the Killer.

Whenever you do a fast-action, cooldown: 12s.

While healthy and running, your footsteps are silent to the Killer.

Whenever you do a fast-action, cooldown: 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: Stealth perk that keeps footsteps silent while healthy and running, with a short cooldown that ticks whenever a fast action like a vault or interaction is performed. Staying healthy is the condition that keeps the silence.
beginner.whyItMatters: It lets a survivor cross open ground quietly during a chase or a risky generator trip, which is the difference between slipping past the killer and being heard. A silent crossing is often what saves a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the map has long straight runs and the plan is to cross them on foot, since the silence only holds while staying healthy and moving. Avoid vaulting constantly, which resets the quiet.

S40P01.name: Champion of Light
S40P01.description:
While you are using a Flashlight, you gain 50% Haste.

Whenever you blind the Killer, they gain 20% Hindered for 6s. Cooldown: 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
While you are using a Flashlight, you gain 50% Haste.

Whenever you blind the Killer, they gain 20% Hindered for 6s. Cooldown: 60s.

While you are using a Flashlight, you gain 50% Haste.

Whenever you blind the Killer, they gain 20% Hindered for 6s. Cooldown: 50s.

While you are using a Flashlight, you gain 50% Haste.

Whenever you blind the Killer, they gain 20% Hindered for 6s. Cooldown: 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Speed safeguard perk that adds haste while holding a Flashlight and briefly Hinders the killer when a blind succeeds, all on a long cooldown. Holding the item up is what keeps the speed bonus active.
beginner.whyItMatters: It pairs a flashlight build with real chase speed and a punishment on the killer, so the same item that hides the killer also pushes the survivor forward. A landed blind becomes a small window to gain ground.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for flashlight-focused survivor builds, since it rewards holding the item up during a chase and landing a blind to slow the pursuer. Spend the blind at the moment it opens a path.

S40P02.name: Boon: Illumination
S40P02.description:
While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Generators.


While you have a Boon Totem, you bless and cleanse 6/8/10% faster.
descriptionTiers:
While next to a totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon totem that combines all your Boons.

Survivors within the Boon's range:
  • See the Auras of Chests.
  • See the Auras of Generators.


While you have a Boon Totem, you bless and cleanse 6% faster.

While you have a Boon Totem, you bless and cleanse 8% faster.

Survivors within the Boon's range:

While you have a Boon Totem, you bless and cleanse 10% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Strategy perk that spends a button next to a totem to bless it into a Boon totem, whose range reveals Chests and Generators while all Boons are combined. Blessing and cleansing also work faster while the Boon totem is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: It converts a totem into a zone of shared information for the whole team, which is the kind of map awareness a group needs when pushing generators. The combined Boons mean one totem covers several needs at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for team-oriented builds that want shared generator and chest visibility, then bless a totem early and keep the Boon totem alive through the push. Place it where the team will actually work.

S40P03.name: Deadline
S40P03.description:
While injured, basic Skill Checks:
  • Are 6/8/10% more likely to appear.
  • Appear in random places.


Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 50% less progress.
descriptionTiers:
While injured, basic Skill Checks:
  • Are 6% more likely to appear.
  • Appear in random places.


Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 50% less progress.

While injured, basic Skill Checks:
  • Are 8% more likely to appear.
  • Appear in random places.


Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 50% less progress.

While injured, basic Skill Checks:
  • Are 10% more likely to appear.
  • Appear in random places.


Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 50% less progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Concealment perk that, while injured, makes basic Skill Checks appear more often and in random spots, and softens the progress lost when one is missed. Being injured is what turns the effect on.
beginner.whyItMatters: It changes the repair rhythm for an injured survivor, turning the usual predictable circles into a scattered pattern that is harder to read and less punishing to botch. Fewer wasted progress points keep the generator moving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when staying productive while wounded is the priority, since it both adds checks to survive and shrinks the damage a miss does. It shines on the survivor expected to keep working through an injury.

S41P01.name: Invocation: Weaving Spiders
S41P01.description:
While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • All Generators gain 8/9/10 permanent charges.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.
descriptionTiers:
While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • All Generators gain 8 permanent charges.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • All Generators gain 9 permanent charges.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • All Generators gain 10 permanent charges.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

beginner.whatItIs: Basement perk that spends a button next to the circle to begin an Invocation, and when it completes it adds permanent charges to all generators at the cost of injury and Broken. Only one Invocation can be completed per trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: It trades a survivor's own health for a chunk of shared generator progress, which speeds up the overall push when the team needs the work done quickly. Other survivors can see the aura and join the Invocation while it runs.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for aggressive early-game builds, then run to the Basement early and complete the Invocation before the killer can stop it. Time it when the team is ready to bank the free charges.

S41P02.name: Strength in Shadows
S41P02.description:
While in the Basement:
  • You can heal yourself, but 30% slower.
  • Whenever you finish healing, you see the Killer's Aura for 6/8/10s.
descriptionTiers:
While in the Basement:
  • You can heal yourself, but 30% slower.
  • Whenever you finish healing, you see the Killer's Aura for 6s.

While in the Basement:
  • You can heal yourself, but 30% slower.
  • Whenever you finish healing, you see the Killer's Aura for 8s.

While in the Basement:
  • You can heal yourself, but 30% slower.
  • Whenever you finish healing, you see the Killer's Aura for 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: Healing adaptation perk that lets a survivor self-heal in the Basement at a slower pace and, on finishing, briefly reveals the killer's aura. Being inside the Basement is the condition for the effect.
beginner.whyItMatters: It makes the Basement a place where an injured survivor can patch themselves up and then read the killer, which is useful when the map pushes play underground. The self-heal removes the need to wait for a teammate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the trial will feature the Basement and the goal is to recover there rather than wait, since it also hands out a free look at the killer. Use it on maps where the Underground is a real part of the loop.

S41P03.name: Wicked
S41P03.description:
While in the Basement, you can unhook yourself.

Whenever you are unhooked, you see the Killer's Aura for 16/18/20s.
descriptionTiers:
While in the Basement, you can unhook yourself.

Whenever you are unhooked, you see the Killer's Aura for 16s.

While in the Basement, you can unhook yourself.

Whenever you are unhooked, you see the Killer's Aura for 18s.

While in the Basement, you can unhook yourself.

Whenever you are unhooked, you see the Killer's Aura for 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Rescue perk that lets a survivor unhook themselves in the Basement and, after any unhook, reveals the killer's aura for an extended window. The self-unhook only works while inside the Basement.
beginner.whyItMatters: It breaks the usual rule that only a healthy teammate can free a hooked survivor, and the long aura reveal afterward makes the escape much safer. Surviving a Basement hook without outside help is the whole point.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when surviving a hook in the Basement is the main threat, since it both enables a self-rescue and pays out a long look at the killer. It is a safety net for a survivor who would otherwise be stuck on the hook.

S42P01.name: Mirrored Illusion
S42P01.description: After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator, or Totem, use Active Ability button 2 to create a static illusion for 40/50/60s.
descriptionTiers: After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator, or Totem, use Active Ability button 2 to create a static illusion for 40s.
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator, or Totem, use Active Ability button 2 to create a static illusion for 50s.
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator, or Totem, use Active Ability button 2 to create a static illusion for 60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Mirrored Illusion is a survivor perk tied to a specific character rather than a general unlock. Once the map's repair progress reaches a threshold, it can conjure a static illusion anchored to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator, or Totem, where it lingers and masks activity in the surrounding area.
beginner.whyItMatters: It creates a fake point of interest that can draw the killer's attention or mislead their path, which is handy when a real objective needs to be reached quietly. A decoy can buy a survivor the few seconds to slip away.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer is hunting a specific objective and a decoy would help, then place the illusion on a nearby object to pull the pursuer off course. Use it right before a risky interaction at that object.

S42P02.name: Bardic Inspiration
S42P02.description:
While idle, use Active Ability button to perform, empowering all Survivors within 16m for up to 15s. While you are performing, other Survivors will see your Aura. Roll a d20:
  • 1 | You scream, but nothing happens.
  • 2-10 | Basic Skill Checks give +1% progress.
  • 11-19 | Basic Skill Checks give +2% progress.
  • 20 | Basic Skill Checks give +3% progress.


If you complete the performance, this effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 110/100/90s.
descriptionTiers:
While idle, use Active Ability button to perform, empowering all Survivors within 16m for up to 15s. While you are performing, other Survivors will see your Aura. Roll a d20:
  • 1 | You scream, but nothing happens.
  • 2-10 | Basic Skill Checks give +1% progress.
  • 11-19 | Basic Skill Checks give +2% progress.
  • 20 | Basic Skill Checks give +3% progress.


If you complete the performance, this effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 110s.

  • 1 | You scream, but nothing happens.
  • 2-10 | Basic Skill Checks give +1% progress.
  • 11-19 | Basic Skill Checks give +2% progress.
  • 20 | Basic Skill Checks give +3% progress.


If you complete the performance, this effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 100s.

While idle, use Active Ability button to perform, empowering all Survivors within 16m for up to 15s. While you are performing, other Survivors will see your Aura. Roll a d20:
  • 1 | You scream, but nothing happens.
  • 2-10 | Basic Skill Checks give +1% progress.
  • 11-19 | Basic Skill Checks give +2% progress.
  • 20 | Basic Skill Checks give +3% progress.


If you complete the performance, this effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 90s.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk that lets a lone survivor stand still and channel an active ability, broadcasting a small skill-check buff to every nearby survivor for a limited window. The performer's aura becomes visible to the whole team while the effect is active.
beginner.whyItMatters: The buff makes routine actions like generator progress, healing, and lockpicking slightly quicker, which adds up over a full trial. It works best when a group is already clustered together so the whole team benefits from each boosted action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team tends to camp near one generator for an extended stretch, since standing still to perform is only safe in a relatively quiet area. Pick a location that is not directly on a killer's loop, because the performer's visible aura makes the spot easy to find.

S42P03.name: Still Sight
S42P03.description:
After being idle for 4/3/2s, within 24m, until you start moving:
  • You see the Killer's Aura.
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.
descriptionTiers:
After being idle for 4s, within 24m, until you start moving:
  • You see the Killer's Aura.
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.

After being idle for 3s, within 24m, until you start moving:
  • You see the Killer's Aura.
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.

After being idle for 2s, within 24m, until you start moving:
  • You see the Killer's Aura.
  • You see the Auras of Chests.
  • You see the Auras of Generators.

beginner.whatItIs: Remaining completely idle for a short moment reveals the killer's aura, the auras of nearby chests, and the auras of unfinished generators all at once. The reveal lasts until the survivor starts moving again.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing exactly where the killer, loot, and remaining generators are lets a survivor plan the next route without guessing. It is especially helpful early in a trial when the map is still unknown and every bit of information saves a wrong turn.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Use it when standing still feels safe enough, such as right after finishing a long heal or while crouched behind a solid obstacle. It is a scouting tool, so pair it with a cautious playstyle that prefers information over aggression.

S43P01.name: Finesse
S43P01.description:
While healthy, you fast-vault 20% faster.

Whenever you fast-vault, cooldown: 40/35/30s.
descriptionTiers:
While healthy, you fast-vault 20% faster.

Whenever you fast-vault, cooldown: 40s.

While healthy, you fast-vault 20% faster.

Whenever you fast-vault, cooldown: 35s.

While healthy, you fast-vault 20% faster.

Whenever you fast-vault, cooldown: 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Fast-vaulting through windows and similar openings becomes noticeably quicker while a survivor is healthy. A short cooldown applies after each use, so it cannot be spammed in rapid succession.
beginner.whyItMatters: Closing a gap to a pallet or a window a moment sooner can be the difference between escaping a chase and taking a hit. The speed boost is most valuable for a survivor who relies on tight loops and quick vaults to stay alive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the preferred playstyle revolves around fast, aggressive chases with frequent vaulting rather than long slow runs. It suits a survivor who wants to feel snappy and responsive in every pallet-and-window exchange.

S43P02.name: Hardened
S43P02.description: When you have blessed or cleansed a Totem and unlocked a Chest, whenever you would scream, you see the Killer's Aura for 3/4/5s instead.
descriptionTiers: When you have blessed or cleansed a Totem and unlocked a Chest, whenever you would scream, you see the Killer's Aura for 3s instead.
When you have blessed or cleansed a Totem and unlocked a Chest, whenever you would scream, you see the Killer's Aura for 4s instead.
When you have blessed or cleansed a Totem and unlocked a Chest, whenever you would scream, you see the Killer's Aura for 5s instead.

beginner.whatItIs: Once the holder has both blessed or cleansed a totem and unlocked a chest at some point in the match, the next moment they would otherwise scream, the killer's aura is revealed briefly instead. The scream itself stays silent, so the killer does not hear the alert.
beginner.whyItMatters: Screaming is normally the killer's favorite trigger, since it announces exactly where a survivor is. Replacing that loud alert with a brief aura reveal removes the killer's best tool for locking down a fleeing survivor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays around totems and chests, since those actions are what arm the perk. It rewards a methodical survivor who cleanses and loots on purpose rather than rushing through every generator in a blind panic.

S43P03.name: Specialist
S43P03.description:
Whenever you rummage or unlock a Chest, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

While repairing a Generator, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 2/3/4% permanent progress.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you rummage or unlock a Chest, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

While repairing a Generator, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 2% permanent progress.

Whenever you rummage or unlock a Chest, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

While repairing a Generator, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 3% permanent progress.

Whenever you rummage or unlock a Chest, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

While repairing a Generator, whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, spend all Tokens. For each Token spent, the Generator gains 4% permanent progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Rummaging through or unlocking chests builds up a small pool of tokens, and spending them all at once during a generator repair grants permanent progress to that generator. The bonus is locked in permanently and does not fade over time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Permanent generator progress means the team needs less total work to finish the remaining generators, which shortens the whole trial. It turns chest unlocks from a minor side quest into a direct investment in the win condition.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team has a clear plan to unlock chests before finishing generators, since the tokens only matter if they are collected and then spent at the right moment. It rewards a survivor who keeps an eye on both the chest and the generator.

S44P01.name: Eyes of Belmont
S44P01.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Killer's Aura for 1/2/3s.

Whenever you see the Killer's Aura for a duration, it is 2s longer.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Killer's Aura for 1s.

Whenever you see the Killer's Aura for a duration, it is 2s longer.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s.

Whenever you see the Killer's Aura for a duration, it is 2s longer.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you see the Killer's Aura for 3s.

Whenever you see the Killer's Aura for a duration, it is 2s longer.

beginner.whatItIs: Completing a generator flashes the killer's aura for a brief moment, and any other aura reveal the survivor gains lasts a little longer than normal. The perk stacks with other aura-revealing effects, making each one feel more substantial.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing where the killer is immediately after a generator finishes helps the surviving team avoid walking straight into the next chase. The extended aura duration also makes totem-related reveals and other informational perks more useful.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team wants a reliable post-generator safety check before deciding where to move next. It suits a survivor who prefers to stay informed and make deliberate route choices rather than reacting to sounds.

S44P02.name: Exultation
S44P02.description:
Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • Your item rarity is upgraded to the next tier, if possible.
  • If the item was upgraded, it recharges 75% Charges.


Cooldown: 30/25/20s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • Your item rarity is upgraded to the next tier, if possible.
  • If the item was upgraded, it recharges 75% Charges.


Cooldown: 30s.

Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • Your item rarity is upgraded to the next tier, if possible.
  • If the item was upgraded, it recharges 75% Charges.


Cooldown: 25s.

Whenever you Pallet-stun the Killer:
  • Your item rarity is upgraded to the next tier, if possible.
  • If the item was upgraded, it recharges 75% Charges.


Cooldown: 20s.

beginner.whatItIs: Pallet-stunning the killer upgrades the survivor's carried item to the next rarity tier, and if the upgrade succeeds the item also recharges a large share of its remaining uses. A cooldown applies after each activation.
beginner.whyItMatters: Item rarity tiers determine how strong a tool is, so climbing a tier mid-chase can turn a mediocre item into a game-changing one. The recharge on top of the upgrade means the upgraded item is not immediately spent.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor already carries an item with multiple rarity tiers and wants a reward for aggressive pallet play. It suits a chase-focused build that wants every successful stun to pay a tangible bonus.

S44P03.name: Moment of Glory
S44P03.description:
After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while not Broken, when you become injured, gain Broken.

After 80/70/60s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.
descriptionTiers:
After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while not Broken, when you become injured, gain Broken.

After 80s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while not Broken, when you become injured, gain Broken.

After 70s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while not Broken, when you become injured, gain Broken.

After 60s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Unlocking a single chest arms a delayed safety net: the next time the survivor becomes injured, they instead gain Broken for a set period and then heal instantly if they have not been downed by the time the timer ends. The effect triggers only once per trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: Getting back to a stable state without outside help matters because it shortens the vulnerable stretch after taking a hit, letting the holder return to repairing or moving instead of waiting on a teammate to patch them up. The catch is staying untouched until the countdown finishes, since another hit before then cancels the free recovery.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor expects to take at least one hit but wants to avoid the slow and vulnerable injured state. It suits a survivor who plays close to generators and accepts some risk in exchange for a guaranteed recovery.

S45P01.name: Invocation: Treacherous Crows
S45P01.description:
While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button 2 to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • Whenever the Killer scares a Crow while a Survivor is in their Terror Radius, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 1/1.5/2s.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.
descriptionTiers:
While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button 2 to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • Whenever the Killer scares a Crow while a Survivor is in their Terror Radius, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 1s.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button 2 to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • Whenever the Killer scares a Crow while a Survivor is in their Terror Radius, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 1.5s.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

While in the Basement next to the circle, use Active Ability button 2 to invoke. While invoking, other Survivors see your Aura and can join your Invocation.

When the Invocation is completed:
  • Whenever the Killer scares a Crow while a Survivor is in their Terror Radius, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 2s.
  • You become injured.
  • You gain Broken.


Each Invocation can only be completed once per trial.

beginner.whatItIs: Standing in a basement circle and channeling an active ability lets nearby survivors join, and once the invocation completes, scaring crows in the killer's terror radius reveals the killer's aura to the whole team. The channeling survivor takes an injury and gains Broken as a cost, and each invocation can only be completed once per trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: Killer aura reveals from crow scares are rare and hard to set up, so having a guaranteed trigger makes them a reliable source of information. The cost of becoming injured and Broken means the team must value the information enough to justify the risk.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team is comfortable playing in or near the basement and is willing to take a hit in exchange for repeated killer location reveals. It suits a coordinated group that can protect the channeling survivor while the invocation runs.

S45P02.name: Clean Break
S45P02.description:
Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while being healed by another Survivor, use Active Ability button to gain Broken.

After 75/60/45s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while being healed by another Survivor, use Active Ability button to gain Broken.

After 75s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while being healed by another Survivor, use Active Ability button to gain Broken.

After 60s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

Whenever you finish healing another Survivor, while being healed by another Survivor, use Active Ability button to gain Broken.

After 45s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Clean Break is a survivor perk taught by a specific character. Pressing the active ability button while you finish a heal on one teammate and are simultaneously receiving a heal from another grants the Broken state. Once that state is active, a countdown runs and, as long as no down lands, the survivor snaps back to full health.
beginner.whyItMatters: Skipping the injured state after a heal means the survivor can immediately return to repairing, healing, or running without the slow, noisy penalty. It keeps the team's momentum going instead of pausing for a full recovery.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays a supportive role and expects to chain heals back and forth between survivors. It suits a selfless playstyle where the focus is on keeping everyone healthy rather than chasing or repairing solo.

S45P03.name: Shoulder the Burden
S45P03.description:
Once per trial, while you do not have 2 Hook States and are next to a hooked Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to unhook them:
  • They lose 1 Hook State.
  • You gain 1 Hook State.
  • You scream.
  • You gain Exposed for 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
Once per trial, while you do not have 2 Hook States and are next to a hooked Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to unhook them:
  • They lose 1 Hook State.
  • You gain 1 Hook State.
  • You scream.
  • You gain Exposed for 60s.

Once per trial, while you do not have 2 Hook States and are next to a hooked Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to unhook them:
  • They lose 1 Hook State.
  • You gain 1 Hook State.
  • You scream.
  • You gain Exposed for 50s.

Once per trial, while you do not have 2 Hook States and are next to a hooked Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to unhook them:
  • They lose 1 Hook State.
  • You gain 1 Hook State.
  • You scream.
  • You gain Exposed for 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: A once-per-trial ability that lets a healthy survivor standing next to a hooked survivor remove one hook state from them, transferring that state onto themselves instead. The action triggers a scream and grants the transferring survivor Exposed for a long period.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reducing a hooked survivor's hook states buys them more time to recover before being killed, which can be the difference between a rescue and a lost teammate. The trade-off of taking a hook state and a long Exposed window makes it a high-stakes, high-reward call.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays a rescue-heavy strategy and wants a backup plan for when a teammate gets hooked in a bad spot. It suits a survivor who is willing to take personal risk to keep a teammate alive past the hook.

S46P01.name: Do No Harm
S46P01.description:
While healing another Survivor:
  • For each Hook State they have, you heal 30/40/50% faster.
  • Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you gain 3% more progress.
descriptionTiers:
While healing another Survivor:
  • For each Hook State they have, you heal 30% faster.
  • Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you gain 3% more progress.

While healing another Survivor:
  • For each Hook State they have, you heal 40% faster.
  • Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you gain 3% more progress.

While healing another Survivor:
  • For each Hook State they have, you heal 50% faster.
  • Whenever you hit a great basic Skill Check, you gain 3% more progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Healing a survivor who already has one or more hook states makes the heal faster for each state they carry, and hitting great skill checks during the heal adds extra progress. The more injured the patient is, the more the heal speed increases.
beginner.whyItMatters: Hook states make a survivor harder to save, so speeding up the heal directly reduces the time a teammate spends in a vulnerable condition. It is a strong reward for taking on the risk of healing a survivor who is already in serious shape.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team expects to have survivors with hook states early and often, such as when playing against a killer who hooks frequently. It suits a dedicated healer who wants to feel effective even when the patient is in bad shape.

S46P02.name: Duty of Care
S46P02.description: While healthy, whenever you take a protection hit, other Survivors within 12m gain 25% Haste for 4/5/6s.
descriptionTiers: While healthy, whenever you take a protection hit, other Survivors within 12m gain 25% Haste for 4s.
While healthy, whenever you take a protection hit, other Survivors within 12m gain 25% Haste for 5s.
While healthy, whenever you take a protection hit, other Survivors within 12m gain 25% Haste for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: Taking a protection hit while healthy sends a burst of haste to every nearby survivor for a short duration. The perk only triggers on protection hits, not on direct hits taken while already injured.
beginner.whyItMatters: A sudden speed boost can help a nearby teammate reach a locker, a pallet, or a hook in time to avoid the next attack. It turns a single protection hit into a team-wide escape window, which is especially valuable in a tight chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays close together and wants a reliable escape tool that triggers on the killer's own aggression. It suits a survivor who expects to be in the middle of a chase and wants the whole group to get a speed bump.

S46P03.name: Rapid Response
S46P03.description:
Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, you gain Exhausted for 30/25/20s.

Whenever you gain Exhausted, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, you gain Exhausted for 30s.

Whenever you gain Exhausted, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s.

Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, you gain Exhausted for 25s.

Whenever you gain Exhausted, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s.

Whenever you fast-exit a Locker, you gain Exhausted for 20s.

Whenever you gain Exhausted, you see the Killer's Aura for 2s.

beginner.whatItIs: Fast-exiting a locker applies Exhausted to the survivor, which in turn reveals the killer's aura for a brief moment. The perk also triggers whenever Exhausted is gained from any other source.
beginner.whyItMatters: Locker escapes are high-risk moments where a survivor has no idea where the killer is, and a brief aura reveal closes that information gap. It turns a panicked vault into a slightly more informed one, which can prevent a second chase from starting immediately.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team relies on lockers as a primary escape tool and wants a small information bonus with every fast exit. It suits a survivor who plays a defensive, hide-and-sneak style rather than a high-chase, high-pallet style.

S47P01.name: Apocalyptic Ingenuity
S47P01.description:
After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while next to a Broken Pallet, use Active Ability button for 3s to create a Fragile Pallet.

Within 24/28/32m, you see the Auras of Broken Pallets.
descriptionTiers:
After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while next to a Broken Pallet, use Active Ability button for 3s to create a Fragile Pallet.

Within 24m, you see the Auras of Broken Pallets.

After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while next to a Broken Pallet, use Active Ability button for 3s to create a Fragile Pallet.

Within 28m, you see the Auras of Broken Pallets.

After you rummage or unlock 1 Chest, while next to a Broken Pallet, use Active Ability button for 3s to create a Fragile Pallet.

Within 32m, you see the Auras of Broken Pallets.

beginner.whatItIs: After unlocking a chest, standing next to a broken pallet lets the survivor channel an active ability to create a new fragile pallet in place. The perk also reveals the auras of all broken pallets within a wide range, making them easy to find.
beginner.whyItMatters: Creating new pallets on the fly gives the team fresh defensive options in areas that previously had none. The broken-pallet aura reveal also makes it easy to identify good loop spots, which is valuable for planning chase routes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays a map with few natural pallets in the areas they use most and wants to manufacture their own defensive cover. It suits a strategic survivor who thinks about where pallets will be needed before a chase starts.

S47P02.name: Come and Get Me!
S47P02.description:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to have injured and downed Survivors within 24m:
  • Make no Grunts of Pain for 10/12.5/15s.
  • Leave no Pools of Blood for 10/12.5/15s.
  • Leave no Scratch Marks for 10/12.5/15s.


You scream, then the Killer sees your Aura for 5s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you unhook a Survivor, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to have injured and downed Survivors within 24m:
  • Make no Grunts of Pain for 10s.
  • Leave no Pools of Blood for 10s.
  • Leave no Scratch Marks for 10s.


You scream, then the Killer sees your Aura for 5s.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to have injured and downed Survivors within 24m:
  • Make no Grunts of Pain for 12.5s.
  • Leave no Pools of Blood for 12.5s.
  • Leave no Scratch Marks for 12.5s.


You scream, then the Killer sees your Aura for 5s.

Whenever you unhook a Survivor, while crouched and idle, use Active Ability button to have injured and downed Survivors within 24m:
  • Make no Grunts of Pain for 15s.
  • Leave no Pools of Blood for 15s.
  • Leave no Scratch Marks for 15s.


You scream, then the Killer sees your Aura for 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Unhooking a survivor and then crouching down activates a silence field that mutes the pain grunts, blood pools, and scratch marks of every nearby injured or downed survivor for a set duration. The unhooker screams first, briefly revealing their own aura to the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: After a rescue the killer immediately knows where the team is, and the injured survivors' sounds make them easy to track. Silencing those sounds for a window gives the whole group a chance to scatter or regroup before the killer re-engages.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays a coordinated rescue style and wants a built-in safety net after every hook save. It suits a survivor who takes the lead on rescues and wants the whole group to disappear from the killer's senses for a critical moment.

S47P03.name: Teamwork: Toughen Up
S47P03.description:
While injured, whenever another Survivor within 24m of you blinds or Pallet-stuns the Killer, for 20/25/30s:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.
descriptionTiers:
While injured, whenever another Survivor within 24m of you blinds or Pallet-stuns the Killer, for 20s:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

While injured, whenever another Survivor within 24m of you blinds or Pallet-stuns the Killer, for 25s:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

While injured, whenever another Survivor within 24m of you blinds or Pallet-stuns the Killer, for 30s:
  • You make no Grunts of Pain.
  • You leave no Pools of Blood.
  • You leave no Scratch Marks.

beginner.whatItIs: While injured, any nearby teammate who blinds or pallet-stuns the killer triggers a silence effect on the injured survivor, removing their pain grunts, blood pools, and scratch marks for a set duration. The effect is passive and requires no button press.
beginner.whyItMatters: A silent injured survivor is a much harder target to find, which means the killer cannot simply follow sounds to close the distance. It rewards a team that actively stuns the killer while a teammate is down, turning aggression into a stealth bonus.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team plays together and at least one survivor is expected to get injured and stay in the fight. It suits a coordinated group that can keep the killer busy with stuns while the injured member hides and recovers.

S48P01.name: Conviction
S48P01.description:
After you finish healing 1 other Survivor, while downed with at least 25% recovery, use Active Ability button to recover instantly.

You gain Broken, then, after 20/25/30s, you are downed instantly.
descriptionTiers:
After you finish healing 1 other Survivor, while downed with at least 25% recovery, use Active Ability button to recover instantly.

You gain Broken, then, after 20s, you are downed instantly.

After you finish healing 1 other Survivor, while downed with at least 25% recovery, use Active Ability button to recover instantly.

You gain Broken, then, after 25s, you are downed instantly.

After you finish healing 1 other Survivor, while downed with at least 25% recovery, use Active Ability button to recover instantly.

You gain Broken, then, after 30s, you are downed instantly.

beginner.whatItIs: After healing one teammate, a downed survivor with meaningful recovery progress can use an active ability to recover instantly, gain Broken, and then go down again after a delay. The perk is a last-resort tool that converts a near-certain death into a temporary reprieve.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being instantly saved from a downed state keeps a survivor in the game long enough to contribute, even if only for a short window. The Broken state and the guaranteed re-down mean it is not a permanent save, but it buys enough time to reach a hook or a locker.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team wants a desperate last chance to keep a teammate alive, especially in situations where a rescue is not immediately possible. It suits a survivor who plays a support role and wants a dramatic final tool in the arsenal.

S48P02.name: Last Stand
S48P02.description: After hiding for 120/105/90s within the Killer's Terror Radius, when you fast-vault, once per trial, stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m.
descriptionTiers: After hiding for 120s within the Killer's Terror Radius, when you fast-vault, once per trial, stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m.
After hiding for 105s within the Killer's Terror Radius, when you fast-vault, once per trial, stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m.
After hiding for 90s within the Killer's Terror Radius, when you fast-vault, once per trial, stun the Killer for 3s if they are within 2.5m.

beginner.whatItIs: Hiding inside a killer's terror radius for a long stretch arms a one-time stun that triggers the moment the survivor fast-vaults, provided the killer is close enough. The stun is brief but can break a chase at the worst possible moment for the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: A stun from a vault is unexpected because the killer expects the survivor to be fleeing, not attacking. That split second of vulnerability can be enough to loop a pallet, reach a window, or simply put distance between the two.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the survivor expects to get caught in a chase and wants a single dramatic escape tool that rewards being close to the killer. It suits a patient survivor who is willing to hide in the open and wait for the perfect vault moment.

S48P03.name: Teamwork: Throw Down
S48P03.description:
Whenever you blind or Pallet-stun the Killer, for 6/8/10s, other injured Survivors within 24m:
  • Gain Endurance.
  • See the Killer's Aura.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you blind or Pallet-stun the Killer, for 6s, other injured Survivors within 24m:
  • Gain Endurance.
  • See the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you blind or Pallet-stun the Killer, for 8s, other injured Survivors within 24m:
  • Gain Endurance.
  • See the Killer's Aura.

Whenever you blind or Pallet-stun the Killer, for 10s, other injured Survivors within 24m:
  • Gain Endurance.
  • See the Killer's Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Blinding or pallet-stunning the killer triggers a team-wide effect that grants Endurance and reveals the killer's aura to every nearby injured survivor for a set duration. The effect requires no button press and triggers automatically on each successful stun or blind.
beginner.whyItMatters: Injured survivors are the most vulnerable members of the team, and giving them Endurance plus a clear view of the killer turns a dangerous moment into a survivable one. The aura reveal also helps them navigate away from the killer instead of running blindly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the team has at least one injured survivor who needs protection during a chase, and another teammate who is actively stalling the killer with blinds and pallets. It suits a coordinated group that divides the roles of stunner and protected clearly.

S49P01.name: Road Life
S49P01.description:
While injured, not Broken and repairing a Generator:
  • Whenever you hit a basic great Skill Check, you earn 1 Token.
  • Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 1 token.


When you have 6/5/4 Tokens, spend all Tokens to heal 100% faster until you stop healing.
descriptionTiers:
While injured, not Broken and repairing a Generator:
  • Whenever you hit a basic great Skill Check, you earn 1 Token.
  • Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 1 token.


When you have 6 Tokens, spend all Tokens to heal 100% faster until you stop healing.

While injured, not Broken and repairing a Generator:
  • Whenever you hit a basic great Skill Check, you earn 1 Token.
  • Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 1 token.


When you have 5 Tokens, spend all Tokens to heal 100% faster until you stop healing.

While injured, not Broken and repairing a Generator:
  • Whenever you hit a basic great Skill Check, you earn 1 Token.
  • Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, you lose 1 token.


When you have 4 Tokens, spend all Tokens to heal 100% faster until you stop healing.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk that tracks Skill Check performance while injured and repairing a Generator. Landed great checks build up a token pool, missed basic checks chip it away, and spending the whole pool grants a burst of accelerated healing.
beginner.whyItMatters: It turns the punishing situation of repairing while hurt into an opportunity, since the same button-mashing that usually risks a miss now pays out in faster healing. A survivor who would normally need a Med-Kit after a rough repair can instead keep working and come out the other side mended.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on an injured survivor who still wants to keep working generators, since the token economy only runs while that survivor is both hurt and at a generator. The payoff is best when the survivor moves between generators rather than sitting at one.

S49P02.name: ONE-TWO-THREE-FOUR!
S49P02.description:
While idle, use Active Ability button 2 to perform, empowering all Survivors within 16m for up to 15s. While you are performing, other Survivors will see your Aura. You get special Skill Checks during that time: while healing or repairing, basic Skill Checks are 20% more likely to appear.

If you complete the performance, the effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 110/100/90s.
descriptionTiers:
While idle, use Active Ability button 2 to perform, empowering all Survivors within 16m for up to 15s. While you are performing, other Survivors will see your Aura. You get special Skill Checks during that time: while healing or repairing, basic Skill Checks are 20% more likely to appear.

If you complete the performance, the effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 110s.

If you complete the performance, the effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 100s.

If you complete the performance, the effect ends after 90s. Cooldown: 90s.

beginner.whatItIs: An active ability that lets a survivor perform on stage while idle, empowering everyone nearby for a short window. During the performance, basic Skill Checks become more likely to appear when healing or repairing.
beginner.whyItMatters: A group of survivors huddled around one generator can stack the odds of clean checks, which reduces the chance of a miss that would alert the killer. Completing the performance extends the effect well beyond the initial window, making it a sustained team buff rather than a one-shot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the team wants a reliable repair boost at a central generator, since the performance only works while the user is standing still and idle. It comes from one specific survivor, so it is not a general Bloodweb slot.

S49P03.name: Ghost Notes
S49P03.description:
While you have Exhausted, your Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster.

You lose Exhausted 5/7.5/10% faster.
descriptionTiers:
While you have Exhausted, your Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster.

You lose Exhausted 5% faster.

While you have Exhausted, your Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster.

You lose Exhausted 7.5% faster.

While you have Exhausted, your Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster.

You lose Exhausted 10% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Stealth-focused and taught by the same character as Road Life, it accelerates the loss of Exhausted while the survivor is in that state. Scratch Marks on the ground also fade at a faster rate, shrinking the trail the killer can follow.
beginner.whyItMatters: Exhausted is the state that gives the killer a long, persistent track to follow, so shrinking its duration means the survivor loses that trail sooner. A survivor who just sprinted through the open can crouch briefly and watch the marks thin out, gaining a few more seconds of safety.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it for any build that relies on sprinting and hiding in quick succession, since the payoff is the gap between a burst of speed and the next moment of safety. The unlock is tied to a single survivor, not the general pool.

S50P01.name: Bada Bada Boom
S50P01.description:
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Window, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 40/50/60s. All Survivors see that Window's Aura for that time.

When the Killer vaults that Window, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 6s.
descriptionTiers:
After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Window, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 40s. All Survivors see that Window's Aura for that time.

When the Killer vaults that Window, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 6s.

After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Window, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 50s. All Survivors see that Window's Aura for that time.

When the Killer vaults that Window, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 6s.

After repairing 20% of Generators, while next to a Window, use Active Ability button 2 to trap it for 60s. All Survivors see that Window's Aura for that time.

When the Killer vaults that Window, the trap explodes and they gain 50% Hindered for 6s.

beginner.whatItIs: Trapping a window is the whole point: once enough generators are repaired, a survivor can place an explosive trap on a nearby Window. When the killer vaults that window, the trap detonates and slows them down briefly.
beginner.whyItMatters: A killer who relies on window vaults to cut corners or maintain chase momentum gets punished for taking the same route twice. Every survivor on the team sees the trapped window's Aura, so it doubles as shared map information for the whole group.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to a match where the killer keeps using the same window loop, since the trap only triggers on a vault of that specific window. One survivor character teaches it, so it will not appear in the shared Bloodweb.

S50P02.name: Change of Plan
S50P02.description:
When the trial starts, you earn 2 Tokens.

While hiding in a Locker and holding a non-event Toolbox, use Active Ability button 2 and spend 1 Token to transform your Toolbox and add-ons into a Med-Kit of the same rarity with 80/90/100% Charges and random add-ons of the same rarity.
descriptionTiers:
When the trial starts, you earn 2 Tokens.

While hiding in a Locker and holding a non-event Toolbox, use Active Ability button 2 and spend 1 Token to transform your Toolbox and add-ons into a Med-Kit of the same rarity with 80% Charges and random add-ons of the same rarity.

When the trial starts, you earn 2 Tokens.

While hiding in a Locker and holding a non-event Toolbox, use Active Ability button 2 and spend 1 Token to transform your Toolbox and add-ons into a Med-Kit of the same rarity with 90% Charges and random add-ons of the same rarity.
