While hiding in a Locker and holding a non-event Toolbox, use Active Ability button 2 and spend 1 Token to transform your Toolbox and add-ons into a Med-Kit of the same rarity with 100% Charges and random add-ons of the same rarity.

beginner.whatItIs: Dustin Henderson teaches a swap that happens inside a Locker. Holding an ordinary Toolbox and spending one of the tokens the trial handed over turns it, add-ons and all, into a Med-Kit of matching rarity. The replacement arrives charged and carries fresh add-ons of that same rarity.
beginner.whyItMatters: A Toolbox that would sit in a Locker doing nothing becomes a Med-Kit that can save a teammate at the critical moment, which is a big deal when the team is short on healing items. The rarity match means a Rare Toolbox becomes a Rare Med-Kit, preserving the add-on value.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it if the survivor wants flexibility in item roles, since the conversion only works from a Locker and only while holding a non-event Toolbox. It is tied to one survivor's character slot.

S50P03.name: Teamwork: Full Circuit
S50P03.description:
For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, good basic Skill Check zones are 15/20/25% bigger.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.
descriptionTiers:
For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, good basic Skill Check zones are 15% bigger.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, good basic Skill Check zones are 20% bigger.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, good basic Skill Check zones are 25% bigger.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: A teamwork perk that widens the good-check zones on a generator for every other survivor repairing alongside the user. The repair speed itself also gets a small boost whenever at least one other survivor is working the same generator.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two survivors at one generator is a classic setup, and this makes that setup more forgiving by making it easier to land clean checks. The faster repair speed on top means the generator finishes sooner, which frees a survivor to move to the next one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it in a coordinated team where survivors plan to work generators in pairs, since the bonus scales with the number of people on the same generator. The unlock belongs to a single survivor, not the general tree.

S51P01.name: Extrasensory Perception
S51P01.description:
After crouching for 4s:
  • You see Auras in an expanding radius up to 44m.
  • You gain Elusive.
  • You gain Oblivious.


When you stop crouching, or after 11s, cooldown: 60/50/40s.
descriptionTiers:
After crouching for 4s:
  • You see Auras in an expanding radius up to 44m.
  • You gain Elusive.
  • You gain Oblivious.


When you stop crouching, or after 11s, cooldown: 60s.

After crouching for 4s:
  • You see Auras in an expanding radius up to 44m.
  • You gain Elusive.
  • You gain Oblivious.


When you stop crouching, or after 11s, cooldown: 50s.

After crouching for 4s:
  • You see Auras in an expanding radius up to 44m.
  • You gain Elusive.
  • You gain Oblivious.


When you stop crouching, or after 11s, cooldown: 40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Crouching long enough unlocks a wide Aura scan that reveals nearby entities in an expanding radius. The survivor also gains Elusive and Oblivious while crouched, making them harder to track and less detectable to the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: A survivor who is spotted mid-crouch gets a moment to pop up and reposition, but this flips the script: the survivor sees the killer and nearby totems or hooks while the killer sees less of them. The Oblivious effect means the killer's own detection tools become less reliable during that window.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a stealth-oriented build that already plans to crouch often, since the cooldown is the main limiting factor. Only one survivor character teaches it, so it sits in their personal Bloodweb.

S51P02.name: We See You
S51P02.description:
Whenever the Killer sees your Aura, you earn 1 Token. Cooldown: 10s.

When you have 4 Tokens, spend them all. Then, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 10/12.5/15s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Killer sees your Aura, you earn 1 Token. Cooldown: 10s.

When you have 4 Tokens, spend them all. Then, all Survivors see the Killer's Aura for 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: A token-based reveal that turns being spotted into an advantage. Every time the killer sees the survivor's Aura, a token is earned, and spending the full pool grants every survivor a clear look at the killer's position for a short window.
beginner.whyItMatters: Being seen is usually a bad thing, but here it becomes fuel for information. A survivor who gets spotted near a generator can feed the team a window where the killer's Aura is visible, which helps teammates make safer decisions about when to hide or move.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who will be out in the open working generators, since the tokens only build when the killer actually sees the user. It lives in one survivor's personal Bloodweb.

S51P03.name: Teamwork: Soft-Spoken
S51P03.description:
For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, the range of Generator repair noises is 15/20/25% smaller.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.
descriptionTiers:
For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, the range of Generator repair noises is 15% smaller.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, the range of Generator repair noises is 20% smaller.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, the range of Generator repair noises is 25% smaller.

While repairing with at least 1 other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk that tightens how far Generator repair noise carries whenever another survivor is working the same machine in parallel. Repair speed also gets a small boost while at least two survivors are at the generator together.
beginner.whyItMatters: Repair noise is one of the killer's main ways to find survivors, so reducing its range gives the team a quiet window to work without constantly worrying about the killer's direction. Two survivors working together benefit more than one working alone, which rewards coordinated play.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it in a team that plans to split generators into pairs, since the noise reduction only applies while another survivor is repairing alongside the user. The unlock is specific to one survivor.

S52P01.name: Flow State
S52P01.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token:
  • You bless and cleanse 8/9/10% faster.
  • You heal 8/9/10% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 8/9/10% faster.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed, earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token:
  • You bless and cleanse 8% faster.
  • You heal 8% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 8% faster.

Whenever a Generator is completed, earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token:
  • You bless and cleanse 9% faster.
  • You heal 9% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 9% faster.

Whenever a Generator is completed, earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token:
  • You bless and cleanse 10% faster.
  • You heal 10% faster.
  • You unhook Survivors 10% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Every completed Generator earns a token for the survivor who holds it. Each token in the pool accelerates blessing, cleansing, healing, and unhooking, so the more generators the team finishes, the faster those actions become.
beginner.whyItMatters: A team that keeps generators going all night stacks these tokens without having to do anything extra, and the payoff shows up in faster heals, quicker totem cleanses, and shorter unhook times. It is a passive, no-button perk that rewards consistent generator work.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the survivor in question handles a lot of healing, totem blessing, or unhooking work, because each token only lands when a generator finishes. One survivor character teaches it.

S52P02.name: A Place For Us
S52P02.description:
While healing another Survivor, you both gain Elusive.

Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, you both gain Elusive for 20/25/30s.

When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.
descriptionTiers:
While healing another Survivor, you both gain Elusive.

Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, you both gain Elusive for 20s.

When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

While healing another Survivor, you both gain Elusive.

Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, you both gain Elusive for 25s.

When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

While healing another Survivor, you both gain Elusive.

Whenever you finish healing the Obsession, you both gain Elusive for 30s.

When the trial starts, you are less likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Healing-focused, it grants both the healer and the patient Elusive while the heal is in progress. Finishing a heal on the Obsession extends that stealth bonus for a longer window afterward, and the survivor who holds it is less likely to be chosen as the Obsession at trial start.
beginner.whyItMatters: Elusive makes a survivor harder for the killer to track, so both parties benefit from the safety during the most vulnerable moment of a trial. The reduced Obsession chance at trial start is a quiet but valuable head start, since being the Obsession means the killer has a strong reason to prioritize that survivor.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it on a survivor who will be the team's primary healer, since the Obsession-stealing effect at trial start and the post-heal stealth window both reward someone who heals often. It is tied to that one character's Bloodweb.

S52P03.name: Five Moves Ahead
S52P03.description:
While you are in the Killer's Terror Radius or chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Auras of the 5 closest Pallets and Windows.
  • After you drop a Pallet, you start moving 50% earlier.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, cooldown: 40/35/30s.
descriptionTiers:
While you are in the Killer's Terror Radius or chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Auras of the 5 closest Pallets and Windows.
  • After you drop a Pallet, you start moving 50% earlier.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, cooldown: 40s.

While you are in the Killer's Terror Radius or chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Auras of the 5 closest Pallets and Windows.
  • After you drop a Pallet, you start moving 50% earlier.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, cooldown: 35s.

While you are in the Killer's Terror Radius or chased by the Killer:
  • You see the Auras of the 5 closest Pallets and Windows.
  • After you drop a Pallet, you start moving 50% earlier.
  • Whenever you drop a Pallet, cooldown: 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: Chase visibility is the entire point: while in the killer's Terror Radius or being chased, the survivor sees the Auras of nearby Pallets and Windows. Dropping a pallet also lets the survivor start moving sooner, giving a head start before the pallet fully drops.
beginner.whyItMatters: Panic in a chase usually means a survivor vaults the wrong direction or fumbles a pallet, and this removes the guesswork by showing exactly where the escape options are. The earlier movement after dropping a pallet can be the difference between a clean escape and getting cornered on the other side.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who struggles with chase navigation or tends to freeze when the killer closes in, since the visibility bonus only activates during a chase or in the Terror Radius. The unlock belongs to one specific survivor.

S53P01.name: Wide Open Throttle
S53P01.description:
Whenever you fast-vault a Pallet:
  • You gain 10/12.5/15% Haste for 3s.
  • The Pallet is reset, blocked for 60s, and all Survivors see its Aura for that time.


Cooldown: 60s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you fast-vault a Pallet:
  • You gain 10% Haste for 3s.
  • The Pallet is reset, blocked for 60s, and all Survivors see its Aura for that time.


Cooldown: 60s.

Whenever you fast-vault a Pallet:
  • You gain 12.5% Haste for 3s.
  • The Pallet is reset, blocked for 60s, and all Survivors see its Aura for that time.


Cooldown: 60s.

Whenever you fast-vault a Pallet:
  • You gain 15% Haste for 3s.
  • The Pallet is reset, blocked for 60s, and all Survivors see its Aura for that time.


Cooldown: 60s.

beginner.whatItIs: Fast-vaulting a pallet is the trigger for everything here. The survivor gains a burst of speed, the pallet resets and blocks for a window, and every survivor on the team sees its Aura during that time.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed burst can carry a survivor through a dangerous tile or across open ground in the split second after a vault, and the blocked pallet denies the killer a chase tool. The team-wide Aura visibility means everyone knows where that pallet is, which helps with coordination.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to a build that already favors fast vaults as an escape route, since the whole payoff depends on vaulting a pallet at speed. One survivor character is the teacher.

S53P02.name: Lend a Hand
S53P02.description: Whenever you bless or cleanse 1 Totem, while healing another Survivor and only once per Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to give them 2/3/4 permanent healing charges.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you bless or cleanse 1 Totem, while healing another Survivor and only once per Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to give them 2 permanent healing charges.
Whenever you bless or cleanse 1 Totem, while healing another Survivor and only once per Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to give them 3 permanent healing charges.
Whenever you bless or cleanse 1 Totem, while healing another Survivor and only once per Survivor, use Active Ability button 2 to give them 4 permanent healing charges.

beginner.whatItIs: Clearing a Totem is the setup that arms the ability. While healing a teammate afterward, a button press hands out a one-time stack of permanent healing charges for that specific survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: Permanent healing charges are rare in a trial, and getting them from a Totem interaction rather than an item drop is a meaningful advantage. The one-time-per-survivor limit means it is a targeted gift, not a team-wide buff, so timing the heal matters.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Pick a survivor who will clear totems and also do healing work, since both conditions must line up before the button becomes ready. It is a personal unlock tied to one survivor character.

S53P03.name: Cross-Examination
S53P03.description: While in the Killer's Terror Radius and not being chased by the Killer, they leave Light Marks that last for 10s that you can see. While on the Killer's Light Marks, you gain Elusive. This ends after 3/4/5s.
descriptionTiers: While in the Killer's Terror Radius and not being chased by the Killer, they leave Light Marks that last for 10s that you can see. While on the Killer's Light Marks, you gain Elusive. This ends after 3s.

While in the Killer's Terror Radius and not being chased by the Killer, they leave Light Marks that last for 10s that you can see. While on the Killer's Light Marks, you gain Elusive. This ends after 4s.

While in the Killer's Terror Radius and not being chased by the Killer, they leave Light Marks that last for 10s that you can see. While on the Killer's Light Marks, you gain Elusive. This ends after 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Inside the killer's Terror Radius while not actively being chased, the killer drops visible Light Marks on the ground. Standing on those marks grants Elusive for a short window before they fade.
beginner.whyItMatters: The killer's own tracking tool becomes the survivor's hiding spot, which is a neat reversal that works in the moments right before a chase starts. Elusive makes the survivor harder to lock onto, so a well-timed crouch-and-stand-on-marks sequence can break a killer's focus.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it for a stealth-heavy build that plans to crouch near the killer's path rather than running, since the effect only works while in the Terror Radius and not being chased. The character who teaches it is a single survivor.

S54P01.name: Fruits of Your Labor
S54P01.description:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you finish repairing a Generator, for each Token:
  • You gain 5% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain 10/15/20% healing progress.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you finish repairing a Generator, for each Token:
  • You gain 5% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain 10% healing progress.

Whenever a Generator is completed, you earn 1 Token.

Whenever you finish repairing a Generator, for each Token:

  • You gain 15% healing progress.

Whenever you finish repairing a Generator, for each Token:

  • You gain 20% healing progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Each generator the team completes adds a token to a personal pool. The moment a survivor finishes their own repair, every token held grants a brief speed boost and a portion of healing progress.
beginner.whyItMatters: The speed burst is useful for the instant after a generator finishes, when a survivor needs to cross open ground to reach safety. The healing progress is a quiet but reliable source of mending that stacks with every generator, so a survivor who works several will feel the difference by the end of the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Give it to a survivor who plans to finish a good number of generators themselves, since the tokens only accumulate as the team completes them. One survivor character teaches it.

S54P02.name: Salvation's Cry
S54P02.description:
Whenever the Killer starts chasing you:
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors for 1/2/3s.
  • Survivors not being chased see your Aura for 5s.
  • Survivors not being chased see the Killer's Aura for 5s.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever the Killer starts chasing you:
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors for 1s.
  • Survivors not being chased see your Aura for 5s.
  • Survivors not being chased see the Killer's Aura for 5s.

Whenever the Killer starts chasing you:
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors for 2s.
  • Survivors not being chased see your Aura for 5s.
  • Survivors not being chased see the Killer's Aura for 5s.

Whenever the Killer starts chasing you:
  • You see the Auras of other Survivors for 3s.
  • Survivors not being chased see your Aura for 5s.
  • Survivors not being chased see the Killer's Aura for 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: The moment a chase starts, the survivor being chased briefly reveals their own Aura to teammates who are not in danger. Those unchased survivors also get a short window to see the killer's Aura, giving the team a snapshot of where everyone is.
beginner.whyItMatters: That split-second of information lets a teammate decide whether to run, hide, or set a trap before the chase reaches them. It also helps the team keep track of who is in danger and where the killer is heading, which is crucial in the chaotic early seconds of a chase.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to a team that values shared awareness over individual stealth, since the effect triggers the instant a chase begins and requires no button press. The unlock is personal to one survivor.

S54P03.name: Boon: Steadfast
S54P03.description:
While next to a Totem, use Active Ability button to bless it, creating a unique Boon Totem that combines all your Boons.

Generators within the Boon's range:
  • Regress 50% slower.
  • Survivors repair them 8/9/10% faster.


Survivors within the Boon's range see the Auras of affected Generators.

Survivors within the Boon's range see the Auras of affected Generators.

Survivors within the Boon's range see the Auras of affected Generators.

Generators within the Boon's range:
  • Regress 50% slower.
  • Survivors repair them 10% faster.


Survivors within the Boon's range see the Auras of affected Generators.

beginner.whatItIs: Blessing a Totem next to it merges all of the survivor's Boons into a single combined Boon Totem with a wider effect. Generators within range regenerate damage more slowly, repair faster, and their Auras are visible to any survivor inside the Boon's radius.
beginner.whyItMatters: A single totem carrying multiple Boon effects is far more efficient than three separate totems, since the survivor only needs to place one. The slower regression and faster repair make the generators inside the radius feel noticeably more stable, and the Aura visibility helps the team spot which ones are affected.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who already runs multiple Boons, since the whole value comes from combining them into one. The unlock is specific to that character.

Saboteur.name: Saboteur
Saboteur.description:
Within 56m of where another Survivor was picked-up by the Killer and is being carried, you see the Auras of Hooks and Scourge Hooks.

You can sabotage Hooks. Cooldown: 70/65/60s.
descriptionTiers:

Within 56m of where another Survivor was picked-up by the Killer and is being carried, you see the Auras of Hooks and Scourge Hooks.

beginner.whatItIs: Taught by Jake, it reveals the Auras of Hooks and Scourge Hooks when another survivor has been picked up and is being carried nearby. The survivor can also sabotage a Hook to break up the rescue attempt.
beginner.whyItMatters: A killer who parks a survivor on a hook and waits for the rescue window to close gets that window interrupted, which can save the whole team from a lost teammate. The wide Aura visibility means the team can also coordinate around the hook location in real time.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it to a team that values rescue attempts and hook play, since the sabotage ability and the hook visibility both center on that moment. Jake teaches it, making it a personal character unlock.

Save_The_Best_For_Last.name: Save the best for last
Save_The_Best_For_Last.description:
Whenever you damage a Survivor who is not the Obsession with a basic-attack, you earn 1 Token, up to 6/7/8.

For each Token, your basic-attack cooldown are 5% shorter.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, lose 2 Tokens.

While the Obsession is dead, you cannot earn Tokens.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you damage a Survivor who is not the Obsession with a basic-attack, you earn 1 Token, up to 6.

For each Token, your basic-attack cooldown are 5% shorter.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, lose 2 Tokens.

While the Obsession is dead, you cannot earn Tokens.

Whenever you damage a Survivor who is not the Obsession with a basic-attack, you earn 1 Token, up to 7.

For each Token, your basic-attack cooldown are 5% shorter.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, lose 2 Tokens.

While the Obsession is dead, you cannot earn Tokens.

For each Token, your basic-attack cooldown are 5% shorter.

Whenever the Obsession takes damage, lose 2 Tokens.

While the Obsession is dead, you cannot earn Tokens.

beginner.whatItIs: Damaging non-Obsession survivors with basic attacks builds a token pool for the killer who holds it. Each token in that pool shortens the basic-attack cooldown, so the more the killer juggles between targets, the faster their attacks recover.
beginner.whyItMatters: A killer who is juggling multiple survivors and taking out the easier targets first can stack these tokens while the Obsession is still healing or repairing. The moment the Obsession takes damage, tokens are lost, which forces the killer to choose between focusing the priority target and building up cooldown reduction.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer build that spreads damage across the group rather than locking onto one target, since the tokens only build from non-Obsession hits. Shape teaches it, so it is a personal killer unlock.

SecondWind.name: Second Wind
SecondWind.description:
After you heal 1 Survivor, while not Broken, when you are unhooked, you gain Broken.

After 28/24/20s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.
descriptionTiers:
After you heal 1 Survivor, while not Broken, when you are unhooked, you gain Broken.

After 28s, if you are not downed, you are instantly healed.

beginner.whatItIs: Survivor perk taught by Steve that belongs to the adaptation category. Once active, after healing one other survivor, the holder gains Broken when unhooked, and after a short delay, if not downed, they are instantly healed.
beginner.whyItMatters: The recovery window turns a hook save into a potential full heal without needing a teammate nearby. This is especially valuable in lobbies where the healer is stretched thin across multiple injured survivors.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who often ends up hooked or who plays in a lobby without reliable hook support. Steve teaches it, so it pairs naturally with a build focused on surviving multiple hookings.

Self_Care.name: Self-Care
Self_Care.description: You can heal yourself, but 75/70/65% slower.
descriptionTiers: You can heal yourself, but 75% slower.
You can heal yourself, but 70% slower.
You can heal yourself, but 65% slower.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk from Claudette in the adaptation category. It lets the holder heal their own wounds, though at a noticeably slower rate than healing another survivor.
beginner.whyItMatters: Making a survivor less dependent on teammates for healing is especially useful when the group is spread thin across the map. A slow self-heal is still better than standing still and waiting for someone to arrive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when a trial will have long stretches away from allies and a self-heal option feels essential. Claudette teaches it, which pairs well with a build that leans on independence rather than relying on teammates for recovery.

SelfSufficient.name: Unbreakable
SelfSufficient.description:
Once per trial, while downed by the Killer, you can fully recover.

While downed, you recover 25/30/35% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Bill teaches a survivor perk in the adaptation category. Once per trial, a downed survivor can fully recover on their own, and the crawl-to-safety recovery also runs noticeably faster than normal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Removing the total dependence on another survivor for a hook save keeps the team's health pool more stable. A survivor who can self-recover from being downed is much harder to pin down in a prolonged trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who plays independently or in a lobby where teammate hook saves are unreliable. Bill is the teacher, so it fits naturally into a build that values self-reliance over coordination.

Shadowborn.name: Shadowborn
Shadowborn.description: Whenever you are blinded, gain 6/8/10% Haste for 10s.
descriptionTiers: Whenever you are blinded, gain 6% Haste for 10s.
Whenever you are blinded, gain 8% Haste for 10s.
Whenever you are blinded, gain 10% Haste for 10s.

beginner.whatItIs: The Wraith's killer perk grants a short burst of extra movement speed every time the killer is blinded by a light source. The boost turns a survivor's flashlight save attempt into an opening for the killer to close distance instead.
beginner.whyItMatters: Turning a defensive survivor action into a killer advantage rewards killers who can push through well-lit generators without hesitation. The speed boost helps close the gap that blinding would otherwise create.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on The Wraith when the plan is to push through generator lights and chase aggressively. Every failed blind against the killer becomes a small speed reward instead of a setback, so it favors an aggressive, close-quarters playstyle.

Slippery_Meat.name: Slippery Meat
Slippery_Meat.description: You can attempt to unhook yourself up to 6 times and have 2/3/4% more chance to succeed.
descriptionTiers: You can attempt to unhook yourself up to 6 times and have 2% more chance to succeed.
You can attempt to unhook yourself up to 6 times and have 3% more chance to succeed.

beginner.whatItIs: General survivor perk available to every survivor. It lets the holder attempt to unhook themselves from the hook a limited number of times, with a small boost to the success chance per attempt.
beginner.whyItMatters: Giving a hooked survivor a self-rescue option removes the total dependence on a teammate arriving in time. Even a modest success chance is better than sitting on the hook and waiting for help that may not come.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into any build that needs a way to claw back from the hook without waiting on a teammate. Since every survivor can unlock it, it works as a safety net for anyone who finds themselves hooked early and far from help.

Sloppy_Butcher.name: Sloppy Butcher
Sloppy_Butcher.description:
Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack:
  • They gain Hemorrhage for 70/80/90s.
  • They gain Mangled for 70/80/90s.


Survivors with Hemorrhage lose healing progress 25% faster.
descriptionTiers:
Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack:

Survivors with Hemorrhage lose healing progress 25% faster.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack:
  • They gain Hemorrhage for 80s.

Survivors with Hemorrhage lose healing progress 25% faster.

Whenever you damage a Survivor with a basic-attack:
  • They gain Hemorrhage for 90s.
  • They gain Mangled for 90s.


Survivors with Hemorrhage lose healing progress 25% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Killer perk that is general to all killers and belongs to the cruelty category. Whenever a basic attack damages a survivor, that survivor gains Hemorrhage and Mangled, and any survivor carrying Hemorrhage also loses healing progress at a faster rate.
beginner.whyItMatters: Punishing survivors who try to heal after taking a basic hit makes recovery slower and more fragile for the whole team. The compounding effect of Hemorrhage and Mangled together makes even a single basic hit feel heavier than it should.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer build focused on stretching out survivor recovery and punishing healing attempts. It is available to every killer, so it slots into any build that wants to pressure the healing side of the game.

Small_Game.name: Small Game
Small_Game.description:
Within 8/10/12m of you, whenever you look at a Totem in a 45 degree cone, you hear a sound cue. Cooldown: 14/12/10s.

Whenever a Survivor cleanses a Totem, you earn 1 Token, up to 5.

For each Token, the cone is 5 degrees smaller.

Within 10m of you, whenever you look at a Totem in a 45 degree cone, you hear a sound cue. Cooldown: 12s.

For each Token, the cone is 5 degrees smaller.

beginner.whatItIs: A general survivor perk in the perception category. It plays a sound cue when a Totem falls inside a narrow vision cone around the holder, and each Totem cleansed shrinks that cone further.
beginner.whyItMatters: Helping survivors locate totems more precisely reduces wasted time sweeping the map for hidden objectives. The shrinking cone rewards consistent totem cleansing and makes late-trial totem hunting more efficient.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor whose role includes cleansing totems quickly, especially in maps with many totem spawns. It is available to every survivor, so it pairs well with any build that values objective awareness.

SoleSurvivor.name: Sole Survivor
SoleSurvivor.description:
Whenever a Survivor dies, you earn 1 Token.

For each Token, within 20/22/24m, the Killer cannot see your Aura.

When all other Survivors are dead:
  • You repair 75% faster.
  • You open Exit Gates and the Hatch 50% faster.


When the trial starts, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Laurie Strode's survivor perk rewards the holder with a stack of protection for every teammate who dies in the trial - each death makes the holder's own aura harder for the killer to see within a modest range. Once every other survivor is down, the last one standing repairs and works the gates or the hatch dramatically faster, though they start the match more likely to be singled out as the Obsession.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rewarding a lone survivor with both stealth and speed turns a lost lobby into a viable solo escape attempt. The increased likelihood of being the Obsession at start is a trade-off, but the mid-to-late trial bonuses make the position far more survivable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who is comfortable playing solo late in the trial and wants to convert a losing situation into a chance. Laurie teaches it, so it fits a build that is okay with early exposure in exchange for late-trial power.

Solidarity.name: Solidarity
Solidarity.description: While injured and healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit, you also gain healing progress at 50/60/70% speed.

beginner.whatItIs: Jane teaches a survivor perk that lets the holder heal themselves at a reduced rate while patching up a teammate, but only when they are injured and not using a Med-Kit. It turns the act of supporting someone else into a chance to recover personal health at the same time.
beginner.whyItMatters: Letting an injured survivor contribute to healing without fully stopping their own recovery keeps the team's health pool more stable. It removes the all-or-nothing choice between healing yourself or healing a teammate.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a survivor who often heals while still injured and wants to avoid a long solo patch-up afterward. Jane teaches it, so it suits a build that values keeping the whole team mobile and healthy.

SoulGuard.name: Soul Guard
SoulGuard.description:
While hexed, you can fully recover.

Whenever you fully recover, you gain Endurance for 4/6/8s. Cooldown: 30s.

beginner.whatItIs: A survivor perk from a specific character that lets the holder shake a hex by fully recovering on their own. Every recovery also grants a short window of Endurance to keep running, after which a cooldown must reset before it can trigger again.
beginner.whyItMatters: Giving a hexed survivor a reliable path back to full health removes the usual pressure to find a healer or wait out the hex. The Endurance burst adds a brief escape window that can carry the survivor to safety.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing solo or in a small lobby where a hexed survivor cannot count on a teammate to cleanse the curse quickly. It fits a self-reliant build that prefers to break free of hexes on its own rather than waiting for help.

Spies_From_The_Shadows.name: Spies from the Shadows
Spies_From_The_Shadows.description: Whenever a Survivor scares a Crow within 20/28/36m of you, you are alerted. Cooldown: 5s.

beginner.whatItIs: Gives the killer a warning signal whenever a nearby Crow is startled by a survivor's movement. A short cooldown separates each alert, so the signal stays useful even in areas thick with Crows. It is a general perk any killer can unlock from the Bloodweb, and it sits in the tracking category.
beginner.whyItMatters: Giving the killer a cheap and passive way to track survivor movement reduces the need to rely on audio cues or direct vision. The alert is quiet and consistent, making it a steady source of information throughout the trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Slot it into any killer build that wants passive positional awareness without spending an action to check. Because every killer can unlock it, it pairs well with styles that already rely on sound and environmental cues to track the pack.

beginner.whyItMatters: Turning being spotted from a distance into a minor mechanical advantage rewards survivors who can keep working while the killer watches. The small speed bonus on repair, healing, and other actions adds up over a long trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the trial has entered its final stretch and the killer is actively watching the action unfold. Every survivor can unlock it, which makes it a flexible slot for any build that benefits from small consistent speed bonuses under pressure.

beginner.whatItIs: Spirit teaches a killer perk in the chasing category. After breaking a set number of Pallets, the next time the killer is stunned by a Pallet, that Pallet is destroyed instead of merely damaged.
beginner.whyItMatters: Reducing the number of usable Pallets over the course of the trial makes chase loops tighter and less forgiving for survivors. The gradual destruction of Pallets shifts the map's geometry in the killer's favor as the trial wears on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on a killer build that relies on Pallet loops to win chases and wants to slowly strip that resource away. Spirit teaches it, so it suits a killer who already plays around Pallets as part of their chase strategy.

Sprint_Burst.name: Sprint Burst

  • You gain 50% Haste for 2s.
  • You gain Exhausted for 60/50/40s.

beginner.whatItIs: Meg teaches a survivor perk in the navigation category. The moment the holder starts running from a stationary or walking state, they gain a brief speed boost but also carry the Exhausted condition for a set duration.
beginner.whyItMatters: A one-shot burst of distance can put real space between a survivor and the killer's terror radius before a chase even begins. The Exhausted penalty afterward means the burst cannot be spammed, so timing matters a lot.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Save the burst for a genuinely dangerous moment, such as a chase where a hit would end the round, rather than for routine map traversal. Meg teaches it and the long Exhausted window that follows means it should stay in reserve until the situation truly demands a fast exit.

StakeOut.name: Stake Out
StakeOut.description:
After hiding for 15s within the Killer's Terror Radius, you earn 1 Token, up to 2/3/4.

Whenever you hit a good basic Skill Check, spend 1 Token:
  • The good Skill Check becomes a great Skill Check.
  • You gain 1% more progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Detective Tapp's survivor perk builds up tokens while the holder hides inside the killer's terror radius. Each token can be spent to upgrade a good skill check result into a great one, along with a small extra bump in progress.
beginner.whyItMatters: Rewarding survivors who use the killer's approach as cover for repositioning turns a defensive moment into a productive one. The small progress boost on upgraded Skill Checks adds up over many generator interactions in a long trial.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the build favors patient, crouched play near active generators and wants to convert quiet moments into a stronger skill check result, since Detective Tapp teaches this perk. It suits a survivor who prefers steady, calculated progress over frantic last-second sprints.

Streetwise.name: Streetwise
Streetwise.description:
The first time you deplete an item's Charges, you see the Killer's Aura for 8s.

Whenever you loot an item from a Chest, it has 60/70/80% more Charges.
descriptionTiers:

beginner.whatItIs: Nea teaches a survivor perk in the support category. The first time the holder depletes an item's Charges, they see the killer's Aura for a short window, and items looted from Chests arrive with extra Charges.
beginner.whyItMatters: Stretching the usefulness of looted items makes every Chest open feel more valuable. The one-time burst of killer awareness at the moment of depletion gives a natural decision point for repositioning or committing to an action.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the build already revolves around item utility, since the extended charges stretch each tool further. Nea teaches it, and the brief killer Aura reveal after the first depletion makes it a strong pick for survivors who play around chests and want a moment of awareness when it matters most.

Stridor.name: Stridor
Stridor.description: Survivors' breathing noises are 15/20/25% louder and their Grunts of Pain are 30/40/50% louder.

beginner.whatItIs: Nurse teaches a killer perk in the tracking category. Survivors' breathing sounds and Grunts of Pain are amplified, making them easier to hear from further away.
beginner.whyItMatters: Extending the killer's audio range over survivors turns quiet moments into usable positional information. The amplified Grunts of Pain are especially useful for confirming a down or a chase from outside the immediate area.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the killer build hunts by sound and the map has short lines of sight that make visual tracking unreliable. Nurse teaches it, which makes it a natural companion for any style that already reads breathing cues and pain grunts to close the gap.

Surge.name: Surge

beginner.whatItIs: Demogorgon teaches a killer perk in the obstruction category. Downing a survivor with a basic attack causes nearby generators to explode, lose some progress, and begin regressing, while the survivor repairing them screams.
beginner.whyItMatters: Creating a strong incentive for survivors to avoid repairing right next to where the killer is actively hunting changes how the map plays. The regression and the scream together make a down feel like a map-wide event rather than a local one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the trial features aggressive generator camping and the kill plan revolves around high-pressure chases that leave survivors scrambling. Demogorgon teaches it, making it a strong pick for a killer who already controls the map through relentless pursuit and punishes hesitation.

Surveillance.name: Surveillance

You see the Auras of regressing Generators.

beginner.whatItIs: Pig teaches a killer perk that keeps the Aura of any regressing generator visible at all times, then holds that visibility for a short window once the sabotage ends. Repair noises also carry further, giving the killer an extra audio clue to locate active work.
beginner.whyItMatters: Giving the killer continuous awareness of sabotage pressure without needing to be near the generator removes a major information gap. The extended repair audio helps track active repair from a distance, making it harder for survivors to work unnoticed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when the kill plan is built around managing multiple generators and the killer needs to track which ones are regressing without constantly repositioning. Pig teaches it, so it pairs well with a controlling style that reads the board from a distance and reacts to repair noise.

Technician.name: Technician
Technician.description:
While repairing a Generator:
  • The range of Generator repair noises is 16m shorter.
  • Whenever you miss a basic Skill Check, the Generator does not explode, but loses 4/3/2% more progress.

beginner.whatItIs: Feng teaches a survivor perk in the concealment and strategy categories. While repairing, the sound radius of the repair noise is reduced, and missing a Skill Check causes extra progress loss instead of an explosion.
beginner.whyItMatters: Making a survivor's generator work quieter lowers the audio footprint that the killer can use to track them. Turning a bad Skill Check into a slow-down rather than a full reset removes the spike of frustration that a reset causes.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it on any survivor lineup that favors cautious, extended generator work where even a bad check still leaves the machine standing. Feng is the character who hands out Technician, so slot it into any build that prizes keeping generators alive over racing them to completion.

Tenacity.name: Tenacity
Tenacity.description:
While downed:
  • You gain 30/40/50% Haste.
  • You can crawl and recover at the same time.
  • Your Grunts of Pain are 75% quieter.
  • The Killer cannot see your Aura.

beginner.whatItIs: Detective Tapp's survivor perk that stays active while downed. It speeds up crawling, allows recovery to continue while crawling, quiets grunts of pain, and hides the downed survivor's aura from the killer.
beginner.whyItMatters: The downed state is the most exposed moment in a match because a survivor is slow, loud, and visible to the killer. It compresses all of that risk into a single window where crawling, healing, and stealth improve at once, making it harder for the killer to read where the next hook should land.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Detective Tapp or when a build needs a downed-state survival tool, especially against killers with strong chase setups where every moment of crawl time matters. It pairs well with stealth-oriented builds because quieter grunts reduce the sound cue a killer would otherwise use to track a crawling survivor.

TerritorialImperative.name: Territorial Imperative
TerritorialImperative.description: Whenever a Survivor enters the Basement while you are 24m away from it, you see their Aura for 4/5/6s. Cooldown: 45s.

beginner.whatItIs: The Huntress's killer perk that watches the basement. Whenever a survivor enters that area while the killer is some distance away, the killer briefly sees that survivor's aura.
beginner.whyItMatters: The basement is a choke point survivors use to loop and escape, and a killer who cannot see into it is blind to what is happening inside. It turns that blind spot into a short window of visibility the moment a survivor commits to the basement, rewarding killers who position nearby and punishing survivors who rely on basement loops.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if playing The Huntress and wanting to control basement entrances without spending power, since it triggers automatically when a survivor commits to that area. It fits a tracking playstyle where the killer wants early warning before a chase starts rather than reactive tools during one.

Thanatophobia.name: Thanatophobia
Thanatophobia.description:
For each injured, downed, or hooked Survivor, all Survivors:
  • Cleanse totems 1/1.5/2% slower.
  • Repair 1/1.5/2% slower.
  • Sabotage Hooks 1/1.5/2% slower.


While 4 Survivors are either injured, downed or hooked, all above actions are additionally 12% slower.

beginner.whatItIs: Nurse's killer perk that scales with how many survivors are injured, downed, or hooked. The more survivors in bad shape, the slower every survivor's cleansing, repairing, and hook-sabotage becomes.
beginner.whyItMatters: It punishes teams that fall behind, because every action a survivor takes to recover or progress gets slower as the team's overall state worsens. It creates a feedback loop where a struggling team struggles more, which suits a killer who wants to snowball momentum after an early hook or injure.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Nurse and wanting a perk that grows stronger as the match progresses and more survivors get hurt. It suits a killer who hooks early and often, since the stacking slowdown makes every subsequent repair and cleanse feel heavier for the team.

TheMettleOfMan.name: Mettle of Man
TheMettleOfMan.description:
After taking 3 protection hits, while injured and until you go down, the next time you would be downed by the Killer, take no damage instead.

When you become healthy, while you are at least 12/14/16m from the Killer, they see your Aura.

When the trial starts, you are more likely to be the Obsession.

beginner.whatItIs: Ashley J. Williams's survivor perk that builds through protection hits: after taking enough of them, while injured, the next hit that would down the survivor is negated instead. Once healthy again, the killer can see the survivor's aura whenever they are far apart, and the survivor becomes more likely to be the Obsession at the start of the trial.
beginner.whyItMatters: The downed-state negation can save a chase that would otherwise end, giving a survivor one extra chance to reach a locker, hook, or window. The trade-off is visibility when healthy and Obsession pressure, which rewards players who can manage positioning carefully rather than hiding in the open.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Ash and wanting a once-per-trial safety net against a down state, especially in matches where the killer has a strong hook or chase setup. It asks the survivor to accept higher visibility when healthy in exchange for a guaranteed save when it counts most.

This_Is_Not_Happening.name: This Is Not Happening

beginner.whatItIs: A general survivor perk available to any character. While injured, the good zone on basic skill checks becomes noticeably larger, making it easier to land a clean press.
beginner.whyItMatters: Basic skill checks are the bread and butter of generator repair and pallet drops, and a larger good zone means fewer missed presses and less time standing still under pressure. It matters most mid-chase when a survivor is injured and trying to drop a pallet without getting hit.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor wants a consistent quality-of-life boost on skill checks during chases, especially when playing injured or when the killer has a strong skill-check punish setup. It is a set-and-forget perk that requires no activation, so it can go in any build that needs reliable repair or pallet drops.

ThrillingTremors.name: Thrilling Tremors
ThrillingTremors.description: Whenever you pick-up a Survivor, all Generators not being repaired are blocked for 16s. Cooldown: 40/35/30s.

beginner.whyItMatters: Picking up a survivor already pulls them out of the fight, and blocking every idle generator on top of that stalls the rest of the team for a meaningful window. It punishes teams that try to race generators while a teammate is being carried, since progress halts the moment a pickup happens.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it on The Ghost Face when every pickup should carry a second effect beyond removing a survivor from play. Generator repair stalls across the whole map, so teams feel the hit even where the killer is not standing, and it pays off most when a pickup happens while multiple repairs are still underway.

beginner.whyItMatters: Undetectability during a generator's progress window lets the killer move unseen while survivors are focused on repairing, creating openings for a hook or scare that would normally be seen coming. It rewards a killer who can read the map and position during those specific moments rather than relying on raw speed.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if playing HillBilly and wanting a stealth tool that activates automatically as generators progress, with no input required from the killer. It fits a patient playstyle where the killer camps near generators and strikes during the undetectable window rather than chasing survivors in the open.

beginner.whyItMatters: The undetectability window lets the killer move freely while survivors are forced to watch the damaged generator, splitting the team's attention. Survivors who see the generator's aura can rush to repair it, which pulls them away from other objectives and creates openings for the killer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when the killer wants a tool that creates a choose-your-own-adventure moment for the team: repair the damaged generator or keep working elsewhere. It suits a killer who wants to force survivors into predictable positions rather than relying on chase speed.

Unnerving_Presence.name: Unnerving Presence

Survivors within your Terror Radius get 10% more basic Skill Checks.

beginner.whatItIs: The Trapper's killer perk that increases how many basic Skill Checks survivors get while inside the terror radius and shrinks the good zone on those checks. The two effects compound, making every Skill Check harder to land cleanly.
beginner.whyItMatters: Skill checks are the main way survivors drop pallets and complete generator presses, and making them harder during a chase directly reduces the survivor's ability to escape. It punishes teams that rely on pallet loops, since every drop attempt in the terror radius becomes riskier.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing The Trapper and wanting to make chases harder for survivors without needing to land every hit. It suits a killer who wants to control the pace of a chase through difficulty rather than raw speed, especially against teams that loop pallets heavily.

beginner.whatItIs: A general killer perk available to any character. Whenever a basic attack is missed, the cooldown before the next swing comes back faster.
beginner.whyItMatters: Missing a swing normally gives a survivor a free window to break the killer's combo or vault away, and it shrinks that window by making the next attack ready sooner. It rewards aggressive killers who swing often, since even a flurry of misses keeps the pressure high.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the killer wants to minimize the penalty for whiffing, especially against survivors who bait misses with pallet drops or window vaults. It fits a relentless chase style where the killer swings as often as possible rather than waiting for a perfect angle.

Up_The_Ante.name: Up the Ante
Up_The_Ante.description:

beginner.whatItIs: Ace Visconti's survivor perk that gives every survivor a small luck bonus that grows with how many other survivors are still alive. It also lets every survivor attempt to free themselves from a hook without help, though that ability itself does not scale with team size.
beginner.whyItMatters: The self-unhook changes the hook dynamic entirely, because a hooked survivor is no longer fully helpless and can potentially save themselves if left alone long enough. The luck bonus is a small but steady boost to skill check outcomes, which adds up over a full match of repairs and pallet drops.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Ace or when a team wants a support perk that helps every survivor rather than just one. It suits a team playstyle where hooks are expected and the team wants at least a chance to self-rescue rather than relying entirely on a teammate to show up.

beginner.whatItIs: Nea's survivor perk that grants a significant speed boost while crouched. The effect is only active in the crouch stance, so it does not affect normal running.
beginner.whyItMatters: Crawling is normally a slow, vulnerable movement that survivors use to stay quiet, and it makes that stance much faster without giving up the stealth benefit. It matters most when a survivor needs to stay low and quiet but also cover ground quickly, such as slipping past the killer's line of sight or reaching a safe corner.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if playing Nea and wanting a faster alternative to normal crouch movement, especially in maps with tight corridors or loops where staying low matters. It fits a stealth playstyle where the survivor prefers to stay quiet and unseen rather than outrunning the killer at full sprint.

beginner.whyItMatters: Negative status effects stack and punish survivors who are injured or mid-chase, and it speeds up the removal of most of them for everyone nearby. It matters most in team play where a survivor is healing others or standing near a generator, since the aura cleanup makes the whole team more resilient.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Quentin in a team composition where other survivors need constant aura cleanup, especially against killers who apply status effects heavily. It suits a support role where the survivor stays near the team and acts as a mobile cleanup zone rather than a solo objective player.

beginner.whatItIs: Felix Richter's survivor perk that reveals the auras of generators within a moderate radius. It has a short cooldown that begins whenever a generator is completed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Generator aura visibility removes the guesswork from repair planning, since a survivor can always see which generators are left and where they are. It matters most in the early and mid game when a team is splitting up and needs to coordinate which generators to target next.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it when tracking remaining generators matters and teammate calls are unreliable. It fits a support role where the survivor serves as the team's live map, pointing others toward whichever repair target is still open.

beginner.whatItIs: Quentin's survivor perk that activates when all generators are completed, revealing the auras of exit gate switches. While opening a gate, the survivor's own aura is visible to teammates, and gate speed increases with the number of survivors still alive.
beginner.whyItMatters: The endgame gate-opening phase is where teams lose the most time, because survivors often waste time hunting for the gate switches in the dark. It removes that search and speeds up the actual gate opening, which can be the difference between a clean escape and a last-second hook.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Quentin and wanting a clean endgame tool that removes the guesswork from finding gates. It suits a team where Quentin is the designated gate opener, since the aura visibility and speed bonus both reward a survivor who commits to the gates early.

WellMakeIt.name: We'll make it
WellMakeIt.description: Whenever you unhook a Survivor, for 30/60/90s, you heal other Survivors 100% faster.

beginner.whatItIs: Any character can unlock We'll make it. Once the holder unhooks a teammate, healing speed for other survivors spikes sharply for a sustained window, turning a single rescue into a rapid follow-up heal.
beginner.whyItMatters: Unhooking is one of the highest-risk actions in the game because the unhooker is exposed and vulnerable immediately after, and it turns that vulnerable moment into a healing power spike. It rewards teams that unhook and then heal immediately, since the bonus healing rate makes the whole sequence faster and safer.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if a survivor is in a team where unhooking is expected and the team wants the unhooker to also be a healer. It suits a support playstyle where the survivor unhooks, heals, and moves on quickly rather than standing still to finish a full heal.

beginner.whatItIs: David King's survivor perk that makes healing a downed survivor much faster. Once that heal finishes, the healed survivor gains a short window of Endurance, with a cooldown before the bonus can trigger again.
beginner.whyItMatters: Downed healing is normally slow and leaves the healer exposed for a long time, and it cuts that exposure window in half. The Endurance bonus gives the healed survivor a brief buffer against the next hit, which can be the difference between surviving a second chase and going down again.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing David King or when a team wants a dedicated downed healer who can finish heals quickly and get out of danger. It suits a team where one survivor is the primary healer and the others focus on repairs, since the fast heal and Endurance bonus make that role more effective.

beginner.whatItIs: Any killer can unlock Whispers, a tracking perk that produces random whisper sounds while a survivor is within close range. The cues arrive intermittently, giving the killer sporadic audio confirmation of a survivor's presence in the area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Whispers give the killer a subtle directional cue when a survivor is hiding or moving quietly, which fills the gap between full aura visibility and total silence. It matters most in the early game or after a hook when the killer needs to find a surviving group without a direct visual.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it if the killer wants a passive tracking tool that requires no input and works across any map. It suits a killer who plays patiently and wants to close the distance on a hiding team without burning power or using a character-specific ability.

beginner.whatItIs: Kate's survivor perk that reveals the auras of pallets, breakable walls, and windows within a moderate radius. The effect is always active and does not require any activation.
beginner.whyItMatters: Knowing where pallets, windows, and breakables are before a chase starts removes a major planning step from every loop. It matters most in maps with dense geometry where a survivor who knows the layout can set up a cleaner loop than one who is still searching for the right tiles.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Kate or when a survivor wants to reduce the planning overhead of every chase. It suits a survivor who loops heavily and wants to walk into a chase already knowing where every escape option is, rather than figuring it out mid-chase.

beginner.whatItIs: Oni's killer perk that reveals the auras of pallets and windows within a moderate radius, and briefly shows a survivor's aura whenever they drop a pallet. Both effects are always active and require no input.
beginner.whyItMatters: Pallet drops are the single most common escape tool in a chase, and seeing the moment a pallet falls gives the killer a brief window to adjust their path. The constant awareness of pallet and window positions also lets the killer pre-plan which loops to block, making chases feel more controlled.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Equip it when playing Oni and wanting a perk that makes every chase more information-rich without spending power. It suits a killer who reads survivor patterns and wants to react to pallet drops instantly rather than guessing where the next loop will go.
